March - 21, 2025
National Socialist Council of Nagaland - Isak-Muivah (NSCN-IM) ‘chairman’ Q Tuccu on March 21, stated that the NSCN is not responsible for the delay in the Naga political solution, asserting that the Government of India (GoI) is to blame, reports Northeast Now. He criticized Naga intellectuals and civil society leaders for aligning with factions backed by India, compromising their moral and ethical integrity.

Calling the Naga Republic Day a historic occasion, Tuccu reaffirmed the NSCN’s commitment to Naga sovereignty. He emphasized that the day marks the assertion of the Naga people's right to self-governance based on their sovereign status.

On March 21, the 4th India-European Union (EU) Maritime Security Dialogue was held in New Delhi, where the Indian delegation was led by Muanpuii Saiawi, Joint Secretary (Disarmament & International Security Affairs), Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), and the EU delegation by Maciej Stadejek, Director for Security and Defence Policy, European External Action Service, reports mea.gov.in. They reviewed ongoing cooperation initiatives in the maritime domain and avenues of reinforcing international and regional mechanisms for comprehensive maritime security. They agreed to strengthen their shared efforts in areas such as countering Illicit Maritime Activities (IMA), protection of critical maritime infrastructure, regional capability development and capacity-building activities.

March - 21, 2025
On March 21, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) charge sheeted two accused arrested for their alleged involvement in the purchase and supply of explosives by the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) in Chhattisgarh, reports latestly.com. NIA, in its charge sheet filed before the NIA Special Court, Jagdalpur, has named Mantosh Mandal and Sela Nagarjun alias S Nagarjun, both residents of Patnampara in the state's Sukma District. The two accused were identified as alleged supporters/overground workers (OGWs) of the CPI-Maoist and were found to have been actively involved in the online purchase of explosives and other necessary items for the proscribed outfit, the NIA said in a statement. They were found to be in unlawful possession of such material, meant for supply to CPI-Maoist members in the Jagargunda area of Sukma for preparation of Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs) to use against Security Forces (SFs). The State Police had originally registered the case following the arrest of Mantosh and Sela on September 25, last year. Based on their disclosures, explosive materials, including tiffin bombs, detonators, potassium nitrate, aluminium metal powder, etc., were recovered, along with other incriminating materials like packaging wrappers, Maoist literature and mobile phones containing incriminating content.

March - 21, 2025
On March 21, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) Court in Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) sentenced three accused, identified as Firoj Saikh, Tajamul Saikh and Enamul Haque, to seven years of rigorous imprisonment in Fake Indian Currency Notes (FICN) smuggling case, reports The Week. Firoz and Enamul were imposed a fine of INR 10,000 each and   Tajamul Saikh had been fined INR 5,000. The case is related to the 2018 case relating to the seizure of fake currency notes with a total face value of INR 10, 20,000. NIA said that the seizure was made from Mohammed Mahaboob Baig and Syed Imran who were travelling on the Howrah-Hyderabad East Coast Express. Their interrogation revealed the involvement of the three accused in the FICN smuggling.

March - 21, 2025
On March 21, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) special court in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, sentenced three accused, Firoj Saikh, Tajamul Saikh, and Enamul Haque, to seven years of rigorous imprisonment (RI) and a fine of INR 10,000 in a fake currency case, and in case of default in fine payment, they will serve an additional 2.5 years in jail, NIA reports. The case pertains to the 2018 seizure of Fake Indian Currency Notes (FICN) with a face value of INR 1.02 million. The counterfeit notes were recovered from two accused, Mahaboob Baig alias Azhar Baig and Syed Imran, who were travelling on the Howrah-Hyderabad East Coast Express. Their interrogation led to the identification of Firoj Saikh, Tajamul Saikh, and Enamul Haque. NIA investigations revealed that all five accused were part of a large-scale counterfeit currency smuggling racket. Mahaboob Baig and Syed Imran were convicted earlier on June 26, 2019, and sentenced to 10 years of RI for their role in the conspiracy. Additionally, Tajamul Saikh received a seven-year RI sentence with a fine of INR 5,000, along with an extra two-year prison term for default in fine payment. He was also sentenced to two years of RI with fines of INR 3,000 and INR 2,000, respectively.

March - 21, 2025
On March 21, Union Home Minister (UHM) Amit Shah informed Rajya Sabha (Upper House of Indian Parliament) that the conviction rate achieved by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) was the highest among all investigative agencies probing cases of terrorism across the world, reports The Print. “There were 652 cases where UAPA [Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act] was imposed and the cases went to the Supreme Court level and it has not declared applying UAPA inappropriate in any of the 652 cases,” he added. He further said, “Chargesheets have been filed in 512 out of 652 cases and 157 have been decided by courts and conviction has taken place in 150 out of them, marking a 95 per cent rate of convictions”. The report added that NIA arrested 11 terror operatives associated with the Islamic State (IS), five terror suspects from Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), and 24 other suspected terrorists.

March - 23, 2025
“Holistic” care for surrendered Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) cadres, a bounty for even Maoist “foot soldiers”, and a cash reward of INR 50,000 for anyone who can persuade their Maoist relatives to surrender – these are some of the major highlights of the Chhattisgarh Government’s ‘Naxal Surrender and Victim Rehabilitation Policy-2025’, reports The Indian Express on March 23. Announced by Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai’s Government, the policy, which is expected to be notified soon, is aimed at not only offering a range of incentives for surrendering Maoists – from promising them jobs to providing financial aid and legal protection – but also offering rewards to security personnel facilitating this. Some of the significant takeaways on the policy are: a) The policy promises to provide rehabilitation to surrendered Maoists in the form of assistance with children’s education and jobs. It also envisions financial assistance of INR 1 million for civilians murdered by Maoists for “assisting the police” and between INR 1.5 and 2.5 million for anyone killed in a Maoist attack. Besides, their families will also be provided financial assistance to build a home. b) The policy encourages the red rebels to surrender with weapons: those surrendering with a light machine gun (LMG), for instance, are entitled to a cash reward of INR 500,000, the highest for such cases.  In cases where 80 percent of the Maoist units surrender together, the reward will be doubled. c) Surrendered Maoists are entitled to financial assistance of INR 5 million. Months after the state government unveiled a new industrial policy encouraging private companies to hire surrendered insurgents, the new rehabilitation policy too promises 40 percent salary reimbursement in such cases, with a limit of up to INR 500,000. d) The policy puts a bounty of INR 100,000 even for foot soldiers. Meanwhile, security personnel who help in the capture or surrender of a Maoist will get an award of INR 500,000, or 10 percent of the bounty. e) The policy also envisions a committee to consider dropping all charges against the surrendered person subject to good behaviour for six months. f) Surrendered red rebels with a bounty of over INR 500,000 will receive 1,742 sq. ft of land to make a home or 1-hectare agricultural land. Instead of land, they can also be given INR 200,000. g) Women are to be provided monetary aid and given loans to start a business.

March - 25, 2025
Intelligence agencies increased surveillance and put on alert in Murshidabad District in West Bengal in the villages close to the international border with Bangladesh, following an input on attempts of infiltration by Jamaat-ul-Mujahideen Bangladesh (JMB) and Hizb-ut-Tahrir (HuT), reports The Statesman on March 25. The agencies had also put an alert on the bordering villages of Malda District. According to the inputs, JMB and HuT cadres, currently operating out of the Rajsahi and Chapai-Nawabganj Districts in Bangladesh, are making attempts in small groups to illegally cross into the Indian territory in the Murshidabad District to reactivate the sleeper cells. Central Intelligence Official received the input through communications made by JMB and HuT cadres with their local moles in Murshidabad through various Internet-based communication channels. Among those local contacts who the JMB and HuT cadres contacted, a couple of them are attached to some ‘khariji (unregistered)’ madrasas (Islamic Seminary) operating out of some India-Bangladesh bordering villages in Murshidabad District. March - 28, 2025
A handwritten Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) letter in Telugu, found in a recent encounter site in a forest in Abujhmarh in Bijapur, claims that the banned outfit has recruited 130 cadres from the Maad region, 80 of them minors, including children aged nine, reports The Times of India on March 28. It says these raw recruits are undergoing training in “guerrilla warfare, weapon handling and IED-making”. It’s believed to be a “review report” of CPI-Maoist from an internal meeting and was found after the encounter in which Maoist ‘commander’ Sudheer alias Sudhakar was shot dead on March 25, the Police said. Sudheer carried a bounty of INR 2.5 million and was responsible for training new recruits in weapons and guerrilla tactics. “Earlier, teenagers were recruited into the Maoist cultural wing, called Chetna Natya Manch (CNM), and later given combat training. If the review report is to be believed, then it indicates a dangerous trend of Maoists recruiting children as ‘child soldiers’ for the battlefield at a tender age. It would be soldiers’ vs children. But we will run campaigns to stop this recruitment,” an unnamed senior officer of Bastar Range said. The Maoist ‘review’ says it’s a ‘report on the experiences of newly recruited comrades’ and has been compiled from ‘North Bureau directives and ground-level accounts’ since Jan 2023. According to the letter, Maoist leaders conducted a gram sabha in the Maad region and recruited 130 cadres — 50 aged 18-22, 40 aged 14-17 and, alarmingly, 40 aged between nine and 11 years. Senior Maoists admit in the letter that the younger recruits are not yet ready for combat and are in need of “more education and preparation”. The letter includes a detailed account of the ongoing challenges faced by the Maoist leadership, particularly the difficulty in recruiting new members. Maoist ‘commanders’ expressed concern about the “growing reluctance” among young people to join their cause and realised that future recruitment efforts might be even more challenging.

Although the police are yet to ascertain the motive behind the murder, it is perceived as a result of the Maoists' frustration with the three new Police posts established in the region within less than six months. Sources said that Pugati's son teaches at a college at Etapalli, while his daughter-in-law is a Police constable. Superintendent of Police (SP) Neelotpal said Maoists are likely venting their frustration due to their depleting strength, diminishing influence, and reducing mass base. "We have opened three police stations in the same sector, with the latest one at Kawande, around 20km away. The post at Pengunda is barely 6km from Juvvi, and the one at Nelgunda is around 12km away. These posts have forced the Maoists to shift their bases from these regions and stop using these crossing points to move to and from Chhattisgarh," said the SP. He added that the Bhamragarh Local Organisational Squad (LOS) is likely behind the murder.

March - 31, 2025
India’s Intelligence agencies are wary of the demographic shift in Nepal, where the Muslim population has significantly increased from 4.2 per cent in 2001 to 5.09 per cent in 2021, reports News 18 on March 31. The report highlighted that the demographic shift expanded terror routes into India. The Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) utilised Nepal to fund terrorism in India, particularly in Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), with cash transfers occurring via local youth in 2021. Nepalese businessmen facilitated cash handovers to conduits in India. it further highlighted that terror groups like the Indian Mujahideen (IM), Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT), and Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM) used Nepal as a hub, as noted in a 2019 United States (US) State Department report. The report further highlighted that the Communist Party of Nepal-Maoist (CPN-Maoist) played a crucial role in creating favourable conditions for Muslim settlement, establishing legal environments with job quotas and funding for madrasas (Islamic Seminary) in 2015. Muslim migrants, including Rohingyas from Myanmar, have settled in Nepal as part of a larger strategy. Post-monarchy, Muslim communities organised initiatives like community radio stations, schools, and charities in cities such as Nepalgunj. In Kapilvastu District, Muslims constitute 18 per cent of the population, and Islamic influence is prominent. Over the past decade, more than 400 mosques and madrasas have been constructed near the Nepal-India border in areas like Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh in India. And more particularly, 4,000 madrasas near the Indo-Nepal border are under scrutiny for foreign funding, mainly from Pakistan and Gulf countries.

March - 31, 2025
India’s intelligence and security agencies are alarmed over two escalating threats emerging from Bangladesh — the resurgence of terror groups like Jamaat-ul-Mujahideen Bangladesh (JMB), Al-Qaeda in Indian Sub-continent (AQIS), and Islamic State (IS) and the deteriorating situation in Rohingya refugee camps, reports New 18 on March 31.  It was revealed that after the release of top terror operatives in Bangladesh, splinter factions of JMB have regrouped and aligned themselves with AQIS, IS, and Ansarullah Bangla Team (ABT). These cadres shifted base to South India, Assam, and West Bengal, reactivating old sleeper cells. Intelligence inputs suggest that JMB, ABT, and IS are now operating under shared command structures, with a common target: Indian interests, as well as Western allies such as the United States (US) and Israel. These operatives blend into densely populated Bengali-dominated areas, and work in slaughterhouses, cotton textile hubs, and other inconspicuous sectors. They travel frequently to activate local cells and remain largely self-funded through small madrassas (Islamic Seminary). While no major funding links with AQIS core in Syria or Afghanistan have been found, online allegiance rituals and cyber activity have kept them connected to global jihadist movements. On the other side, India’s porous border with Bangladesh—especially in West Bengal and Assam—leaves it vulnerable to large-scale infiltration, both by Rohingya refugees and potential militants. This may trigger internal security challenges in sensitive regions like Jammu & Kashmir (J&K) and Manipur.

April - 1, 2025
On April 1, one Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM) militant was killed and another was injured in a clash between Security Forces (SF) and militants in the Panjtirthi area of Juthana village in the Ramkot tehsil (revenue unit) of Billawar (town) in the Kathua District of Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), reports The Week. This was the third encounter in the district since March 23. As reported earlier by the SATP, the first incident occurred on March 23 in Sanyal village in Hiranagar Tehsil (revenue unit) of Kathua, where all terrorists evaded capture, while one civilian was injured. Subsequently, a second encounter unfolded in the Safiyan forest area in Hiranagar Tehsil under the Rajbagh Police Station’s jurisdiction in Kathua District, where two militants were neutralized. Four policemen — identified as Tariq Ahmad, Jaswant Singh, Balwinder Singh, and Jagbir Singh — lost their lives, with three bodies recovered on March 27 and the fourth on March 28, as reported by The Hindu. SATP had earlier reported that three militants and three SF personnel were killed in the encounter in Hiranagar.  A multi-tier operation in the dense forested regions of the Kathua District which was launched on March 23, entered its 12th day on April 3, reports Daily Excelsior.

April - 1, 2025
On April 1, Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi met with Gabriel Boric Font, the President of the Republic of Chile, at Hyderabad House in New Delhi and both leaders reaffirmed their unequivocal condemnation of terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including cross border terrorism, reports pib.gov.in. The two leaders called upon all United Nations (UN) member countries to implement the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) Resolution 1267 and work towards eliminating terrorist safe havens and infrastructure and disrupting terrorist networks and all terror financing channels. Both reiterated their commitment to work together in the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), No Money For Terror (NMFT) and other multilateral platforms to combat terrorism. The two leaders also reiterated the importance of the early finalisation of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism. They also reviewed the bilateral relations spanning a wide range of sectors, including trade and investment, health and pharmaceuticals, defence and security, infrastructure, mining and mineral resources, agriculture and food security, green energy, ICT, digitization, innovation, disaster management, cooperation in science and technology, education and people-to-people linkages.

April - 1, 2025
On April 1, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (UMHA) claimed that the number of most Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist)-affected districts has reduced to six from 12, reports etvbharat.com. "The number of districts of concern has also come down to 6 from 9, and the number of other LWE-affected districts has also been reduced from 17 to 6," the UMHA said. Out of total LWE-affected districts, the number of ‘most affected districts’ has been reduced from 12 to six, which include four districts from Chhattisgarh (Bijapur, Kanker, Narayanpur, and Sukma), one from Jharkhand (West Singhbhum), and one from Maharashtra (Gadchiroli). Similarly, out of the total 38 affected districts, the number of ‘districts of concern’, where additional resources need to be intensively provided beyond the severely affected districts, has reduced from nine to six. These six districts are Andhra Pradesh (Alluri Sitarama Raju), Madhya Pradesh (Balaghat), Odisha (Kalahandi, Kandhamal, and Malkangiri), and Telangana (Bhadradri-Kothagudem). Earlier, the total number of districts affected by Naxalism [Left Wing Extremism, LWE] in the country was 38. "Due to persistent action against Naxalism, the number of other LWE-affected districts has also decreased from 17 to 6. These include districts from Chhattisgarh (Dantewada, Gariabandh, and Mohla-Manpur-Ambagarh Chowki), Jharkhand (Latehar), Odisha (Nuapada), and Telangana (Mulugu)," the UMHA said. Union Home Minister (UHM) Amit Shah said, "The Modi government is building a Sashakt, Surakshit and Samriddh Bharat with a ruthless approach to Naxalism and relentless efforts for all-pervasive development. Bharat is determined to uproot Naxalism for good by 31st March 2026."

April - 2, 2025
Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) Party ‘Central Committee (CC)’ ‘spokesperson’ Abhay stated that Maoists were ready for peace talks with the State and Central governments, provided the governments should create an amicable situation for the purpose, reports Telangana Today on April 2. In a statement released to the media, he said the Maoists welcomed a round table meeting held in Hyderabad on March 24 on the topic of ‘Stopping of war in central India-announcement of ceasefire by the Indian government-CPI-Maoist Party’ by a Peace Talks Committee. Abhay said the party Dandakaranya Special Zonal Committee (DKSZC) ‘spokesperson’ Vikalp twice expressed the party’s readiness for peace talks in response to a call given by Chhattisgarh Home Minister Vijay Sharma to Maoists to come for peace talks and the government is ready to discuss the issue. Vikalp appealed to the government to create an atmosphere conducive for peace talks by stopping the ‘Operation Kagar’ launched in January 2024, by confining the security forces to their barracks and by stopping setting up of new police camps. But the government has not responded to the appeal and continued the ‘Operation Kagar’ for the last 15 months killing over 400 Maoist cadres so far, besides arresting thousands of people, Abhay said. If the governments in Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Telangana stop the ‘genocide’ they are carrying out; stops setting up new police camps, the Maoist party would announce a ceasefire, he noted.

April - 2, 2025
On April 2, Police arrested a terror suspect, identified as Feroz Khan, from Ratlam District of Madhya Pradesh, who was wanted in connection with a 2022 explosives conspiracy case that was initially uncovered by the Rajasthan Police in Chittorgarh, reports The Times of India. The suspect carried INR 5,00,000 reward announced by National Investigation Agency (NIA). The case came to light in March 2022 when Police seized 12 kilograms of explosives, along with battery clocks and bomb-making materials, during a vehicle inspection in Nimbahera town in Chittorgarh District of Rajasthan. He is the founding member and treasurer of the terror outfit Al-Sufa which was established around 2012-13 and had planned to orchestrate attacks using the seized explosives. Earlier, three suspects, identified as Zubair Khan, Sarfuddin alias Saifulla and Altamas Khan were arrested in the case. The case was subsequently transferred to the NIA, which filed a chargesheet against 11 accused, including Feroz Khan, in September 2022.

April - 3, 2025
As the government intensifies operations in Chhattisgarh’s Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) strongholds, the Maoists have reportedly offered conditional peace talks, reports The Hindu on April 3. The State government said that any talks must be unconditional. In a press release attributed to the CPI-Maoist and released on March 28 in Telangana, its ‘central committee (CC)’ stated that it was ready for peace talks on the condition that the government halts its anti-Maoist operations in the region and stops the establishment of new camps of armed forces in various States, including in Chhattisgarh. “We are always ready for peace talks in the interest of the public. Therefore, on this occasion, we are proposing to create a positive atmosphere for peace talks in front of the Central and State governments,” said the purported Maoist statement. Explaining its new stance, it said that its Peace Talks Committee had held a round table meeting in Hyderabad on March 24 on the theme: ‘The ongoing war in Central India must be stopped immediately, Government of India – CPI-Maoist must declare unconditional ceasefire and hold peace talks’. State Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Sharma said that the government was ready for talks and for the Maoists to return to the mainstream, but it could not be subject to conditions laid down by the Maoists. He added that the government was not going to form any committees for peace talks and reiterated the Maoists could initiate it through any channel of their choice. “They have written themselves that the last time they had said that they would discuss if [security forces] should not leave their camps for six months, there should be a reduction in the number of troops, the weapons should remain unused or be deposited. Back then, we had made it clear that with these conditions, there will be no talks,” he said. “Talks will be without any conditions and we are still ready for that, our Central leadership is ready, Hon. [Chief Minister] Vishnu Deo Sai ji is ready, there is no problem with talks. But the government will not form any committee. They should make one if they want or use the channel they like, we are ready,” he added.

April - 4, 2025
On April 4, a special trial court in Jaipur District in Rajasthan, convicted four accused, identified as Saif-Ur-Rehman, Mohammed Saif, Sarwar Azami and Shahbaz Ahmed, for their involvement in the live bomb detection case linked to the serial bomb blasts in Jaipur on May 13, 2008, reports The Times of India. The bomb blasts resulted in 71 fatalities across a series of eight explosions in Jaipur. A 9th bomb, discovered near the Ramchandraji temple in Chandpole, Jaipur, was found to be live but successfully diffused by Security Forces (SFs). Saif-Ur-Rehman, Mohammed Saif, Mohammed Salman (another accused) and Sarwar Azmi had earlier been convicted in December 2019 for the eight serial blasts and sentenced to death, a verdict that the Rajasthan High Court overturned in March 2023. Accordingly, Saif-Ur-Rehman and Mohammed Saif were lodged at Jaipur Central Jail in the live bomb detection case. However, Sarwar Azmi was out on bail. Shahbaz Ahmed, who was convicted in the live bomb case, was acquitted by the trial court in the eight serial blasts case. In this case of a live bomb, Mohammed Salman’s trial is underway at the juvenile justice board in Jaipur.

April - 4, 2025
On April 4, Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with Muhammad Yunus, Chief Advisor of the Interim Government of Bangladesh on the sidelines of the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) in Bangkok, Thailand, reports mea.gov.in. Prime Minister Modi Minister reiterated India’s support for a democratic, stable, peaceful, progressive and inclusive Bangladesh. He also said that strict enforcement of the law and prevention of illegal border crossings, especially at night, are necessary for maintaining border security and stability. He further underlined India’s concerns related to the safety and security of minorities in Bangladesh, including Hindus and expressed his expectation that the Government of Bangladesh would ensure their security, including by thoroughly investigating the cases of atrocities committed against them.

April - 4, 2025
On April 4, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) arrested Shamnad E.K., alias Shamnad Illikkal, from the Ernakulum District of Kerala, the main accused in the 2022 Popular Front of India (PFI)-orchestrated murder of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) leader Palakkad Sreenivasan, reports NIA. The accused had been on the run for the past three years and was carrying a reward of INR 7,00,000 for his arrest. He had been under the protection of PFI and was living under a concealed identity since the gruesome killing of the RSS leader. The NIA, which registered the case in September 2022, revealed that PFI leaders and cadres hatched the murder conspiracy to create a communal divide. The outfit was engaged in radicalizing vulnerable Muslim youth to promote its violent agenda of establishing Islamic rule in India by 2047. Recruits were trained in the handling of weapons by PFI, which was also actively raising funds to carry out acts of terror and violence in the country. The NIA has so far charge sheeted 63 accused as part of its ongoing investigations in the case (RC-02/2022/NIA.KOC).

April - 4, 2025
On April 4, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) filed a charge sheet against Faizul Hussain, a top Hizb-ut-Tahrir (HuT) leader, before the NIA Special Court in Poonamallee, Chennai (Tamil Nadu), for promoting the proscribed terrorist group’s violent ideology and inciting youth to carry out its vicious anti-India agenda, reports NIA. He is the 7th accused to be charged in the case RC-02/2024/NIA/CHE (Hameed Hussain HuT case). Faizul Hussain was arrested on October 8, 2024, for radicalizing Muslim youth and propagating HuT’s violent agenda to establish an Islamic Caliphate in India. According to NIA investigations, he and his associates used to conduct covert HuT meetings under the guise of the Modern Essential Education Trust (MEET) at a rented accommodation on Jani Jhan Khan Road, Royapettah, Chennai. The accused was using the premises to propagate HuT’s extremist beliefs through social media handles. He was disseminating anti-national content to spread disaffection and incite communal discord by promoting a secessionist ideology. The case was taken over from the state police in July 2024.

April - 5, 2025
As many as 86 members of the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist), which operates out of Sukma and Bijapur Districts in Chhattisgarh, surrendered before the Telangana Police in Bhadradri Kothagudem District on April 5, reports The Indian Express. The surrendered Maoists, including 20 women cadre, were provided with immediate cash assistance of INR 25,000. The 86 who surrendered include Maoist cadres of various formations, including four ‘area committee members (ACM)’, five party members, eight from the Revolutionary People’s Committee (RPC), 27 RPC ‘militia’ (people’s army of Maoists), 20 of the RPC Dandakaranya Adivasi Kisan Mazdoor Sangh (DAKMS/KMS), 13 RPC Chaitanya Natya Mandali (CNM) members and nine RPC Gram Raksha Dal (GRD) members. “They decided to leave the violent path of Naxalism [Left Wing extremism, LWE] and lead a peaceful life with their family members and surrendered before the Inspector General of Police (IGP) Multi Zone-I in Bhadradri Kothagudem District today, after knowing about the welfare measures being taken up for the surrendered Maoists and also the development of welfare schemes for tribal (Adivasi) people, provided under the ‘Operation Cheyutha’ programme by the Telangana Police Department,” a statement from the Police said. With this, the total number of Maoists who have surrendered before the Police in Bhadradri Kothagudem and Mulugu this year adds up to 224.

April - 5, 2025
Union Home Minister (UHM) Amit Shah, on April 5, said Naxals [Left Wing Extremists, LWEs] would not be able to stop the development of tribals in Chhattisgarh’s Bastar region and urged them to lay down arms while asserting that nobody is happy when they are killed, reports Telangana Today. Addressing the closing ceremony of the state government’s ‘Bastar Pandum’ festival, Shah reiterated that the government is committed to eliminating the Naxal menace by March 2026, adding that those who surrender will become part of the mainstream, while the rest will be taken on by Security Forces (SFs). “The days when bullets were fired and bombs exploded in Bastar are over. I urge Naxalite brothers to lay down arms and join the mainstream. You are our own. No one feels happy when any Naxalite is killed. Just surrender your weapons and join the mainstream. You cannot stop the development of your tribal brothers and sisters by taking up arms,” he said, offering an olive branch to the outlawed movement.

April - 7, 2025
A special court of the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in Mumbai (Maharashtra) sentenced four accused, identified as Samir Mandal and Mohammad Shadab Khan (on April 7) to seven years and five years of rigorous imprisonment respectively and Anees Iklakh Shaikh and Kishor Namdeo Fular (on April 8) to five years and nine months of rigorous imprisonment, along with a fine of INR 10,000 each, in 2018 Fake Indian Currency Notes (FICN) seizure case, confirming cross-border links to a FICN racket operating from Bangladesh, reports The Free Press Journal. The case pertains to the seizure of 203 high-quality FICN with a face value of INR 4,78,000 from a shop near Sai Dhaba in Wadape, Bhiwandi in Thane District of Maharashtra in October 2018. The initial arrests were made in this case by the Police in October 2018, when five individuals Rehan Abbas Shaikh, Shafahad Mukhtar Ansari, Anees Iklak Shaikh, Kishor Namdeo Fular, and Rohit Nagendra Singh were taken into custody. The NIA took over the probe in December 2018 and subsequently arrested four more individuals: Samir Mandal, Sabir Ali, Abdul Kadir, and Mohammad Shadab Khan. The key accused in the case is Karim Shaikh, who is absconding and an investigation into the role in the FICN racket spread across Bangladesh, West Bengal, Maharashtra, and other parts of India is ongoing.

At least 26 cadres of the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist), including three carrying bounties, surrendered before Security Forces (SFs) in Dantewada District in the Bastar division of Chhattisgarh on April 7, reports etvbharat.com. April - 8, 2025
On April 8, the Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) said that it arrested seven individuals, identified as Shelabhai Boliya, Vishal Pandya, Arjun Algotar, Dhairya Jariwala, Sadam Hussain, Brijesh alias Bittu Mehta, and Mukesh Bamba, who were found carrying forged arms license and detected over 100 people who bought firearms with fake licenses from Manipur and Nagaland, reports Hindustan Times. During the operation, Gujarat ATS formed teams that were dispatched to Nagaland, Manipur, and Haryana. The teams recovered three twelve-bore guns with 70 rounds of ammunition, two pistols with 59 rounds of ammunition and one revolver with 6 rounds of ammunition, it added. In all, six firearms and 135 rounds of ammunition have been seized, and a case has been registered under the Arms Act. “Our investigation revealed that approximately 108 individuals from various districts of Gujarat had managed to acquire weapons through fraudulent means using fake arms licenses allegedly made in Nagaland and Manipur,” said a senior unnamed ATS official. The investigation revealed that arms dealers from Nuh, Haryana, including Saukat Ali Chhotukhaan, Faruk Ali Chhotekhaan, Asif, and their associates, had been creating fake arms licenses for Gujarat residents for the past six years. According to a statement issued by Gujarat ATS, these dealers sold revolvers, pistols, 12-bore guns, and ammunition to individuals possessing these fraudulent licenses.

April - 10, 2025
On April 10, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) secured the extradition of Tahawwur Hussain Rana, the key conspirator of 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, 2008 from the judicial custody in the United States (US) pursuant to proceedings initiated under the India-US Extradition Treaty for his extradition, reports NIA. After his arrival at the Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGIA), New Delhi, NIA formally arrested, Tahawwur Hussain Rana on the same day. Further, NIA took his custody in the evening of April 10, on the orders of the Special Court in New Delhi. NIA had produced Rana before NIA Special Court at Patiala House. He will remain in NIA custody for 18 days. Earlier, the District Court for the Central District of California, US, had ordered his extradition on May 16, 2023. Rana then filed multiple litigations in the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, all of which were rejected. He subsequently filed a petition for a writ of certiorari, two habeas petitions, and an emergency application before the US Supreme Court, which were also denied. Rana’s various litigations and appeals, including an emergency application before the US Supreme Court, were rejected with the assistance of US Department of Justice’s Office of International Affairs, US Attorney Office of the Central District of California, US Marshals Service, Federal Bureau of Investigation’s (FBI’s) Legal Attache Office in New Delhi and US Department of State’s Office of the Legal Adviser for Law Enforcement. With the active assistance of United States Department of Justice (USDoJ), the US Sky Marshal, NIA worked closely with other Indian intelligence agencies, National Security Guard (NSG) through the entire extradition process, which also saw India’s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and Union Ministry of Home Affairs (UMHA) coordinating with the other relevant authorities in the US to take the matter to its successful conclusion. Rana is accused of conspiring with David Coleman Headley alias Daood Gilani, and operatives of Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT) and Harkat-ul-Jihadi Islami (HUJI) along with other Pakistan-based coconspirators, to carry out the attacks in Mumbai in 2008. A total of 166 persons were killed and over 238 injured in the attacks.

The Security Forces (SFs) demolished as many as five underground Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) bunkers in the jungles of Kulpaburu under Jaraikela Police Station in Chaibasa, the district headquarters of West Singhbhum District in Jharkhand on April 10, reports The New Indian Express. It is believed that the CPI-Maoist rebels have been using those bunkers for hiding after executing subversive activities. The Police and paramilitary forces blew up the bunkers one after another after they had stumbled upon the existence of one of such bunkers at the Kulpaburu jungle. “We have recovered five bunkers, being used by the Maoists for hiding themselves during operations, till the security forces receded. These bunkers were large enough to accommodate several rebels at a time measuring nearly eight feet high and 15 feet long,” said Chaibasa Superintendent of Police (SP) Ashutosh Shekhar.

April - 11, 2025
Chhattisgarh government has formally implemented its ‘Naxalite Surrender, Victim Relief, and Rehabilitation Policy 2025’ offering Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) a chance to surrender and start anew, and guaranteeing timely rehabilitation, skill training, and a dignified life, reports The Times of India on April 11. Among the key features of the new policy include guaranteed rehabilitation within 120 days for surrendered cadres, monthly stipend of INR 10,000 for three years, provision of urban housing plots or agricultural land in rural areas. As per the govt’s notification district-level rehabilitation committees are being formed across the state. Each committee will be chaired by the District Collector, with the Superintendent of Police (SP) acting as the secretary. Other members would be divisional forest officer, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Zila Panchayat, two officers nominated by the collector, representatives from armed forces. Each district and sub-division will also appoint dedicated nodal officers, responsible for monitoring and coordinating all rehabilitation efforts. Their contact details will be submitted to the state government. To ensure transparency and accountability, a dedicated digital portal is under development. Each beneficiary—surrendered Naxalite or violence victim—will be assigned a unique ID. District officials will monitor this dashboard to track and expedite all rehabilitation activities. Under the new policy, the surrendered cadres will be given access to skill training and livelihood opportunities based on personal interest, safe transit camps or rehabilitation centers for initial settlement and training, comprehensive support for self-employment or business ventures.

April - 12, 2025
A special National Investigation Agency (NIA) court in Lucknow sentenced Rajendra Munda, an active cadre of the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist), to nine years imprisonment for conspiring against the nation and attempting to disrupt the country’s unity, integrity, and sovereignty, reports The Times of India on April 12. Special judge Hussain Ahmad Ansari also fined the convict INR 43,000. Munda was convicted under Indian Penal Code (IPC) Section 121A (conspiracy) and various sections of Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA), government counsel MK Singh said. He said the case dated back to 2010 when several members of the proscribed Maoist outfit and its frontal organisations were arrested in Gorakhpur, Kanpur, and Prayagraj. According to officials, Munda was attempting to meet his sister, Hiramani alias Asha, a fellow Maoist operative who was arrested and lodged in Gorakhpur jail. On receiving intelligence, Special Task Force (STF) arrested Munda near a temple on Station Road in Gorakhpur. Maoist literature and antinational propaganda material were recovered from him.

April - 13, 2025
On April 13, Indian Army Air Defence units brought down a Pakistan Army drone using the indigenously designed and developed ‘Integrated Drone Detection and Interdiction System’ while it was attempting surveillance along the Line of Control (LoC) in the Jammu region of Jammu and Kashmir, reports Daily Excelsior. According to defense sources, the drone — of Chinese origin — was brought down by Army Air Defence units deployed in the 16 Corps area, located south of the Pir Panjal ranges in the Jammu region. The incident occurred when the hostile drone was detected operating close to Indian territory along the LoC. The indigenously designed and developed ‘Integrated Drone Detection and Interdiction System’ is capable of jamming, spoofing, and bringing down enemy drones across a variety of ranges and scenarios. According to the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), the system has been deployed in significant numbers along India’s borders. It is also equipped with a 2-kilowatt laser beam that can strike down enemy drones from an effective range of 800 to 1,000 meters.

April - 13, 2025
On April 13, the Africa India Key Maritime Engagement (AIKEYME) 2025 was inaugurated in Dar-es-Salaam, Tanzania, marking a significant step in strengthening maritime cooperation between India and African nations, reports pib.gov.in. The ceremony was graced by the presence of Stergomena Lawrence Tax, Minister of Defence and National Service of Tanzania, Sanjay Seth, India's Raksha Rajya Mantri (RRM) and Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi. The event also saw the attendance of distinguished military leaders, including the Chief of Defence Force of the Tanzania Peoples' Defence Force (TPDF). Stergomena Lawrence Tax, whilst inaugurating the exercise, stressed the "significance of going along" to tackle maritime threats like piracy and trafficking. She called for "collaborative effort towards Maritime security by like-minded partners" and highlighted the aim of building an "enduring framework of maritime security, including innovation and information sharing." For AIKEYME, the Indian Navy is represented by Indian Navy Ship (INS) Chennai and INS Kesari. It will be conducted over six days with participation from Comoros, Djibouti, Kenya, Madagascar, Mauritius, Mozambique, Seychelles and South Africa, alongside India and Tanzania

April - 16, 2025
According to the National Investigation Agency (NIA), the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks conspirator Tahawwur Hussain Rana, along with his co-conspirators David Coleman Headley and Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT) operative Sajid Mir, operated under coded aliases while planning and coordinating terror activities in India, reports The Free Press Journal on April 16. Encrypted email communications showed that Rana was referred to as “Doctor,” Headley as “Dave,” and Sajid Mir as “Pir Sahab.” The term “business” was used as a covert code to refer to terrorist operations, reconnaissance missions, and target acquisition. Several email IDs were created to facilitate communication between Tahawwur Rana, David Coleman Headley, handlers of Ilyas Kashmiri, and top LeT operatives, A identified as Sajid Mir and B identified as Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) handler Major Iqbal. An email ID linked to “mov.monie@yahoo.com” was found to have been accessed from Rana’s Chicago-based immigration office, First World Immigration Services, later used by Headley while operating from the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Investigations revealed that, in addition to Rana's immigration consulting services through First World Immigration Services, which had offices in Chicago, Toronto, and New York, he was also running a halal meat supply business from his farm in Kinsman, Illinois, and owned a grocery store in Chicago. The NIA investigation revealed that Sajid Mir's operational base during the planning phase of the 26/11 attacks was located in the Razmak region of North Waziristan in Pakistan. Findings suggest that Headley is believed to have travelled to this facility multiple times to directly coordinate with Mir. After his time in India, Headley made regular trips to Pakistan, where he met with Major Iqbal, Sajid Mir, and several LeT ‘commanders’. During these visits, Headley provided video footage, pictures, and reconnaissance of several sensitive locations, which he meticulously gathered over all eight of his trips.

April - 16, 2025
On April 16, India and nine African countries began the sea phase of their maiden naval drills as part of a six-day multilateral exercise called Aikeyme (Africa India Key Maritime Engagement) in the western Indian Ocean region (IOR) to boost maritime security cooperation, reports Hindustan Times. The exercise is co-hosted by India and Tanzania and involves Comoros, Djibouti, Kenya, Madagascar, Mauritius, Mozambique, Seychelles and South Africa. The harbour phase ended at Dar es Salaam in Tanzania on April 15, paving the way for the sea phase, where the participating navies will conduct joint manoeuvres, anti-piracy drills, visit, board, search, and seizure (VBSS) exercises, and search-and-rescue operations. The exercise also aimed at addressing the shared challenges in a maritime expanse where China seeks to expand its presence. The exercise also aimed to enhance interoperability, refine joint operational strategies and address maritime challenges such as piracy, trafficking and illegal fishing.

On April 19, Delhi Police said that the Police's Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) dismantled a cross-border narco-terror syndicate operating between Afghanistan, Pakistan and India, and arrested 10 accused, including its kingpin, and seized heroin worth over INR 100 million in the international market, reports The Times of India and The Print. The accused Parminder Singh was arrested in Ludhiana in Punjab and disclosed a network smuggling drugs from Afghanistan to Pakistan, from there to Punjab and Jammu and Kashmir (J&K) and finally to Delhi. April - 20, 2025
On April 20, the Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) registered a First Information Report (FIR) and launched a probe into an inter-state module that was using encrypted messaging platforms to circulate anti-national content and radicalise youth to carry out fidayeen (suicide) attacks, reports The Times of India. The FIR lodged at ATS's Gomtinagar Police Station (PS) in Lucknow District under sections of the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA), the Foreigners Act, and the Explosives Act. According to ATS officials, a group was active on secure platforms such as Signal (under the name Al-Maut-ul-Hind), Instagram (Green Birds), Discord (Strangers), and WhatsApp, where they shared content promoting jihad, encouraged attacks on Indian security forces, and discussed targeting Hindu leaders and Israeli establishments in India. The FIR was filed on April 17 by ATS Sub-Inspector Rahul Satyal against three youths, two of whom belong to Sambhal and one from Patna. Their identities have not been revealed, and an interrogation with the ATS team is being conducted. “The suspects were reportedly engaged in testing explosives and practising with air and pellet guns. They also shared training videos and posts to recruit new members for “suicide missions,” the ATS stated in the FIR. “Initial inputs suggest that the accused were part of a larger network preparing for proxy warfare against the Indian govt. They aimed to foment communal tension and incite attacks on sensitive installations”, said an unnamed ATS official.

April - 21, 2025
At least eight Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) cadres, including senior ‘commander’ Prayag Manjhi alias Vivek Da alias Phuchna alias Nago Manjhi alias Karan Da, who carried a bounty of INR 10 million on his head, were killed in an ongoing encounter with Security Forces (SFs) in the Lugu Hill area under Lalpania Police Station limits in Bokaro District of Jharkhand on April 21 (today), reports ommcomnews.com. The gun battle began around 5.30 a.m. [IST] on April 21 and was still underway, with intermittent firing reported from both sides. Officials said the number of casualties could rise further. Prayag Manjhi is a ‘central committee (CC)’ member of the CPI-Maoist who was active in the Parasnath Hills and surrounding areas of Giridih over the past few months. Manjhi, originally a resident of Dalbudha in Tundi (Dhanbad District), was a key Maoist figure wanted in over 100 incidents across Jharkhand, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha. In Giridih District alone, he was wanted in more than 50 cases. Two sophisticated weapons, an INSAS (Indian Small Arms System) assault rifle and a Self-Loading Rifle (SLR), a few infantry arms, a pistol and eight country-made guns were recovered from the site. An official statement from the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) released on Monday (April 21) morning initially confirmed the killing of four Maoists. The number has since increased to eight. The identity of the remaining seven Maoists is yet to be ascertained.

However, Pakistan never took any action against the perpetrators”. Similarly, after the Pathankot terror attack in January 2016, in which several security personnel were killed, “first a letter rogatory (LR) from the NIA (National Investigation Agency) special court was handed over to Pakistan on March 2, 2016, through our high commission in Islamabad,” the officer added. “And then, a Pakistani Joint Investigation Team (JIT) was allowed to visit Pathankot and collect evidence from Indian investigators for five days in March 2016,” he said. Another unnamed officer detailed the information that was handed over to JIT.  He said, “The National Investigation Agency facilitated the Pakistani JIT’s conversation with 16 witnesses; and DNA samples of four fidayeen attackers --Nasir Hussain, Abu Bakar, Umar Farooq and Abdul Qayum (residents of Pakistan’s Punjab and Sindh) were also handed over to them”. He further added, “Besides, detailed individual dossiers, call detail records (CDRs), chats/messages of four terrorists with Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM) leaders and handlers, and financial details of Al-Rehmat Trust (financial arm of JeM) were also given to Pakistan”. Following the September 18, 2016, Uri camp attack --17 Indian army soldiers were killed by JeM -- and the November 29, 2016, attack on Nagrota camp --7 soldiers were killed – separate LRs were sent in 2017 to Pakistan with details of DNA samples, and information was sought on Abdul Rouf Asghar, JeM chief Masood Azhar’s brother and others. Similarly, after Pulwama 2019 attack, NIA sent a detailed LR seeking information on four Pakistan based perpetrators including Azhar, Asghar, another brother Ibrahim Athar, cousin Ammar Alvi, and three Pakistanis who came to India to execute the attack. The report further added, “Other than LeT, JeM and Hizb-ul Mujahideen, fringe elements of other outfits like Al Badr, Harkat-ul- Hehad-e-Islami also operate from Pakistan. The ISI runs a thriving OGW network in the Kashmir Valley to assist the terrorists in their activities”.

April - 27, 2025
The Financial Intelligence Unit of India (FIU-Ind) flagged suspicious crypto transactions for terror financing, fuelling secessionist activities, cybercrime, narcotics trafficking, apart from illegal betting and gambling, reports The Free Press Journal on April 27. The typologies report for the virtual digital assets (VDAs) and their service providers (crypto exchanges) was prepared by the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) after conducting “operational analysis” of suspicious transaction reports (STRs) having financial and national security implications. The report was shared with “credible" intelligence on the operations of cryptocurrency to the Enforcement Directorate (ED), Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Income-Tax Department for further enforcement action. The report on trends analysis found that VDAs and cryptocurrency were involved in Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM), terror financing, narcotics trafficking, betting and gambling activities using mule accounts at Indian crypto exchanges through VPN (virtual private network) receiving high volume deposits from un-hosted and offshore exchanges and laundering of cybercrime funds. The FIU-IND concluded that VDAs like Bitcoin, Tron and Stable coins (USDT/TRC-20) are very "widely" used by “illicit actors” because of their widespread acceptability and stability in value with offshore VDA service providers and un-hosted/un-identified wallets used to launder the proceeds of crime.

April - 28, 2025
Twenty-four cadres of the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist), including fourteen carrying a combined bounty of INR 2.85 million on their heads, surrendered in the Bijapur District in the Bastar division of Chhattisgarh on April 28, reports daijiworld.com. The surrendering Maoists reportedly cited their disillusionment with the Maoist ideology, the atrocities committed by the insurgents against local tribal communities, and internal conflicts within the banned organization as reasons for laying down their arms. They were also reportedly influenced by the state government's 'Niyad Nellanar' initiative, a development program focused on improving remote villages situated near security camps, police officials indicated. The surrendered individuals were associated with various Maoist formations, including the east Bastar division, Partapur area committee, and west Bastar division. Notable among them were Sudru Hemla, 33, a member of the Bhairamgarh area committee, and Kamli Modiam alias Urmila, 36, from the Partapur area committee. Both carried a reward of INR 500,000 each. Other significant surrenders included Jaymoti Punem, 24, with a bounty of INR 300,000, and Mangu Punem, 21, who had a reward of INR 50,000. Additionally, Buchchi Madvi alias Roshni, Sukhmati Ursa, Shamnath Kunjam, Chaitu Kursam, and Somli Hemla, each carrying a reward of INR 200,000, also surrendered. Other Maoists who surrendered include Bujji Padam, Sukko Punem, Hidme Veko, Soni Korsa, and Lachha Tati, each with a bounty of INR 100,000. The identity of the remaining Maoists is being ascertained.

April - 30, 2025
Around 167 terrorists were present in December 2024, 146 were present in January 2025, 138 in February, and 122 in March, across the border in Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), reports Hindustan Times on April 30. Over 120 militants were positioned monthly since December 2024 along the Line of Control (LoC), only around 40–50 terrorists were ready to infiltrate during the same months last year. “Some 40-50 terrorists attempted to enter every month between January and March last year. But from December 2024 onwards, Pakistan army and ISI activated their entire terror machinery. From Gurez, Uri and Keran sectors in Valley to Bhimber Gali, Poonch, Krishna Ghati and Samba in Jammu, over 167 terrorists were present in launch pads across the border, armed and ready to enter. In January, February and March too, over 120 terrorists each were present across the border, and they had orders to carry out regular shooting incidents, BAT attacks and IED blasts,” the officer said, citing intelligence inputs.

April - 30, 2025
On April 30, the 4th Meeting of the India-Egypt Joint Working Group (JWG) on Counter Terrorism was held in Cairo, Egypt, which was led by K. D. Dewal, Joint Secretary (Counter Terrorism), Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and Walid Al-Fiqi, Director of the Department of Counter Terrorism, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Egypt, reports mea.gov.in. India and Egypt strongly condemned the terrorist attack in Pahalgam in Jammu and Kashmir (J&K). Egypt reaffirmed its full support for India in confronting all forms of violence and terrorism aimed at undermining the country's security and stability. Both countries agreed to strengthen joint efforts in combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. Both sides discussed ways to strengthen areas of cooperation to counter new and emerging challenges such as the use of technology for terrorist purposes and financing of terrorism, including cryptocurrencies, unmanned aerial systems and misuse of cyberspace by terrorists for spreading terrorist propaganda. The two sides agreed to further strengthen bilateral cooperation in anti-money laundering efforts, drug trafficking and organised crime. Both sides agreed to deepen cooperation in training and capacity building, cyber security, use of AI for counter terrorism, exchange of best practices and information sharing. The two sides also discussed strengthening of multilateral cooperation in counter terrorism, including in the United Nations (UN), BRICS, the Global Counter Terrorism Forum (GCTF) and FATF.

April - 30, 2025
On April 30, the Government unveiled a dossier detailing Pakistan's global terror trail, spanning from Jammu and Kashmir (J&K) and Afghanistan to Russia, the United Kingdom (UK), and Bangladesh, labelling it as one of the most dangerous forces in the world, reports Tribune India. The document listed terror training camps hosted by Pakistan across Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Waziristan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK). These camps, operated by groups such as Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT), Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM), Hizbul Mujahideen (HM) and transnational outfits like Islamic State-Khorasan Province (IS-KP), served as hubs for radicalisation, weapons training and suicide mission preparation. Former Pakistani Army personnel often assist in training, lending military expertise to enhance operational lethality, it said. The report added, “For decades, Pakistani soil has been used as a launchpad for cross-border terrorism, insurgency and extremist ideology”. In Afghanistan, Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) backed the Afghan Taliban and the Haqqani network, responsible for numerous deadly attacks, including the 2008 Indian Embassy bombing in Kabul and the 2011 attack on the US Embassy. In Russia, Pakistan’s link was found in the 2024 Moscow concert hall attack, with reports suggesting the attackers may have had logistical or ideological support from Pakistani networks. the dossier details Pakistan’s ISI training and funding of Jamaat-ul-Mujahideen Bangladesh (JMB), the group behind the 2016 Gulshan café attack in Dhaka, which killed 20 hostages. In 2015, Bangladeshi authorities expelled Pakistani diplomats for funnelling funds to JMB operatives. A 2020 intelligence report revealed ISI’s involvement in training 40 Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh’s Cox’s Bazar camps through JMB, aiming to infiltrate them into India. JMB’s network, funded via Gulf-based Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs) and Pakistani intermediaries, extends to Bangladesh and India, with sleeper cells identified in West Bengal and Kerala.

Six cadres of the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist), three of them carrying rewards on their heads, surrendered in Dantewada District in the Bastar division of Chhattisgarh on April 30, reports The Print. With the latest surrender, 967 Maoists, including 229 carrying bounties, have so far quit the violence in Dantewada District under the ‘Lon Varratu’ (‘return to your home/village’ in the Gondi dialect) campaign since June 2020, Police said.

May - 1, 2025
For the ninth consecutive day on May 3 (today), the Pakistan Army resorted to unprovoked small arms firing on the Indian posts along the Line of Control (LoC) in Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), reports The Free Press Journal. A Defence Ministry statement on May 3 said, "During the night of May 2 and May 3, the Pakistan Army resorted to unprovoked small‑arms fire across the LoC opposite the Kupwara, Uri, and Akhnoor areas of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. The Indian Army responded promptly and proportionately." Pakistan opened fire in Poonch, Nowshera and Akhnoor sectors involving three districts of Poonch, Rajouri and Jammu in the Jammu region and Baramulla and Kupwara in the Kashmir valley on May 1, adds Daily Excelsior. The firing by the Pakistan army continued even after the Director Generals of Military Operations (DGMOs) of India and Pakistan spoke on the hotline on April 29. However, there was no damage on the Indian side in the Pakistan firing, while casualties or losses on the Pakistan side couldn’t be ascertained immediately. “During the night of May 1-2, 2025, Pakistani army posts resorted to unprovoked small arms fire from posts across the LoC opposite Kupwara, Baramulla, Poonch, Nowshera, and Akhnoor areas of Jammu and Kashmir,” a Defence spokesperson said.

A total of 17 locations came under the NIA’s scanner in the districts of Gurdaspur, Batala, Ferozepur, Fazilka, Tarn Taran, Amritsar and Faridkot, leading to the seizure of several incriminating materials, including mobile phones, digital devices and documents, it said. The searches were conducted in the case at the premises of suspects linked to Happy Passian and his nodes based in various countries, said the statement issued by the NIA. Passian is currently in the US where he was arrested last month and is a key operative of Pakistan-based Babbar Khalsa International (BKI) terrorist Rinda, it said. “Happy is believed to be the mastermind behind the series of recent grenade attacks at various police stations and police posts in the states of Punjab and Haryana,” the probe agency said. Rinda’s network of operatives, spread across various countries, has been actively involved in recruiting India-based associates for carrying out terrorist activities, according to NIA investigations. Besides recruitment of terror associates, Happy has also been engaged in a criminal conspiracy to provide funds, weapons and explosives to the field operatives of BKI through their associates and acquaintances based abroad, including in Pakistan, the statement said. Happy has already been declared a proclaimed offender (PO) in the case, it added. The NIA has also declared a reward of INR 500,000 against him. The NIA, which had registered the case suo motu against BKI operatives on the directions of the Ministry of Home Affairs, has so far arrested five accused and chargesheeted three. The anti-terror agency has also arraigned 12 others as accused in the case, including Rinda, another designated individual terrorist, Lakhbir Singh alias Landa, as well as Passian, the NIA said. All three, along with six others, are absconders in the case, in which a total of seven absconders have been declared as POs, it said. The NIA is continuing with its investigations in the case and is actively examining the incriminating materials seized during Thursday’s (May 1) searches, the statement added.

May - 2, 2025
A hill with an altitude of 5,000 feet that was once a hub of Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) along the Chhattisgarh-Telangana border has been reclaimed by the Security Forces (SFs) after driving out the extremists during a nine-day-long intense operation, reports The Telegraph on May 2. The rugged Karregutta hill located in a dense forest was a den of Maoist leaders like Hidma, Deva, Damodar, Azad and Sujata, but has now been taken over by SFs, with the Tricolour hoisted atop it. The operation launched in Chhattisgarh’s Bastar region, involved around 24,000 security personnel belonging to different units, including the District Reserve Guard (DRG), Bastar Fighters, Special Task Force (STF), all units of the state police, the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and its elite Commando Battalions for Resolute Action (CoBRA). The forces completed the climb over a span of nine days to take control of this strategic high point that is at an altitude of nearly 5,000 feet, sources said. The operation is part of the government’s action against Maoists. Union Home Minister (UHM) Amit Shah has set a deadline of March 31, 2026, to wipe out Maoists from the country. The Chhattisgarh government has categorically stated that no peace talks will be held with the Maoists. “A clear message has been sent out — those who surrender will be rehabilitated under the government’s surrender policy, but those who choose the path of violence will be dealt with strictly,” an officer said.

May - 2, 2025
Chaibasa Police, in coordination with Security Forces (SFs) including Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (CoBRA) 203 BN, 209 BN, Jharkhand Jaguar, Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) 26 BN, and other specialised units, have successfully dismantled a Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) arms cache in the forest areas of Vangram Luiya, Bamaibasa, and Gauburu under Tonto Police Station limits in West Singhbhum District of Jharkhand on May 2, reports aninews.in. During the operation, SFs discovered and destroyed an old Maoist dump, seizing significant quantities of explosives, including gelatin rods, detonators, and improvised explosive devices (IEDs), along with various other materials and daily-use items. A Bomb Disposal Squad (BDS) safely destroyed the recovered explosives to prevent any potential threat to security. The operation recovered six gelatine rods, two detonators, and one fuse. The SFs also seized 5 kilograms of semi-liquid explosives. Additionally, 3 IEDs with codex, each weighing approximately 3 kilograms, were found. The team recovered 41 iron rods, two pipes, and 80 metres of wire. Furthermore, two batteries and various other daily-use items were also seized from the site, according to a press statement.

May - 2, 2025
The ‘Government of the People’s Republic of Nagalim’ (‘GPRN’) said that the recent premeditated attack by Indian Security Forces (SFs) on a Naga Army camp under the Iloi Hau Battalion in Assam pushed the Indo-Naga peace process dangerously close to collapse, reports Northeast Now on May 2.  According to a press release issued by the GPRN, the incident took place in the forested area between New Kubin and Herakilua villages on April 29, 2025. The Naga Army confirmed the loss of three of its cadres. “It makes no sense to engage in peace talks in one region while waging war in another,” the statement said. They referenced the joint statement from June 14, 2001, which declared the ceasefire between the Government of India and the National Socialist Council of Nagalim-Isak-Muivah (NSCN-IM) as an understanding between two entities without territorial limits. In keeping with this, Naga Army camps continue to operate in all Naga-inhabited areas, observing ceasefire ground rules. However, GPRN accused Indian security forces of repeatedly violating the ceasefire’s spirit under various pretexts. Calling for clarity, ‘GPRN’ urged the Government of India to publicly declare whether the ceasefire extends to Naga areas in Assam and Arunachal Pradesh. If not, they warned, they would treat these regions as conflict zones.

On May 4, the Amritsar Police arrested two accused suspects, identified as Falaksher Masih and Suraj Masih, both residents of Ajnala’s Ballarhwa village, for allegedly passing sensitive information and photographs of Army cantonments and airbases to Pakistan’s spy agency Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), reports The Tribune. On May 5, a Pakistani hacker group calling itself the ‘Pakistan Cyber Force’ claimed to have accessed sensitive information after breaching Indian defence institutions, including the Indian Military Engineering Services (MES), the Manohar Parrikar Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses (MP-IDSA), and other websites, reports Hindustan Times. (iii) Gulpur Camp, Kotli, PoJK: Base for LeT terrorists operating in Rajouri-Poonch. Attacks in Poonch on April 20, 2023, and pilgrims on June 9, 2024, were planned in Gulpur. (iv) Abbas Camp, Kotli, PoJK: Nerve centre for training LeT’s suicide bombers, had a terrorist training infrastructure for about 50 terrorists; (v) Barnala Camp, Bhimber, PoJK: Used for training terrorists in weapons handling, Improvised Explosive Device (IED) making and jungle survival techniques (vi) Sarjal Camp, Sialkot District in Punjab Province of Pakistan: Terrorists who killed four J&K police personnel in March 2025 were trained here; (vii) Mehmoona Joya Camp, Sialkot District: Key training facility of Hizbul Mujahideen (HM) for operations in Kathua and Jammu regions; (viii) Markaz Taiba, Muridke in Sheikhupura District in Punjab Province: Headquarters of LeT led by Hafiz Syed. Terrorists trained here were also involved in the Mumbai attacks in 2008, and (ix) Markaz Subhan, Bahawalpur District in Punjab Province: Headquarters of JeM.

May - 9, 2025
Cornered by paramilitary forces and the State Police, the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) Party Telangana State Committee has announced a ceasefire for a period of six months, reports Telangana Today on May 9. A statement was released to the media in this connection by Maoist Telangana State Committee spokesperson Jagan. The ceasefire was announced in the wake of growing demand from majority political parties, people’s organisations and the common public for peace talks between the Maoists and the government, he said. The demand for peace talks first came forth in the Telugu States, as part of which a peace talks committee was formed. Hundreds of organisations, individuals, noted personalities and parties across the country have been supporting the demand, he said. He also lauded former Chief Minister K Chandrashekhar Rao’s reference to peace talks between Maoists and the government and his demand to the Centre to stop Operation Kagar. He welcomed Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) Member of the Legislative Council (MLC) K Kavitha’s demand for the same. A few days ago, Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy also wanted peace talks. All these have to be understood as a process to create a conducive atmosphere for holding peace talks. In order to build up the right conditions, the Maoist party announced a ceasefire, Jagan added.

May - 11, 2025
On May 11, Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) Lieutenant General Rajiv Ghai of the Indian Army confirmed that multiple high-value Pakistani terrorists,  belonging to Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT) and Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM), including those involved in the 1999 Indian Airlines flight (IC-814) hijacking and the 2019 Pulwama attack on security personnel, were among the 100 terrorists targeted in Operation Sindoor, at nine terror infrastructures in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK) on May 7, reports India Today and The Indian Express. These five terrorists were identified as Mudassar Khadian Khas and Khalid alias Abu Akasha of the LeT; and Mohammed Yusuf Azhar, Hafiz Mohammed Jaleel, and Mohammad Hassan Khan of the JeM. Mohammed Yusuf Azhar is the senior operative of the JeM and JeM ‘founder’ Masood Azhar’s brother-in-law, and a wanted accused in the 1999 IC-814 hijacking case. He was leading the JeM’s largest training camp in Balakot, Pakistan, when the IAF carried out airstrikes on it in 2019 as a response to the Pulwama terror attack. Mudassar Khadian Khas managed the affairs of Markaz Taiba, considered to be the LeT headquarters, in Pakistan’s Muridke. Hafiz Muhammed Jameel is a senior JeM operative and in charge of Markaz Subhan Allah, the headquarters of the JeM in Bahawalpur, Punjab Pakistan. According to the Army, Jameel was a member of the JeM Shura (its highest decision-making body) and a confidante of Masood Azhar. Mohammad Hassan Khan, the son of JeM’s ‘operational commander’ for PoJK, Mufti Asghar Khan Kashmiri, he was also associated with Indian fugitive Ashiq Nengroo, who is wanted for the 2019 Pulwama attack. Khalid alias Abu Akasha was involved in multiple terror attacks in J&K and played a key role in smuggling weapons from Afghanistan for the LeT. Khalid was a trained LeT terrorist who operated in J&K and exfiltrated back to Pakistan, where he operated from Peshawar. He recently shifted to the LeT HQ in Muridke and was part of the group’s ‘central committee’. “He worked closely with Central LeT/JuD entities: Yahya Mujahid, Qari Yakub Sheikh, Abdul Rehman, Khalid Waleed, Engineer Haris Dar and Abdul Rehman Abid,” an Army statement said.

May - 11, 2025
The massive anti-insurgency operation involving 28,000 troops, including the Indian Air Force (IAF), in Karregutta Hills on the Chhattisgarh-Telangana border to help eliminate the top leadership of the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) has been called off 20 days after it first started, reports The Indian Express on May 12. The operation, which also involved central and state police forces, first began on April 21 based on intelligence reports that the top Maoist leadership was “holed up” in the hill, safeguarded by the insurgents’ strongest and most dreaded armed wing — the Battalion 1 of the People’s Liberation Guerrilla Army (PLGA), officials said. Although officials have confirmed the operations have been called off, there is no official word yet on why this has happened. However, the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and the state police are scheduled to address the media Tuesday (May 13) morning.

May - 16, 2025
On May 16, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) arrested two Islamic State (IS) operatives, identified as Abdullah Faiyaz Shaikh alias Diaperwala, and Talha Khan, at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport in Mumbai, Maharashtra, reports Hindustan Times. They were arrested after being intercepted by the Bureau of Immigration at Terminal 2 as they attempted to return to India from Jakarta, Indonesia, where they had been in hiding. According to NIA, the duo was wanted in connection with a 2023 case involving the fabrication and testing of Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs) at a rented residence in Pune’s Kondhwa area, Maharashtra. During 2022-2023, they had organised a bomb-making training workshop at the same location, where a controlled explosion was conducted to test an IED they had manufactured. “These individuals were on the run for over two years and were declared absconders. Non-bailable warrants had been issued against them by the NIA Special Court in Mumbai,” the agency stated. A cash reward of INR 3,00,000 each had also been announced for information leading to their capture. They have already been charge-sheeted, along with eight other accused IS operatives, who are currently in judicial custody. The other arrested accused in the case include Mohammed Imran Khan, Mohammed Yunus Saki, Abdul Kadir Pathan, Simab Nasiruddin Kazi, Zulfikar Ali Barodawala, Shamil Nachan, Akif Nachan, and Shahnawaz Alam.

May - 18, 2025
Tritiya Sammelan Prastuti Committee (TSPC), a splinter group of the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist), registering its activity, has issued a stern warning to the Kendu leaf contractors by pasting pamphlets for the third consecutive day in Kunda in Chatra District of Jharkhand on May 18, reports livehindustan.com. Therefore, this time a strict warning has been issued to the middlemen. The TSPC outfit has asked the contractors to fulfill several demands in the name of helping the bidi leaf workers.

May - 19 May - 22, 2025
At a United Nations (UN) Commission on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice (CCPCJ) meeting held in Vienna in Austria from May 19-22, India highlighted the continued threat posed by Pakistan-based terror groups such as Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM), reports The Hindustan Times. Niraj Kumar Bansod, joint secretary at the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (UMHA), cited attacks including the 2008 Mumbai strikes and the recent Pahalgam attack, urging global action against terrorism. India called for the swift adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism, first proposed in 1996. The statement stressed that no motive can justify terrorism and pressed for accountability of perpetrators. Bansod also underscored India's efforts in Financial Action Task Force (FATF), its strengthened legal mechanisms, and steps against cybercrime, including the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). The address follows India’s Operation Sindoor, launched after the April 22, Pahalgam attack, and New Delhi’s global outreach to highlight cross-border terrorism.
