May - 20, 2025
On May 20, India reiterated that maritime security and counter-terrorism are vital to its national security and economic interests, especially amid evolving threats and geopolitical shifts in the Indo-Pacific, reports business-standard.com. Speaking at a United Nations Security Council (UNSC) high-level open debate chaired by Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis, India’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish, highlighted India’s comprehensive maritime strategy. Harish said India’s approach integrates strong defence capabilities, regional diplomacy, international cooperation, and domestic infrastructure development. As a nation with a long coastline and a major seafaring community, India is committed to being a responsible maritime power. He emphasized that India’s strategy addresses both traditional threats from state actors and non-traditional challenges like piracy, maritime terrorism, smuggling, illegal fishing, and hybrid threats. Harish noted that in response to rising piracy in the Western Arabian Sea, the Indian Navy deployed over 35 ships, conducted 1,000 plus boarding operations, and responded to over 30 incidents in 2024. India also underscored its adherence to a rules-based maritime order under UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and outlined five key principles, including peaceful dispute resolution, environmental protection, and responsible maritime connectivity.

May - 21, 2025
‘Politburo’ member and ‘general secretary’ of the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist), Nambala Keshavrao alias Basavaraj, is suspected to be among the 26 Maoists killed in an encounter with Security Forces (SFs) in the dense Abujhmad Forest in Narayanpur District in the Bastar division of Chhattisgarh on May 21 (today), reports The Times of India. The operation is ongoing along the border of Dantewada, Narayanpur, and Bijapur Districts, with high-ranking Maoist cadres among those killed, Police said. The number may be 26 or even more; however, Prabhat Kumar, Superintendent of Police (SP), Narayanpur, said, “The number (of eliminated Maoists) is not confirmed as the encounter is going on; we will inform later.” Police said that the encounter broke out when Maoists opened fire on teams of District Reserve Guards (DRG) during an operation in the Abhujmadh area following intelligence inputs about the presence of senior cadres of the ‘Maad division’ of Maoists. A 'supporter' of Police was killed, and a Police jawan (trooper) was injured in the gunfight, it is said. The encounter took place in dense forests between Abhujmadh and Indravati National Park when a joint team of DRG of Police from four districts was out on an anti-Naxal operation, said Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Sharma. "More than 26 Naxalites, some of them probably top cadres, were killed. One supporter of the Police was killed, and a Police jawan was injured in the action," said Sharma, who holds the state home portfolio. Combing operations are still underway, he added. Other prominent names reportedly killed include Madhu, a key leader of the Dandakaranya Special Zonal Committee (DKSZC), and Naveen, associated with the outfit’s publication wing ‘Jung’. Basavaraj had previously served as the head of the group’s ‘Central Military Commission (CMC)’ before becoming the ‘general secretary’ of the CPI-Maoist. Originally from Vizianagaram District in Andhra Pradesh, Basavaraj joined the Maoist movement during his student years in Warangal, where he was active in the Radical Students Union (RSU). He was wanted by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) and Police forces in both Telangana and Andhra Pradesh. The identities of the remaining slain Maoists are yet to be ascertained...A District Reserve Guard (DRG) jawan was killed in an improvised explosive device (IED) blast suspected to have been planted by the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) when the forces were returning after completing a combing operation in Bijapur District in the Bastar division of Chhattisgarh on May 21, reports The Indian Express. The blast took place hours after Security Force (SF) personnel gunned down 27 Maoists, including top leader Nambala Keshava Rao alias Basavaraju (70), in a major operation in the Abujhmad region. Ramesh Hemla accidentally stepped on an IED and died on the spot in the explosion. However, it is not clear whether the deceased jawan, Ramesh, was carrying out searches or returning from the morning’s encounter. Earlier, during the operation, another DRG jawan was killed in an IED blast. That jawan, Khotluram Korram (38), was from Bhatbeda village in Orcha, Narayanpur District. Earlier, South Asia Terrorism Portal (SATP) had reported the killing of ‘Politburo’ member and ‘general secretary’ of the CPI-Maoist, Nambala Keshavrao alias Basavaraj, along with 26 Maoists in an encounter with SFs in the dense Abujhmad Forest in Narayanpur District in the Bastar division of Chhattisgarh on May 21; it stands corrected to 27 Maoists killed, including top CPI-Maoist leader Basavaraju. One supporter of the Police was also killed in the encounter. Thus, the total fatality stands at 29 in the Narayanpur encounter on May 21.

May - 22, 2025
The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) Tribunal upheld the Union Ministry of Home Affairs' (UMHA) decision to extend the ban on the Hynniewtrep National Liberation Council (HNLC) of Meghalaya for another five years, The Hindu reports on May 22. The UMHA has consistently renewed the ban on HNLC since November 2000, with the latest extension in December 2024. According to the UMHA, 15–20 active HNLC cadres, including key leaders Sainkupar Nongtraw and Bobby Marwein, operate from Maulvi Bazar in Bangladesh. The UMHA noted that the HNLC remains actively involved in insurgent activities, including extortion, abductions, arms smuggling, and has ties with other insurgent outfits like the United Liberation Front of Asom-Independent (ULFA-I). The group also leverages social media platforms to radicalise and recruit local youth. From November 2019 to June 2024, authorities registered 48 cases against the HNLC, arrested 73 cadres, and recovered arms and explosives.

May - 24, 2025
Jharkhand Jan Mukti Parishad (JJMP) ‘supremo’ Pappu Lohra, who was carrying a bounty of INR 1 million on his head, and his aide, Prabhat Ganjhu, who was carrying a bounty of INR 500,000, were killed during an anti-Naxal operation conducted jointly by the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and the Jharkhand Police in a forest under the Latehar Police Station limits in Latehar District of Jharkhand on May 24 (today), reports Telangana Today. Acting on a tip-off that Lohra and his associates were in the forest, a team of security personnel led by Latehar Superintendent of Police (SP) Kumar Gaurav launched a search operation, Palamu Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIGP) YS Ramesh said. “As the Maoists spotted the security personnel, they fired at them, and the team retaliated. A cadre of the outfit was also injured and arrested during the encounter. Security Forces (SFs) recovered an INSAS (Indian Small Arms System) assault rifle from the arrested cadre. The deaths of Lohra and Ganjhu mark a significant blow to the JJMP’s activities in the region, further weakening the influence of the outfit in Jharkhand. JJMP is a splinter group of the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist).

May - 24, 2025
Police have intensified training for their Special Operations Group (SOG) personnel in jungle warfare to counter increasingly adept militants in the mountainous terrain of Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), reports India Today on May 24. The decision follows the attack in Baisaran Valley in Pahalgam in Anantnag District on April 22, where terrorists used dense forest cover to launch an assault, killing 26 people. The incident prompted security forces to re-evaluate their preparedness for guerrilla tactics. The initiative includes partnerships with the Greyhounds and the Jungle Warfare School in Telangana. Training is underway at regional camps like the White Knight Corps base in Talwara and the Corps Battle Schools in Doda district. Alongside combat skills, the strategy also emphasises human intelligence (HUMINT) as a critical component.

May - 26, 2025
India has resumed issuing visas to Afghan nationals, ending a suspension imposed after the Taliban’s takeover in August 2021, AMU TV reports on May 26. A new online visa platform launched in April 2025, now allows Afghans to apply for various categories, including business, medical, student, and cultural visas. Entry visas are also available for Afghan cultural figures, professionals, and family members of Indian citizens or Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) cardholders. The move is seen as a step toward re-engagement with Afghan citizens amid ongoing humanitarian and economic crises, although India has not formally recognized the Taliban regime.

May - 27, 2025
On May 27, Border Security Force (BSF) Inspector General (IG) Shankar Anand reiterated that they had also planned to strike terrorist launchpads near the Line of Control (LoC) on the night of May 9 and 10, reports Daily Excelsior. He emphasised that a Pakistani post had opened fire on Indian positions, for which the BSF was already prepared. “As a result of this preparedness, we inflicted heavy damage on several Pakistani posts during the cross-border firing. We did not suffer any losses ourselves,” Anand said. “On the night of May 8, when we carried out this operation, the enemy’s morale in that area was visibly shaken.” On May 9, Pakistan initiated unprovoked cross-border firing along the international border in the northern areas of Jammu, shifting focus from the Samba region. The BSF, anticipating such action, responded with heavy shelling on Pakistan’s border belt on May 9 and 10. “During this period, we had planned that if the opportunity arose, we would also strike the terrorist launchpads located near the international border,” he added. He further stated that the BSF conducted a “deliberate” and “planned” attack on a Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT) launchpad in the Looni area of Sialkot, Pakistan, located just three kilometres from the international border. Virender Dutta, Deputy Inspector General (DIG), said they had received intelligence about the presence of 18–20 militants in the Looni area who were planning to infiltrate by taking advantage of the cross-border firing. “After May 8, we received intelligence that 18–20 militants were present in Looni and were likely to attempt infiltration to target our installations. We executed a highly coordinated and well-planned operation in two phases to inflict maximum casualties. We achieved that goal, and Looni was destroyed,” Dutta stated.

May - 28, 2025
Bastar — once synonymous with the rise of Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) insurgency — and Kondagaon have been removed from the list of Left Wing Extremism (LWE)-affected districts by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (UMHA), marking a turning point in Chhattisgarh's mission to shed the baggage of Naxalism, reports The Times of India on May 28. Bastar and Kondagaon have now been sub-categorized as ‘districts of legacy and thrust', which means Maoist activities have come down to a great extent but still need sustained vigilance and developmental / operational focus. Other districts of Bastar division — Sukma, Bijapur, Narayanpur and Kanker — are still categorized as ‘most affected LWE districts' while Dantewada is identified among ‘other LWE districts'. Apart from this, several digital devices containing large volumes of incriminating data and documents have been recovered by NIA in these searches. These will be subjected to a thorough scrutiny by the agency to unravel the details of the terrorist conspiracy,” the statement said.

June - 5, 2025
On June 5, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) conducted a series of searches across Jammu and Kashmir (J&K) as part of its continuing investigations against terror conspiracy by Pakistan-backed proscribed terrorist organisations and their offshoots to destabilize J&K, reports x.com. Twenty-two locations in the Union Territory of J&K were searched as part of crackdown. The searches were conducted at the premises of hybrid terrorists and Overground Workers (OGWs) linked with the newly-formed affiliates such as The Resistance Front (TRF), United Liberation Front Jammu & Kashmir (ULF J&K), Mujahideen Gazwat-ul-Hind (MGH), Jammu & Kashmir Freedom Fighters (JKFF), Kashmir Tigers, People's Anti-Fascist Front (PAFF), a proxy outfit of the terror group Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM), among others. The case relates to the conspiracy and attempts by these newly floated outfits to destabilize the security situation in J&K by carrying out terror attacks by radicalizing local youth and mobilizing overground workers. The searches have led to the seizure of various digital devices and incriminating material. Investigations have revealed that Pak-based operatives were using various modes of online apps to plan and execute terror acts. They were also using drones to deliver weapons, bombs, and narcotics to their operatives and cadres in the Kashmir valley. The terror conspiracy was being hatched both physically and in cyberspace. It was being executed by the operatives of proscribed terrorist organisations, such as Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), JeM, Hizb-ul-Mujahideen (HM), Al-Badr, Al-Qaeda, etc., and their newly launched offshoots.

Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) is using social media influencers through a variety of lures to build a web of informers among the community, reports Indian Express on June 5. Two YouTubers, Jyoti Malhotra (Hisar, Haryana) and Jasbir Singh (Punjab), are part of a well-planned operation by Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) to increase its reach through the twin aims of collecting information and spreading propaganda. Central intelligence agencies and the Punjab Police have been unravelling the spy network which was cultivated by several officials based in the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi. The first step is to invite the influencers of various platforms like YouTube, Instagram, X, Snapchat, etc, to the get-togethers of the Pakistan High Commission, and then offer them visas to visit Pakistan,” the official said.

June - 7, 2025
A new terrorist outfit Tehrik-e-Taliban Kashmir (TTK), led by ex-Pakistan Air Force (PAF) officer Abdullah Umar Khan alias Ghazi Shehzad, has been formed, reports news.abplive.com on June 7. No sooner was it formed than it declared 'jihad' against India, rejected the Line of Control (LoC), and warned the Pakistan Army not to interfere in its anti-India jihad. According to a letter released by TTK, the group is led by Maulana Maqbool Dar and its spokesperson is Mufti Mehboob Butt Sopore. However, Intelligence sources claim these are fictitious names. In reality, the ISI has handed over the command to two individuals: former Pakistan Air Force officer and India's wanted terrorist Ghazi Shehzad, and Murtaza Khan alias Moosa Ghaznavi. Sources say Ghazi Shehzad served as a Captain in the Pakistan Air Force during the Kargil War. In 2000, he was awarded a certificate by then Pakistan Army Chief General Pervez Musharraf, a recognition typically given to junior officers for acts of valour during wartime. Shehzad has also served as a top ‘commander’ of Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK) and hails from Sudhnoti District in PoJK. The letter announcing the formation of TTK, which was released this past Sunday (June 1), was first issued by Moosa Ghaznavi, a former Lashkar ‘commander’ from Rawalakot, via a Telegram group. Both men have now been tasked with running this new terror group. Counter-terrorism experts from both India and Pakistan believe this new outfit is part of Pakistan Army Chief General Asim Munir's covert strategy to revive terrorism in Kashmir.

June - 7, 2025
Ahmedabad police have intensified efforts to curb the circulation of fake Indian currency notes (FICN), particularly INR 500 and INR 100 denominations, reports Times of India on June 7. A new, mobile-friendly identification system—developed by researchers at the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU)—is set to aid this initiative. Unlike traditional methods, the system uses the serial number on the currency note to cross-check with a central database, flagging instances where the number appears on the FICN watchlist. The NFSU team has been granted an Indian patent for this innovative method of counterfeit detection.

June - 9, 2025
Cybersecurity leader Fortinet reveals new findings from an International Data Corporation (IDC) survey highlighted 72 per cent of Indian organisations experienced Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered cyberattacks in the past year, and are struggling to detect or defend against such intrusions, reports Economic Times on June 9. The survey, which covered 550 information and Technology (IT) and cybersecurity leaders across 11 Asia-Pacific markets, shows that AI is rapidly becoming a preferred tool for attackers, allowing them to launch faster, more targeted, and harder-to-detect assaults. Nearly 70 per cent of Indian organisations reported a 2X surge in AI-driven threats, and 12 per cent observed a 3X increase. These AI-powered attacks exploit human behaviour, configuration errors, and identity systems. The top threats identified include: AI-assisted credential stuffing and brute-force attacks; Deepfake impersonations in business email compromise (BEC); Polymorphic malware; Automated reconnaissance; AI-generated phishing emails; Yet only 14 per cent of organisations said they were very confident in their ability to defend against these threats. 21 per cent admitted they cannot track AI-powered threats at all. The findings indicate a shift from episodic security incidents to constant exposure. The most commonly reported threats were: Software supply chain attacks (64 per cent); Cloud vulnerabilities (60 per cent); Phishing (54 per cent); Zero-day exploits (50 per cent); Ransomware (44 per cent). The survey also underscores a resourcing crisis in cybersecurity teams.

June - 12, 2025
Currently 12 terror training camps are functional in Pakistan, providing training in sophisticated weaponry and religious indoctrination to the new recruits, reports The Assam Tribune on June 12. In order to facilitate cross-border infiltration into India, 141 launch pads are currently functional in Pakistan occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK) and Pakistan. Pakistan army often indulges in cross-border firing as well as targeted actions against the Indian forces deployed along the border to facilitate infiltration of terrorists. Though Security Forces (SFs) are on high alert along the international border and many infiltration bids were foiled, it is not possible to guard every inch of the border round the clock because of the terrain involved. The terrorists take advantage of the situation and sneak into India, sources added. Sources pointed out that terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir (J&K) has been actively supported by Pakistan by way of aiding recruitment, training, infiltration and providing weaponry and funds to the terror groups. Ever since the emergence of Pakistan-sponsored terrorism in J&K in 1988, a total of 63,110 incidents of terror violence occurred in J&K with 31,791 incidents targeting SFs and 19,452 incidents involving civilians. As many as 47,841 people have lost their lives in these terror attacks, including 16,199 civilians, 6,270 SF personnel and 25,372 terrorists. At one point of time, around 30 different terrorist outfits were sponsored by Pakistan to operate in J&K. Presently, the prominent terror groups operating in J&K include Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM), Hizbul Mujahideen (HM), Muslim Jaanbaz Force, Al Badr, Al Barq, etc. In order to give an indigenous colour to their depredations and to escape international scrutiny, these groups have continued their activity in the name of The Resistance Front (TRF), a front for LeT, and People’s Anti-Fascist Front (PAFF), a front of JeM. The terror groups also have their presence on various social media platforms and indulge in online indoctrination and targeting of the youth to boost up recruitment.

On June 13, Maharashtra State Cooperative Bank (MSC Bank) launched Sahakar Suraksha, the country’s first Cyber-Security Operation Centre (C-SOC), in Vashi, Navi Mumbai (northern part of Navi Mumbai falls under Thane District, while the southern part is in Raigad District) of Maharashtra with an investment of INR 500 million, reports Economic Times. It aims to safeguard cooperative banks and their customers against rising cyber threats. One single fraud led to a loss of around INR 500 million,” said MSC Bank Chairman Vidyadhar Anaskar. C-SOC is designed to serve 31 District central cooperative banks in Maharashtra. Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven C-SOC can detect both known and emerging cyber threats in real-time and issue instant alerts to participating banks.

One of the chargesheeted accused is under arrest, who has been identified as Sodi Baman alias Deval. The absconders include two each of ‘central committee (CC)’ members and ‘special zonal/state committee (SZSC)’ members and other top cadres of the People's Liberation Guerrilla Army (PLGA) Battalion No. 1, Telangana ‘state committee’, and Pamed ‘area committee’ of CPI-Maoist, the officials said. The PGLA is the armed wing of CPI-Maoist. June - 14, 2025
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), in its Annual Report for 2024–25, reported a decline in counterfeit INR 2,000 notes, which contributed to an overall reduction in the value of fake banknotes, and rise in Fake Indian Currency Notes (FICNs) of INR 500 during the financial year 2025 (FY25), reports Times of India on June 14. Banknotes of the INR 2,000 denomination were withdrawn from circulation in May 2023, though they continue to be legal tender. According to the report, counterfeit notes detected in the denominations of INR 10, INR 20, INR 50, INR 100, and INR 2,000 declined in FY25. However, the number of fake notes in the INR 200 and INR 500 denominations increased by 13.9 per cent and 37.3 per cent, respectively, compared to FY24. A total of 2,17,396 FICNs were detected by banks and the Reserve Bank in FY25, marking a marginal decline of 2.3 per cent from 2,22,639 FICNs recorded in FY24. Specifically, fake INR 500 notes rose from 85,722 in FY24 to 1,17,727 in FY25, with their value increasing from around INR 43 million to INR 59 million. Meanwhile, counterfeit INR 2,000 notes saw a steep year-on-year decline of 86.5 per cent, falling from 26,035 in FY24 to 3,508 in FY25. Their total value dropped from INR 52 million to INR 7 million. Additionally, 32,660 fake INR 200 notes and 51,069 fake INR 100 notes were detected in FY25. Of the total counterfeit notes identified during the year, 95.3 per cent were detected by banks, while 4.7 per cent were detected at the Reserve Bank.

June - 16, 2025
On June 16, Goa Shipyard Ltd (GSL), a premier defence public sector undertaking, launched ‘Achal’—the fifth Fast Patrol Vessel (FPV) in a series of eight being built for the Indian Coast Guard (ICG), reports fortuneindia.com. The launch took place at the GSL facility in Goa. ‘Achal’ strengthens India’s coastal security and advances the goal of defence self-reliance. The 52-metre-long vessel is designed and constructed under dual-class certification from the American Bureau of Shipping and the Indian Register of Shipping, and features over 60 per cent indigenous content. Weighing 320 tons, the FPV is powered by a Controllable Pitch Propeller (CPP)-based propulsion system, allowing it to achieve a top speed of 27 knots, making it ideal for rapid-response maritime operations. Its core operational roles include the protection of offshore assets, surveillance of exclusive economic zones (EEZs), and security of island territories—missions that are becoming increasingly critical amid evolving maritime security challenges in the Indian Ocean Region.

June - 18, 2025
On June 18, Ottawa’s intelligence agency confirmed in a report that Khalistani extremists continue to operate from within Canada—raising funds, spreading propaganda, and targeting India as their primary focus, Hindustan Times reported. The report highlighted that politically motivated violent extremism (PMVE) in Canada, particularly since the mid-1980s, has largely manifested through Khalistani elements advocating for an independent Khalistan carved out of India’s Punjab. It stated that a small group of these extremists continues to use Canadian soil as a base for fundraising and planning violence, primarily targeting India. The agency emphasised that such ongoing activities pose a serious national security threat not only to Canada but also to its global interests. “Since the mid-1980s, the PMVE threat in Canada has manifested primarily through Canada-based Khalistani extremists seeking to use and support violent means to create an independent nation state called Khalistan, largely within Punjab,” the report said. Under its section on India, the report further alleged that “Indian officials, including their Canada-based proxy agents, engage in a range of activities that seek to influence Canadian communities and politicians.” It added that when such activities are “deceptive, clandestine, or threatening,” they are considered acts of foreign interference. The report also identified China as the most significant intelligence threat to Canada, while also naming Pakistan, Russia, and Iran as countries of concern. Additionally, it referenced the assassination of Sikh separatist Hardeep Singh Nijjar, who was shot dead in Surrey, British Columbia, on June 18, 2023.

June - 19, 2025
On June 19, the Special Court of the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in Kolkata, West Bengal, sentenced an accused—Najiur Rahman Pavel alias Joyram Byapari alias Joseph—to six years of rigorous imprisonment (RI) in connection with an anti-India terror conspiracy linked to Jamaat-ul-Mujahideen Bangladesh (JMB), reports NIA. In addition to the prison term, the court imposed a fine of INR 20,000 on the convict. The case was originally registered in July 2021 at the Special Task Force (STF) Police Station in Kolkata regarding the illegal entry of Bangladeshi nationals Sk Shabbir, Joseph, and others into India. Investigations revealed that members and sympathisers of JMB had conspired with unknown associates to wage war against India and Bangladesh. The accused were reportedly motivated by extremist ideology to establish a ‘Caliphate’ by overthrowing India’s democratically elected government through violent means. The NIA took over the investigation in August 2021 and filed its main chargesheet against five accused in January 2022. All five remain in judicial custody. Earlier, in November 2024, another accused—Rabiul Islam—was convicted and sentenced to five years of RI and fined INR 20,000 in (RC-19/2021/NIA/DLI). The trial against the remaining three accused is currently ongoing.

June - 19, 2025

Two ‘divisional committee members (DCMs)’, Madakam Rama alias Raghu and Madakam Bheema alias Srikanth, four ‘area committee members (ACMs)’, two party members, two ‘militia’ (people’s army of the Maoists) members, and two Revolutionary People’s Committee (RPC) members were among those who surrendered to Police, SP B Rohith Raju said. With increasing pressure from the Chhattisgarh Police, Maoists were moving towards villages on the borders of Telangana. The district Police, in coordination with the CRPF, were maintaining high alert to prevent them from entering the State, Rohith Raju noted, appealing to underground Maoist cadres to surrender and join mainstream life to live peacefully with their family members. The district Police would ensure to provide them with livelihood support and rehabilitation, he added. The identities of the remaining surrenderees are yet to be ascertained.

As many as 294 Maoists surrendered to the Kothagudem Police so far this year because of the welfare measures being taken up for the surrendered Maoists and adivasi people under the ‘Operation Cheyutha’ programme. Three divisional committee members (DVCM), 17 area committee members (ACM/PPCMs), 34 party members, 107 militia members, 35 Revolutionary People’s Committee (RPC) members, 47 Dandakaranya Adivasi Kisan Mazdoor Sangathan (DAKMS/KAMS) members, 30 Chaitanya Natya Mandali (CNM) members and 21 Grama Rakshaka Dalam (GRD) members were among those who surrendered before Police, the SP said.

June - 20, 2025
Intelligence agencies have uncovered new strategies adopted by terrorist groups to expand their networks in India following the interrogation of Javed Munshi, a suspected senior operative of the banned outfit Tehreek-ul-Mujahideen (TuM), reports by ETV Bharat on June 20. Munshi was arrested on December 22, 2024, in a joint operation by the Jammu and Kashmir (J&K) Police and West Bengal’s Special Task Force (STF) near Canning in South 24 Parganas District, West Bengal. A resident of J&K, Munshi is believed to be deeply involved in TuM’s operations. Information extracted during interrogation indicates that the group has been operating covertly, focusing on indoctrinating and radicalising youth. The TuM reportedly incites hatred against the Indian government and has discussed launching a youth-driven movement similar to that of Bangladesh’s liberation struggle. Munshi, who is skilled in assembling improvised explosive devices (IEDs), received training in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (POK). He is also reported to have links with key terrorist figures, including Talha Saeed, son of Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT) founder Hafiz Saeed. His level of training has been compared to that of Ajmal Kasab, the lone surviving attacker from the 2008 Mumbai attacks, raising alarm about the potential scale of the threat. Investigations reveal that Munshi facilitated the illegal entry of Bangladeshi nationals into India, providing them with fake Indian documents and Pakistani passports to enable their onward travel to Pakistan via Nepal. His operations reportedly spanned multiple states and included a network of active sleeper cells both within India and abroad. Central agencies have filed complaints against Munshi, citing his widespread influence and involvement in producing fraudulent documents to aid cross-border terrorist movements. Further interrogation is expected to yield critical intelligence regarding TuM’s plans and its network infrastructure across the country.

June - 21, 2025
On June 21, an Afghan national, Mohammad Yousaf alias Yaha Khan, was arrested at Bhubaneswar airport upon arrival from Dubai on an IndiGo flight, reports New Indian Express. He was found using a forged Indian passport (No. U1380251) issued in the name of Yaha Khan, allegedly a resident of Cuttack District of Odisha. The arrest was made after Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) (Immigration) Samapika Pattnaik’s team flagged the suspicious document during routine immigration checks. A subsequent verification revealed a lookout circular (LOC) issued from Kolkata airport and confirmed Yousaf’s true identity using his genuine Afghan passport (No. 02457655). He had allegedly entered India illegally in 2018 and lived undetected for years by adopting a fake Indian identity. Investigators found that Yousaf had fraudulently obtained multiple Indian documents, including Aadhaar, PAN, Voter ID, and Driving License, and used them to travel, open bank accounts, and conduct business across states. Authorities seized forged identity cards, foreign currencies, INR 80,000 in cash, a smartphone, gold earrings, a motorcycle registration certificate, and bank documents. Officials have raised concerns over the potential misuse of such fake identities for espionage, smuggling, or terrorist activities. Yousaf has confessed during interrogation and is currently in judicial custody.

June - 21, 2025
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has dismantled a criminal network run by the banned Popular Front of India (PFI) and its political wing, the Social Democratic Party of India (SDPI), that channeled over INR 620 million to finance terrorist training, communal unrest, and radicalisation across India, reports News18 on June 21. According to ED sources, the network laundered funds through fake trusts, underground hawala routes, and fraudulent financial practices, aided by operatives with domestic and international connections. At the core of the operation is MK Faizy, SDPI National President of SDPI and PFI National Executive Council (NEC) member, who mobilised funds from within India and Gulf nations, especially Qatar and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Faizy handled INR 15,40,000 in illicit funds through HDFC Bank, camouflaged as political income, later used to support riots, murder plots, and radical training camps. He was supported by Wahidur Rahman, who managed field-level cash movement through party sympathisers. Rauf Sherif, head of PFI’s student wing Campus Front of India (CFI), played a key role in channelling funds from abroad, working with Shafeeque Payeth, a Doha-based operator critical in routing donations from overseas. Operatives Ashraf MK and Abdul Razak were instrumental in converting illegal funds into real estate, laundering money into legitimate assets. Rasheed and Kunju, also linked to SDPI, were directly involved in ground-level violent acts, including communal attacks and unrest. The investigation reveals that the SDPI-PFI network exploited India’s political and civil liberties infrastructure to mask their true agenda of terror financing and radicalisation, using party status and activism as a front.

June - 22, 2025
On June 22, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) arrested a key accused involved in the attempts to revive a Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) Northern Region Bureau (NRB) terror module, reports The Hindu. The agency also seized digital devices, including hard drives, pen drives, and mobile phones, as well as other “incriminating” material during a search in the West Delhi house of the accused person identified as Vishal Singh, originally from Mathura District in Uttar Pradesh. “Investigations have revealed that the accused, a member of the CPI (Maoist), had delivered a drone to leaders of the banned terror outfit in the Chhakarbandha/Panchrukhiya Forest area of Bihar to further its anti-national activities. He had imparted technical training to other members of the group and had also attended meetings with its ‘central committee (CC)’ members in Bihar in 2019,” the probe agency said, adding, “The case relates to the terror organisation’s conspiracy to re-energise its decrepit influence in the Northern Regional Bureau (NRB) area, comprising Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Delhi, Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh. The conspiracy involves recruitment and strengthening of the organisation in the region through underground cadres working in urban areas, along with some Over Ground Workers (OGWs) operating in the guise of activists”. According to the NIA, several front organisations and student wings have been used to prepare the ground as part of the conspiracy in order to “wage war against the Government of India”. The suspects were receiving funds from the outfit’s Eastern Regional Bureau, particularly from Jharkhand.

June - 22, 2025
On June 22, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) has arrested two persons for harbouring the terrorists who had carried out the attack at the Baisaran Maidan near Pahalgam in the Kashmir Valley on April 22, 2025, that killed 25 tourists and a local pony walla and injured 16 others, reports Daily Excelsior. The NIA, in a statement issued in Srinagar, said that the two persons – Parvaiz Ahmad Jothar from Batkote, Pahalgam, and Bashir Ahmad Jothar of Hill Park, Pahalgam – have been arrested for harbouring the terrorists who carried out the attack. The statement said that the arrested duos have disclosed the identities of the three-armed terrorists involved in the attack. It said that they have also confirmed that they were Pakistani Nationals affiliated with the proscribed terrorist outfit Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT). “Parvaiz and Bashir had knowingly harboured three armed terrorists at a seasonal dhok (hut) at Hill Park before the attack, as per NIA investigations. The two men had provided food, shelter and logistical support to the terrorists, who had, on the fateful afternoon, selectively killed the tourists on the basis of their religious identity, making it one of the most gruesome terrorist attacks ever,” it read.

June - 28, 2025
Over the past 18 months, Security Forces (SFs) have achieved significant success in anti-Naxal operations in Chhattisgarh, neutralising 435 Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) cadres, including a record 48 women operatives, officials said on June 28, reports The New Indian Express. According to the official data, women now account for approximately 10 per cent of the total Maoists killed between 2024 and June 20, 2025, the highest number of female Naxal casualties recorded in any such period since 2001. The sharp increase in neutralisation of Maoist operatives (198) in 2025 alone marks a significant blow to Left Wing Extremism (LWE) in the region. A senior security official stated, “The CPI (Maoist), a banned organisation under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA), has for years strategically coerced, misled and forcibly inducted women and young girls into its ranks. These recruits were subjected to emotional, social and psychological manipulation, depriving them of the opportunity to make informed decisions about their lives.” He added that once inducted, women were rarely empowered or promoted within the Maoist hierarchy. “Instead, they were exploited as foot soldiers and human shields during encounters, while senior male leaders stayed protected.” The data also highlights a growing disillusionment within Maoist ranks. In the same 18-month period, 1,457 operatives surrendered, and 1,469 were arrested. Officials attribute this shift to sustained security pressure and the government’s rehabilitation and infrastructure development efforts in affected regions.

If you do not surrender, we have decided to end Naxalism by March 31, 2026. Should we not end the Naxalites who have killed adivasis and police personnel?” Shah said. Addressing a gathering in Nizamabad, the UHM said that while he “feared that the Congress might provide shelter to Maoists, there was no cause for concern as Narendra Modi was in power at the Centre”. “The Congress is asking for talks with Maoists. Our government’s policy is clear — no talks with those who hold weapons. Surrender and join the mainstream,” he said. “In the last one-and-a-half years, around 2,000 Maoists surrendered,” he added. “From Telangana’s soil, I want to ask those who speak of protecting Naxals: What answer will you give to the families of police personnel and adivasis who lost their lives in Naxal violence? Naxals have obstructed development in adivasi areas for decades. What is your answer?” he asked.

June - 30, 2025
The Border Security Force (BSF) has recovered over 130 drones from along the International Border with Pakistan in Punjab in the first six months of the year, The Tribune reported on June 30. In addition, the BSF has also seized close to 135 kilograms of narcotics, including heroin, and 79 weapons of different kind from January 1 till June 30 this year, according to sources. Last year, the BSF had seized 283 kg of narcotics along the border in Punjab while neutralising 294 drones, a substantial increase from 107 drones in 2023. According to an unnamed BSF personnel, the use of drones has increased substantially to smuggle narcotics, weapons and fake currency in the country from across the border. The Amritsar Tarn Taran belt and the Ferozepur region are hotspots in Punjab for illegal drone activity. Most drug consignments recovered by the BSF had been dropped by drones originating from Pakistan. China-made Mavick series drones are commonly used for smuggling, which carry a packet weighing 450-550 gram, generally wrapped in a yellow adhesive tape. BSF personnel said that the drone menace was being effectively countered by increasing employment of anti-drone systems along the border and regularly reviewing operational procedures.

June - 30, 2025
The Tamil Nadu Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), with support from the Annamayya District Police, arrested two absconding operatives of the banned terrorist outfit Al Ummah — Abu Bakar Siddique alias Amanullah and Mohammed Ali alias Mansoor — in Rayachoti town, in Annamayya District of Andhra Pradesh, on June 30, reports India Today. The duo had been on the run since 1999 and were wanted in multiple high-profile bomb blast cases across Tamil Nadu, including in Chennai, Trichy, and Coimbatore. During a house search, the accused's wives — Saira Bhanu (wife of Siddique) and Sheikh Shamim (wife of Ali) — initially cooperated but later attempted to assault women police personnel. Both women were arrested and remanded to Kadapa Central Jail. Extensive searches were conducted at locations including Kothapalli and Mahbub Basha Street in Rayachoti. Police recovered a large quantity of explosive material: Ammonium nitrate mixed with fuel oil, Slurry explosives (possibly containing Trinitrotoluene (TNT) or nitroglycerin), A 20 kg suitcase bomb based on pentaerythritol tetranitrate (PETN), Two other suspected Improvised explosive device (IEDs), Potassium nitrate, chlorate, permanganate, Gunpowder, ball bearings, nuts and bolts, Timer mechanisms, pressure and pull switches, and speed controllers. In addition, authorities seized walkie-talkies, radio equipment, hacking software, mobile phones, digital storage devices, coding manuals, binoculars, edged weapons, maps of Indian cities, religious literature, and financial documents including cheque books and property papers. Both suspects have a history of involvement in terror cases. Siddique is named in the 1995 Nagur Police Station murder and explosives case, the Chintadripet blast, and the 2011 pipe bomb attempt targeting former Deputy Prime Minister L.K. Advani during his rath yatra in Madurai. Mohammed Ali is accused of planting a bomb outside the Commissioner’s Office in Egmore, Chennai, in 1999. In another notable 1999 incident, the duo was allegedly transporting explosives on the Cochin–Kurla Express when a fire broke out, leading to their interception at Kasaragod, Kerala. Earlier, on July 3, SATP had reported the arrest of Abu Bakar on July 1, however, disclosing the details at a press conference, Kurnool Range Deputy Inspector General Dr Koya Praveen, Indian Police Service (IPS), and Annamayya District Superintendent of Police V Vidyasagar Naidu, IPS, said the two accused — Abu Bakar Siddique and Mohammed Ali were arrested on June 30.

July - 1, 2025
The Allahabad High Court (HC) has denied bail to a 62-year-old man, Ansar Ahmad Siddique, who was arrested for sharing a video on Facebook containing slogans of "Pakistan Zindabad," reports The Times of India on July 1. The court held that Siddique’s actions were “disrespectful to the Constitution and its ideals” and amounted to “a challenge to the country’s sovereignty.” The video, posted on May 3—shortly after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir—was seen by the state as evidence of support for terrorism on religious grounds. While Siddique sought bail citing his age and medical condition, the prosecution strongly opposed his plea. Justice Siddharth observed, “Commission of such offences is becoming a routine affair... because the courts are liberal and tolerant towards such acts of people with an anti-national bent of mind. It further stated that Siddique’s “irresponsible and anti-national conduct does not entitle him to seek protection of his right to liberty guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution.”

July - 2, 2025
A senior Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) couple active in Left Wing Extremism (LWE) for over 25 years surrendered before the Police and Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) in Mohla Manpur district of Chhattisgarh on July 2, reports hornbilltv.com. The Maoist couple—Jeevan Tulavi alias Ram Tulavi (45), and his wife, Agasha alias Aarti Korram (35)—surrendered in the presence of Inspector General of Police (IGP), Rajnandgaon Range, Abhishek Shandilya; Superintendent of Police (SP) Y. P. Singh; and Commandant of 27 Battalion ITBP Vivek Kumar Pandey, along with officers from 44 Battalion ITBP. According to an official release from the ITBP, Jeevan Tulavi, a resident of Parvidih village under Mohla Police Station, was a ‘Divisional Committee Member (DVCM)’ and the ‘Education Unit Commander’ of the Maad Division and carried a reward of INR 800,000 on his head. His wife, Agasha, a resident of Telitola village under Mohla Police Station, served as an ‘Area Committee Member (ACM)’ and worked with the press team of the Maad Division. She also headed the Chetna Natya Mandali (CNM), the Maoists’ cultural wing. Since the early 2000s, she had been active as a singer, dancer, poet, orator, and composer, in addition to managing computer operations and preparing press releases for the outfit.

July - 4, 2025
The overground workers (OGW) and sympathisers of the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) central zone have been actively found involved in extortion and harbouring cadres of the banned terror organisation, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) revealed following the interrogation of a CPI-Maoist operative, Rajesh Deogam, of the West Singhbhum District of Jharkhand, reports etvbharat.com on July 4. Following his direct involvement in supporting Maoists, Deogam has been charged under various sections of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), the Arms Act, the Explosive Substances Act, and the UAPA. The revelation comes at a time when the security agencies have launched an all-out operation to end the menace of Left-Wing Extremism (LWE) in India by March 2026. Union Home Minister (UHM) Amit Shah has recently reiterated that Maoists will be eliminated by next year. Following strong directives from the Centre, the security agencies, especially the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), have launched ‘Operation Black Forest’ in the forest areas of Chhattisgarh and Telangana. Interrogation conducted by the NIA has revealed that the ultras at present are facing a severe crisis of funds and weapons. "Between January and February, the central zone of the CPI (Maoist) held a meeting where it was decided to intensify extortion, arms collection, and other activities to revive the Maoists," said a senior security official aware of the development. The meeting, according to the official, took place in the jungle of Chhattisgarh. Some of the OGW and sympathisers who were present in the meeting have been instructed to handle arms, collect ‘levy’ (extortion money), and harbour cadres of the banned terror organisation. The central zone of the Maoists involves areas of Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Bihar, Maharashtra, and Andhra Pradesh. "We have the anticipation that following pressure from the security agencies, the ultras would try to revive the organisation by any means," the official said, adding that "both the central and state security agencies have been directed to take strong actions against anybody found involved in terror activities or supporting terrorists."

July - 4, 2025
The Supreme Court (SC) has issued a notice on a plea filed by Safdar Nagori, former chief of the banned outfit Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI), seeking clarity on the status of his sedition case appeal, reports India Today on July 4. Nagori, who has been in jail for 17 years, was sentenced to life imprisonment by a trial court in a sedition case and had challenged the verdict in the Madhya Pradesh High Court. However, the High Court recently declined to pronounce an order, citing the Supreme Court’s 2022 directive to pause all sedition proceedings nationwide. Nagori has now approached the apex court for clarification on whether this stay applies to appeals against prior convictions. His petition argues that a ruling is necessary to resolve his pending appeal filed in 2017. Acknowledging the legal complexity, the Supreme Court noted that the matter involves interpreting a decision by a three-judge bench and cannot be clarified by a two-judge bench. Nonetheless, it has agreed to examine the issue and has issued notice to the concerned parties. Nagori remains imprisoned under multiple charges, including sedition and anti-national activities.

July - 7, 2025
Fresh clashes between two pro-democracy rebel groups in Myanmar's Chin State have triggered a massive influx of refugees into Champhai District of Mizoram, reports Northeast Now on July 7. Fighting between the Chin National Defence Force (CNDF) and Chinland Defence Force (CDF)-Hualngoram erupted near Khawmawi village in Myanmar, close to the Indo-Myanmar border, forcing over 3,000 civilians to flee into Zokhawthar village in Champhai District of Mizoram. The two groups—comprising members of the same Zo ethnic community—are battling for control over Khawmawi, a key commercial transit point. Gunfire and stray bullets caused panic in Zokhawthar village, with some rounds reportedly hitting houses. Although no local casualties were reported, one Myanmarese refugee drowned in the Tiau River while attempting to cross into India. Assam Rifles sealed the border but are permitting refugee entry on humanitarian grounds. Injured cadres have also been brought to Mizoram for treatment.

July - 8, 2025
On July 8, in its latest report titled "Comprehensive Update on Terrorist Financing Risks," the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) has flagged the growing misuse of e-commerce platforms and online payment services for terror financing, reports indiatvnews.com and Indian Express. Citing incidents from India, including the 2019 Pulwama attack and the 2022 Gorakhnath Temple assault, FATF warned that digital platforms are increasingly being used by terrorists to mobilise funds, evade detection, and finance operations. A key component of the Pulwama Improvised Explosive Device (IED) - aluminium powder - was procured via the EPOM Amazon platform to enhance the blast impact. FATF noted that terrorists use such platforms not only for procuring materials like weapons, chemicals, and 3D-printing supplies but also to sell low-value items to fund their activities. Regarding the 2022 Gorakhnath Temple incident, the report detailed how an Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIL)-inspired attacker transferred INR 6,70,000 (USD 7,736) via PayPal to foreign accounts and received INR 10,323 (USD 188) from abroad. The accused used Virtual Private Network (VPN) services to mask his location and made payments to VPN providers through his bank account. Investigations revealed 44 international third-party transactions and transfers to ISIL-linked individuals abroad. “Several forms of support have been reported, including direct financial support, logistical and material support, or the provision of training. Delegations reported state sponsorship for TF purposes coupled with sanctions circumvention techniques through trade and smuggling mechanisms where the national government potentially plays a supportive role,” the report said.

July - 10, 2025
On July 10, Financial Action Task Force (FATF) report on global terrorist financing risks has, for the first time, acknowledged the role of “states” as sponsors of terrorism — a position India has long advocated, particularly in relation to Pakistan, reports Times of India. India had highlighted state-sponsored terrorism from Pakistan as a key source of terrorist financing risk in its 2022 money laundering and terror financing risk assessment. A senior government official said the FATF’s latest findings reinforce India's stance, noting that this is the first time the intergovernmental watchdog has explicitly introduced the concept of state-sponsored terrorism in its assessments. The report states, “Political and economic realities within states play a significant role in the close cooperation between criminal elements and terrorist organisations' operations and settlements.” It emphasised that weak governance, systemic corruption, and high crime levels within certain states significantly shape terror financing risks. Terrorist and criminal groups, the report said, flourish in states lacking effective legal and institutional frameworks, particularly those offering lucrative criminal opportunities. The FATF also highlighted the use of formal banking channels by Pakistan-based terror groups and noted that organisations like Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT) and Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) have exploited non-profit organisations (NPOs) and gaming platforms to raise funds. “Sham NPOs are established or registered knowingly for terror financing and used to raise, store, and move funds, commonly under false charitable pretexts,” the report stated. It also raised alarms about the growing use of online gaming platforms by terror outfits for financial transactions.

His wife, also an active Maoist, surrendered alongside him. The surrendered members were active in the Kutul, Nelnar, and Indravati area committees within the Maad division of Narayanpur District. Superintendent of Police (SP) Robinson Guria said that among the notable ones who surrendered are Manku Kunjam alias Sukhlal Kunjam, ‘secretary’ of the Kutul Area Committee, with a bounty of INR 800,000; Hidme Kunjam, Supply Team ACM, with a bounty of INR 500,000; Punna Lal alias Boti alias Santu Oyam, Nelnar Area ‘Jan Militia’ (peoples’ army of the Maoists) ‘commander’, with a bounty of INR 500,000; and other cadres holding various leadership positions within the Janatana Sarkar (People's Government of the Maoists) and militia groups, with bounties ranging from INR 50,000 to INR 100,000. The identities of remaining surrendered Maoists are being ascertained. SP Robinson Guria appealed to the Maoists to “leave behind deceptive external influences and restore Maad to its rightful inhabitants so they can live fearless, normal lives.”

July - 11, 2025
The Maharashtra Legislative Assembly has passed the Maharashtra Public Security Bill 2024, aimed at tackling the spread of radical Left-Wing Extremism (LWE) ideologies and Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) influence in the state, reports India Today on July 11. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, who introduced the bill, said it seeks to ban individuals and organisations that promote violence, engage in guerrilla warfare, or attempt to destabilise the government through unlawful means. Fadnavis highlighted that the influence of Maoist ideology had been reported in both urban and rural regions of Maharashtra, particularly in districts like Gadchiroli and Konkan. The bill is designed to address these threats, especially where existing laws like the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA) fall short, as UAPA is limited to direct terrorist activities. Under the new law, a three-member authority – comprising a sitting or retired High Court judge, a district magistrate, and a public prosecutor – will oversee case reviews before prosecution to ensure fair and transparent application.

July - 14, 2025
Hindustan Times reported on July 14, that evidence collected by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), including intercepted conversations and emails between 26/11 accused Tahawwur Rana, David Coleman Headley and Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT) planners in Pakistan, forms the key basis of conspiracy charges filed by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in a supplementary charge sheet. Tahawwur Rana, accused in the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, was extradited to India from Los Angeles, California, US, on April 10, 2025, following a five-year legal battle. The FBI recorded a crucial conversation between Rana and David Headley during a car ride on September 7, 2009, where they discussed the Mumbai attacks, praised LeT, and spoke of a meeting with 26/11 handler Abdur Rehman Hashim Syed alias Pasha in Dubai. Emails from August 2009 between Headley and LeT operative Sajid Mir also revealed Rana's approval of the attacks. Evidence includes travel records of Rana’s Dubai visit before the attacks, memory cards with photos and videos of Indian targets, false documents for Headley’s Indian visa, and financial records showing Rana wired money to Headley during his trips to India. Rana’s Mumbai office of the Immigration Law Centre, which served as a front for Headley’s surveillance activities, is also central to the case. Indian investigators, who questioned Headley in the US in 2010, used his testimony to establish his close relationship with Rana, dating back to their time at a military boarding school in Pakistan. The NIA has included leases, travel details, and statements from a protected witness who received Headley in Mumbai on Rana’s instructions.

July - 14, 2025
India’s Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) has launched a sweeping investigation into cryptocurrency exchanges Binance and WazirX over suspected use of digital assets in cross-border terror financing, reports ainvest.com and financefeeds.com on July 14. The investigation, triggered by recent intelligence inputs and the July 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, focuses on suspicious transactions involving TRX tokens linked to wallets in Pakistan, Jammu & Kashmir, (J&K) and Syria—regions associated with extremist activity. Authorities believe private crypto wallets and lax Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) practices may be facilitating these illicit flows. Enforcement Directorate (ED) and Jammu & Kashmir’s State Investigation Agency (SIA) are coordinating efforts, with ED probing Binance for Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) violations and freezing accounts linked to Indian partners. SIA recently raided locations in Jammu, Doda, and Handwara under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA). WazirX is also under scrutiny, with links to a 2023 National Investigation Agency (NIA) case involving a student who used the platform to fund slamic State of Iraq and Syria/Daish (ISIS) operations via TRX tokens.

On July 14, the Supreme Court dismissed a plea challenging the five-year extension of the ban on the Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI), reports NDTV. July - 14, 2025
The Centre on July 14, raised objections to the maintainability of the Popular Front of India’s (PFI) petition challenging the five-year ban upheld by a tribunal under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA) in Delhi High Court, reports The Hindu. Additional Solicitor General S.V. Raju argued that since the tribunal was headed by a sitting High Court judge, its decision could not be challenged under Article 226 or 227 of the Constitution. Instead, he said the only legal remedy lay under Article 136 before the Supreme Court. PFI’s counsel maintained that a similar issue was previously heard by a division bench of the High Court, making the petition maintainable. The court deferred the matter for further hearing on August 7, and has yet to issue a formal notice.

July - 15, 2025
According to The Times of India on July 15, the April 22 terrorist attack in Baisaran valley in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), was a secretive operation jointly planned by Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) and terror group Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT), under directives from Pakistan’s political and military leadership. It was executed by Pakistani terrorists, with no local operatives involved in the planning. The attack squad was led by Sulaiman, a suspected former Pakistani Special Forces commando, trained at LeT’s Muridke camp in Punjab Province of Pakistan and armed with an M-4 rifle. He infiltrated J&K in 2022 and was also involved in the April 2023 Poonch District of J&K Army truck attack. Satellite phone tracking placed Sulaiman near the Baisaran valley a week before the Pahalgam incident. Two other Pakistani terrorists were part of the squad, though their identities remain undisclosed. Investigations ruled out the involvement of previously suspected Pakistani terrorists Hashim Musa and Ali Bhai, and local terrorist Adil Hussain Thoker. Currently, around 68 foreign and three local terrorists are active in the Valley, with only one new local recruitment reported in 2025.

July - 15, 2025
Seven accused, including Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) linked Thadiyantavide Naseer, pleaded guilty in the 2023 Bengaluru Central Prison terror conspiracy case, The Indian Express reports on July 15. A special court in Bengaluru accepted their application, filed under Section 229 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC), which allows conviction without a full trial. The accused admitted guilt voluntarily, according to the court. The case, being investigated by the National Investigation Agency (NIA), involves 12 accused, with Naseer allegedly radicalising inmates between 2017 and 2023 to pursue jihad upon release. The NIA also recently arrested three more individuals—Anees Fathima (mother of absconding accused Junaid Ahmed), Dr Nagaraj S (a prison psychiatrist), and ASI Chan Pasha—for aiding the accused through financial transactions, smuggling phones, and leaking escort details. The initial chargesheet was filed in February 2024, and further charges were added after the extradition of Salman Khan from Rwanda and links to another accused arrested earlier. Naseer, a key figure in the 2008 Bengaluru blasts and a convict in a Kerala Students' Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) case, is accused of orchestrating a terror module within prison.

July - 16, 2025
India has reaffirmed its commitment to combating money laundering and terror financing by aligning its domestic frameworks with global standards set by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), reports ddnews.gov.in on July 16. The FATF regularly identifies jurisdictions with weak measures through its public “grey list” and “blacklist.” As of June 13, 2025, 24 countries — including South Africa, Syria, and Vietnam — are under increased monitoring. Nations like North Korea, Iran, and Myanmar remain on the blacklist due to persistent strategic deficiencies. Notably, FATF data shows that out of 139 countries reviewed, 86 have undertaken reforms to strengthen their AML/CFT frameworks. India’s proactive approach is reflected in its consistent alignment with FATF standards and its contributions to global assessments and case studies, demonstrating its role as a responsible player in safeguarding global security and financial transparency.

Security Forces (SFs) conducted searches in Kathua and Samba Districts on July 16 after villagers reported the movement of suspicious persons in the twin border towns, reports Daily Excelsior. The SFs said a search operation along the Hiranagar forward area of Kathua District was launched after villagers spotted two suspected individuals late on July 15 night. Another operation was launched in Dagore Village of Samba District after villagers reported the movement of two suspected persons on July 15 night. Locals said they spotted two suspicious individuals moving towards a river in the village and informed the Police. Accordingly, the area was cordoned off and searched thoroughly by the Special Operation Group (SOG) and Army teams who found nothing during the searches, they said.

July - 17, 2025
An Indian-Canadian gangster was arrested in the United States (US) for running a transnational drug operation along with a notorious Irish gang, Hindustan Times reported on July 17. The gangster, identified as Opinder Singh Sian (37), worked with the Irish Kinahan gang to smuggle methamphetamine and fentanyl precursors at an international level. US court documents reveal that Sian was arrested in Nevada in the month of June by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). The court documents also reveal that Sian, supported by Turkish and American criminal organisations, was involved in a conspiracy to import “precursor chemicals from China and export narcotics through the port of Los Angeles to Australia,” the report added. Sian, linked with Brothers Keepers in Surrey in British Columbia, was arrested in Arizona, and the affidavit was filed in California. A Nevada judge ordered Sian held in custody pending his transfer to California, adding that other suspects in the case have not been charged yet.

July - 17, 2025
An international narco-terror network has been uncovered through a covert operation by the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) at Vancouver Port, Canada, exposing a dangerous alliance between Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Chinese chemical suppliers, and Latin American drug cartels, reports Money Control on July 27. Top Indian intelligence sources confirm this operation validates long-standing concerns about Canada becoming a hub for hybrid security threats. The DEA’s investigation, which began in 2022, ended in the unsealing of an affidavit revealing a British Columbia-based fentanyl syndicate with deep global links. At the centre of the network is Indo-Canadian national Opinder Singh Sian, kingpin of the brothers Keepers gang, which Indian agencies describe as a proxy for Mexico’s Sinaloa cartel. Sian acts as a key intermediary between ISI handlers in Lahore, Chinese chemical firms, and global drug syndicates. The gang’s activities reportedly extend beyond drug trafficking to include funding Khalistani propaganda, arms smuggling, and sleeper cell recruitment in Punjab. ISI and Chinese actors are exploiting Canada’s permissive legal and political environment to channel synthetic opioids and launder money through crypto-based hawala systems, NGO fronts, and encrypted networks routed via Dubai, Hong Kong, and Lahore. Indian security agencies have identified over 40 Indo-Canadian individuals, including gurdwara-linked fundraisers and radical influencers, as part of this transnational network supporting extremist activities in Punjab, Delhi, and Kashmir. Officials warn that this ISI–China–Cartel nexus presents a serious hybrid threat to national security and stress the urgent need for stronger international counterterrorism cooperation.

On July 21, in a major verdict, the Bombay High Court acquitted all 12 individuals convicted in the 2006 Mumbai train blasts case, including five who were on death row, reports Hindustan Times. July - 22, 2025
On July 22, India condemned Pakistan’s sponsorship of cross-border terrorism during a high-level open debate at the United Nations (UN), chaired by Pakistan, reports the Hindustan Times. Ambassador P. Harish, India’s Permanent Representative to the UN, stated: "I am also constrained to respond to the remarks made by the representative of Pakistan. The Indian subcontinent offers a stark contrast in terms of progress, prosperity, and development models. On the one hand, there is India—a mature democracy, a surging economy, and a pluralistic and inclusive society. At the other extreme is Pakistan, steeped in fanaticism and terrorism, and a serial borrower from the IMF." The debate was one of two signature events organized by Pakistan as part of its Presidency of the UN Security Council for July. India’s remarks came in response to Pakistan’s Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar, who earlier condemned India’s so-called “occupation” of Jammu and Kashmir and criticized India's move to place the Indus Waters Treaty in suspension. July - 24, 2025
Bengaluru, Karnataka-based cybersecurity and threat intelligence firm, CloudSEK, has uncovered a vast and organised Fake Indian Currency Note (FICN) network operating across popular social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube, and FICN worth INR 175 million was pushed into circulation over just six months, reports cnbctv18.com on July 24. CloudSEK’s threat intelligence division, STRIKE (threat intelligence team of CloudSEK), identified over 4,500 social media posts, more than 750 user accounts, and 410+ phone numbers actively promoting FICN. Sellers showcased bundles of fake INR 500 and INR 2,000 notes in videos, offering as much as INR 5,00,000 FICN in exchange for INR 1,00,000 in genuine money. One such video even advertised: “COD available. Delivery across India,” with the seller’s contact number clearly displayed. The report highlights that many transactions are initiated via WhatsApp or phone calls, with sellers providing live video demonstrations and handwritten signs displaying contact numbers as proof of authenticity. Alarmingly, some sellers also exploit Meta Ads and hashtags like #fakecurrency and #A1note to evade detection. High-quality counterfeit notes are reportedly produced using Adobe Photoshop, industrial-grade printers, and specialised paper embedded with green security threads and watermarks. Photoshop (.PSD) templates are also shared within the network, enabling individuals to print fake notes at home. Employing a combination of Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) and Human Intelligence (HUMINT) techniques, CloudSEK traced several key operators to Jamade village in Dhule District of Maharashtra. Identified sellers include Vivek Kumar, Karan Pawar, and Nishant Chavare. Overall, the network is estimated to comprise around 350 active sellers. CloudSEK believes at least INR 175 million worth of counterfeit currency circulated between December 2024 and June 2025—though the actual amount could be significantly higher.

July - 24, 2025
The Uttar Pradesh (UP) Police's Anti-Terror Squad (ATS) has uncovered a terror funding network in Balrampur District of UP, bordering Nepal, with illicit funds traced to Pakistan, reports India Today on July 24. This follows recent attention due to the Chhangur Baba religious conversion case in Balrampur. According to police, the accused used cyber fraud to transfer money into the bank accounts of local youths in Balrampur, a region known for criminal activities due to its proximity to the Nepal border. These funds, totalling nearly INR 500 million, were subsequently funnelled to Pakistan through approximately 100 identified bank accounts. The investigation revealed connections to a larger INR 7000 million cyber fraud case in Raebareli District of UP, indicating a broader syndicate. July - 28, 2025
Terrorist activity in Jammu and Kashmir (J&K) has seen a sharp decline this year, with Indian Security Forces (SFs) tightening their grip on militant networks, particularly those led by Pakistani operatives, reports India Today on July 28. According to intelligence inputs, 42 terrorist launch pads remain active across the Line of Control (LoC) in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), housing an estimated 110 to 130 terrorists. Currently, around 70 to 75 terrorists are active in the Kashmir Valley, and another 60 to 65 in the Jammu, Rajouri, and Poonch districts. Of these, about 115 are believed to be Pakistani nationals. Intelligence reports also note that terrorist recruitment among the local young populace has dropped significantly; only four locals have joined terror groups this year, pointing to a major setback for Pakistan-backed terror operations. SFs have reportedly neutralised one terrorist every five days this year. Of the 75 terrorists killed so far, a majority were foreign nationals. These include 17 militants killed while attempting infiltration along the LoC and International Border (IB) and 26 eliminated in interior encounters. The counter-terror operations have dealt a severe blow to militants across the region. Most of the 42 non-local terrorists killed were in five districts of Jammu division: Jammu, Udhampur, Kathua, Doda, and Rajouri. In the Kashmir division, foreign terrorists were mostly gunned down in Baramulla, Bandipora, Kupwara, and Kulgam. Baramulla has emerged as the deadliest zone for foreign terrorists, with 14 non-local militants killed in nine encounters. SFs struck key locations like Sabura Nala, Kamalkot, and Main Uri sectors near the LoC, as well as interior regions such as Chak Tappar Kriri, Sopore’s Nowpora, Hadipora, Sagipora, Watergam, and Rajpore. "The local terrorist group has almost been wiped out," said a senior official.

July - 28, 2025
The Aurangabad bench of the Bombay High Court (HC) in Maharashtra granted bail to three suspected Popular Front of India (PFI) members — Sayyad Faisal Sayyad Khaleel, Abdul Hadi Abdul Rauf Momin, and Shaikh Irfan Shaikh Salim alias Irfan Milli — reports livelaw.in on July 28. The court held that merely attending seminars or physical training sessions like karate conducted by the PFI does not amount to a terrorist act under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). The trio was arrested on September 22, 2022, following an FIR lodged by the Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) a day earlier. The FIR, based on secret information, alleged that PFI organized arms training and hate speech events in 2021 and 2022, promoting anti-government narratives and urging Muslims to join the outfit. The court noted that the PFI was banned only on September 28, 2022, a week after the arrests, and was not listed as a terrorist organization under UAPA at the time. The National Investigation Agency (NIA) cited the recovery of weapons and videos, but the court found no evidence linking the accused to any terrorist act or government destabilization. It also highlighted the slow progress of the trial, with only five of 145 witnesses examined in over two years. Citing prolonged custody and lack of substantive evidence, the bench granted bail to the accused.

July - 29, 2025
On July 29, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) informed the Lok Sabha (Lower house of the Parliament) that the Government of India has adopted a comprehensive, multi-dimensional strategy to tackle internal and cross-border terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), reports risingkashmir.com. The approach focuses on enhanced security deployment, intelligence coordination, financial crackdowns, and legal enforcement. In a written reply, Minister of State for Home Affairs Nityanand Rai emphasised the Centre’s “zero-tolerance” policy towards terrorism, particularly in sensitive regions like J&K. These measures are being implemented in close coordination with the Union Territory administration, security forces, and intelligence agencies. To bolster internal and border security, the Centre has deployed additional Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and reinforced the counter-insurgency grid. Surveillance capabilities have been scaled up using drones, UAVs, satellite imagery, and thermal sensors under the Comprehensive Integrated Border Management System (CIBMS), now operational along vulnerable stretches of the Line of Control (LoC) and International Border (IB). Other initiatives include intensified day-and-night domination, construction of strategic roads, tunnels, border outposts, and round-the-clock checkpoints at critical points across the region. Joint patrolling and enhanced coordination with neighboring countries aim to secure cross-border routes. Internally, sustained operations by CAPFs, the Indian Army, and J&K Police seek to dismantle terror networks. Preventive measures and targeted investigations by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) focus on identifying and neutralizing strategic supporters of terrorism. To disrupt terror financing, the government has institutionalized dedicated units—the Combating Financing of Terrorism (CFT) Cell in the MHA and the Terror Funding and Fake Currency (TFFC) Cell within the NIA. These bodies collaborate with financial intelligence units to monitor suspicious transactions, hawala operations, and NGO-linked funding.

July - 29, 2025
On July 29, Union Home Minister (UHM) Amit Shah told Parliament that terror incidents in Jammu and Kashmir (J&K) have dropped by nearly 80 per cent between 2015 and 2025 compared to the preceding decade, attributing the decline to the revocation of Article 370 and decisive security action on the ground, reports kashmirlife.net. Citing comparative figures, Shah said that from 2004 to 2014, the region witnessed 7,217 terror incidents, resulting in the deaths of 1,770 civilians and 1,060 security personnel. In contrast, between 2015 and 2025, there were only 2,150 such incidents, with 357 civilians and 542 security personnel killed. “The number of terrorists neutralised has increased by 123 per cent,” he added.
