July - 30, 2025
According to a Zee News report dated July 30, Pakistani government agencies are actively supporting major terror outfits in rebuilding infrastructure destroyed during India’s Operation Sindoor. At least 13 new terror camps and launchpads are reportedly under construction in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), utilizing new methods and advanced technologies to evade surveillance and bolster militant capabilities. The camps are being reconstructed in key locations including Kel, Shardi, Dudhniyal, Athmuqam, Jura, Lipa Valley, Tandapani, Nayyali, Jankot, and Chakothi. Additionally, four launchpads along the International Border in the Jammu region — Masroor, Chaprar, and a drone center at Shakargarh — are reportedly being reactivated. Unlike earlier methods, the reconstruction is being executed using modern tactics and technologies. To avoid detection by Indian intelligence and minimize casualties during potential future operations, Pakistan is now constructing small, high-tech “mini camps” that train 20–30 terrorists at a time, compared to earlier camps which trained 70–80 militants. These camps are located in densely forested areas and are reportedly equipped with radar camouflage, satellite masking, and other advanced tools. The Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) has allegedly allocated 100 crore Pakistani rupees to fund the reconstruction efforts. The decision was finalized during a high-level meeting in Bahawalpur — a known stronghold of Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) — in June. This meeting was intercepted by Indian intelligence agencies and reportedly included top commanders of JeM, Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT), Hizbul Mujahideen (HM), The Resistance Front (TRF), and senior ISI operatives. The key agenda of the meeting was to reorganize operational leadership, redistribute weapons, and resume recruitment efforts both in Pakistan and Jammu & Kashmir. Sources reveal a renewed focus on recruiting local youth and leveraging existing networks in PoK, in response to the depletion of terrorist ranks due to India’s ongoing counter-terrorism operations.

July - 30, 2025
On July 30, India and United Arab Emirates (UAE) decided to further strengthen their bilateral defence ties, including maritime security collaboration through real-time information sharing, joint manufacturing initiatives and enhancing military training cooperation, reports Times of India. The two countries agreed to elevate their defence ties to match the growing momentum in areas such as trade, investment, and social relations during the 13th joint defence cooperation committee (JDCC) meeting co-chaired by defence secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh and UAE’s under-secretary of defence Lt General Ibrahim Nasser M. Al Alawi here. “India offered to provide customized training courses tailored to the UAE military’s needs. A MoU was also signed between the Indian Coast Guard and the UAE National Guard to establish a framework for enhanced cooperation in search and rescue operations, pollution response, anti-piracy efforts, and related maritime security domains,” an official said. This comes after India in April had offered the indigenous Akash air defence missile system, which can intercept hostile aircraft, helicopters, drones and subsonic cruise missiles at a range of 25-km, to the UAE at a meeting between defence minister Rajnath Singh and Dubai crown prince Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.the two sides also held discussions on training cooperation, defence industrial partnerships, and Service-to-Service engagements. “They agreed to pursue joint manufacturing initiatives, including models similar to the collaboration between ICOMM (India) and CARACAL (UAE) for small arms production,” the official said. “The potential for co-developing next generation defence technologies in emerging areas such as Artificial Intelligence was also discussed, alongside opportunities in shipbuilding, refits, upgrades, and maintenance of common platforms,” he added. India and the UAE share a growing defence relationship, underpinned by the “comprehensive strategic partnership” established during PM Narendra Modi’s visit to the country in 2015, as part of the former’s continuing outreach to the Gulf region.

July - 30, 2025
The Resistance Front (TRF) had twice claimed responsibility for the Pahalgam terror attack and “published a photograph of the attack site”, the UN Security Council’s sanctions monitoring team has said, reports Daily Excelsior on July 30. The team in a report also cited assertions that the attack could not have happened without the support of Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Tayyiba (LeT). The 36th report of the Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team concerning ISIL (Da’esh), Al-Qaeda and associated individuals and entities, released United Nations on July 29, mentions the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack in which 26 civilians were killed, saying “five terrorists attacked a tourist spot in Pahalgam, in Jammu and Kashmir”. The report, which was submitted to the 1267 ISIL (Da’esh) and Al-Qaeda sanctions committee of the UN Security Council said, “The attack was claimed that same day by The Resistance Front (TRF), who in parallel published a photograph of the attack site.” The report said that the “claim of responsibility” by TRF was “repeated the following day. On 26 April, however, TRF retracted its claim. There was no further communication from TRF, and no other group claimed responsibility,” it said. The report cited a member state which said that “the attack could not have happened without Lashkar-e-Taiba support, and that there was a relationship between LeT and TRF. Another member state said that the attack was carried out by TRF, which was synonymous with LeT.” It also noted that one member state “rejected” these views and said that LeT was “defunct”.

July - 31, 2025
A new report titled "Transnational Repression in the UK" by the UK Parliament’s Joint Committee on Human Rights (JCHR) has accused 12 foreign governments, including India, of targeting critics, activists, and dissidents living in Britain through threats, surveillance, and intimidation, reports bhaskarenglish.in on July 31. The report claims such interference is instilling fear among affected communities, curtailing their freedom of expression and movement, and creating an unsafe environment in the UK. The committee has urged the British government to take stronger action against such foreign interference, which it says poses a serious threat to human rights and democratic freedoms. Alongside India, the report names Bahrain, China, Egypt, Eritrea, Iran, Pakistan, Russia, Rwanda, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and the United Arab Emirate (UAE). In India’s case, the report specifically references activities related to the pro-Khalistan group Sikhs for Justice (SFJ). The report also raises concerns about the misuse of Interpol’s mechanisms to pursue political dissidents abroad — with China, Russia, and Turkey identified as primary offenders, and India among several other countries cited. As of now, India has not issued an official response to the allegations.

July - 31, 2025
On July 31, a special National Investigation Agency (NIA) court acquitted all seven individuals charged in connection with the 2008 Malegaon bomb blast in Maharashtra, citing insufficient and unconvincing evidence, reports Hindustan Times. The verdict comes nearly 17 years after the September 29 blast during the final namaz of the day at a public compound in Malegaon, which killed six people and injured 95 others. Among those acquitted were Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Member of Parliament (MP) Pragya Singh Thakur, 55, and Lt. Col Prasad Purohit, 53, an officer in the Indian Army. “Terror has no religion, as no religion promotes violence,” observed special NIA judge A.K. Lahoti while delivering the judgment. The five others acquitted were retired army officer Ramesh Shivaji Upadhyay (73), Pune-based businessman Samir Sharad Kulkarni (53), Purohit’s alleged associates Ajay Eknath Rahirkar (56) and Sudhakar Omkarnath Chaturvedi (53), and Swami Amritananda Devtirth, also known as Sudharkar Dhar Dwivedi (56). The court noted that there was no credible evidence proving that Purohit had procured RDX from Kashmir, as alleged in the chargesheet. It also found no evidence linking the bomb-laden motorcycle recovered from the scene to Pragya Thakur.

On August 2, India firmly rejected a British parliamentary committee report that accused India of engaging in transnational repression against political dissidents residing in the UK, calling the allegations "baseless," reports India Today. Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated, “These claims stem from unverified and dubious sources, predominantly linked to proscribed entities and individuals with a clear, documented history of anti-India hostility.” The report, titled Transnational Repression in the UK and published by the UK Parliament's Joint Committee on Human Rights, cited claims made by 'Sikhs for Justice'—a US-based group advocating for a separate Khalistan state. The organization has been banned in India under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). The committee called for stricter measures to counter transnational repression and urged British authorities to support affected diaspora communities.

August - 2, 2025
Security Forces (SFs) arrested three suspected Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) operatives near Go Gunda village in Bijapur District in the Bastar division of Chhattisgarh on August 2, recovering a significant stockpile of explosives and materials linked to extremist activity, reports daijiworld.com. The arrests were made during a joint operation by the District Reserve Guard (DRG) and local Police under the Kerala Pal Police Station limits, an area known for Maoist presence and ongoing counterinsurgency operations. According to Bijapur Superintendent of Police (SP) Jitendra Yadav, one of the arrested individuals carried a bounty of INR 200,000, suggesting his possible involvement in high-level Maoist activities. While the identities of the suspects have not yet been made public, officials confirmed they are being interrogated for more information on their network and recent movements. Among the items recovered were tiffin bombs, detonators, fuse wires, and other components typically used in Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs), a method frequently employed in Maoist ambushes against SFs and public infrastructure. Preliminary intelligence indicates the trio may be affiliated with DAKMS (Dandakaranya Adivasi Kisan Mazdoor Sangh) and KAMS (Krantikari Adivasi Mahila Sangathan), two organisations often identified as Maoist frontals involved in local mobilisation in tribal belts.

August - 3, 2025
A railway trackman was killed and another was severely injured in a landmine blast suspected to have been triggered by the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) in the Sundargarh District of Odisha on August 3, reports The Telegraph. Deceased Etawa Oram, 37, had been carrying out maintenance work on tracks with others when the explosion occurred. Injured Budharam Munda has been admitted to the Rourkela General Hospital. The blast occurred on the last day of the ‘martyrs’ week’ observed by Maoists since July 28. Police seized several Maoist leaflets from the area, which falls within the Saranda Forest region along the Odisha-Jharkhand border. Rourkela Superintendent of Police (SP) Nitesh Wadhwani said, “The IED [Improvised Explosive Device] blast occurred around 10am on the Rengra (Odisha) and Karampada (Jharkhand) rail route, mainly used for mineral transport. We had prior information about Maoists. Sanitisation began in the morning. During track scanning, the blast occurred, killing a South Eastern Railway employee and injuring another. The injured worker is stable.” The explosion left a deep crater on the tracks. “Train movement will remain suspended until complete sanitisation is ensured. We will not take any risks,” Wadhwani said.

August - 4, 2025
On August 4, Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi hailed Operation Sindoor as a pivotal, intelligence-driven mission that has redefined India’s counter-terrorism strategy, reports The Hindu. Speaking at Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras on the theme “Operation Sindoor – A New Chapter in India’s Fight Against Terrorism,” General Dwivedi emphasized the operation as a landmark moment that demonstrated the Armed Forces’ capability to address evolving threats and showcased preparedness for fifth-generation warfare. He highlighted that the 88-hour operation was unprecedented in its scale, range, depth, and strategic impact, carried out across the DIME spectrum (Diplomatic, Information, Military, and Economic). General Dwivedi underscored the shifting nature of modern warfare, pointing to the rise of non-contact warfare, strategic tempo, and psychological dominance as defining characteristics of fifth-generation conflicts. He affirmed the Indian Army’s commitment to self-reliance under the initiative “Swadeshikaran Se Sashaktikaran.” The Army Chief also detailed key collaborations under national technology missions like INDIAai, Chip-to-Startup, and Project QuILA, with MCTE Mhow serving as a strategic partner. He commended innovative projects undertaken by Indian Army Cells at IIT Delhi, IIT Kanpur, and Indian Institute of Science (IISc Bengaluru), recognizing the importance of academic partnerships in enhancing military capabilities.

August - 4, 2025
On August 4, while speaking at Indian Institute of Technology (IIT-Madras), Indian Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi said the four-day clash under Operation Sindoor between India and Pakistan could have lasted “14 days, 140 days, or even 1,400 days,” and stressed the need to prepare for a potentially larger, multi-front war, reports Daily Excelsior. Calling the operation a “whole-of-nation” effort with a rare political free hand, Gen. Dwivedi revealed that Indian forces struck seven of nine planned targets, hitting deep into Pakistan’s “heartland” for the first time, killing several terrorists and shocking the adversary. He said the Army was prepared to absorb any blowback. Emphasizing the importance of “narrative management,” he noted that strategic messaging—such as the first post-strike statement, “justice done”—was key to influencing domestic, adversary, and neutral audiences. He warned that future conflicts could involve multiple countries, with both of India’s borders “live or semi-live.” Gen. Dwivedi also called for modernizing the Army down to the soldier level, advocating an “eagle on the arm” approach—equipping each of the 12 lakh soldiers with a drone—to meet the demands of multi-domain, next-generation warfare.

August - 4, 2025
The Punjab Government on August 4 rolled out the second phase of its anti-drug campaign, Yudh Nasheyan Virudh 2.0, aiming to involve citizens directly in the war against drugs, reports New Indian Express. As part of this initiative, Defence Committees will be formed in both rural and urban areas to help uproot drug trafficking networks. These village-level (rural) and ward-level (urban) committees will consist of 10 to 20 members each, serving as community vigilantes to monitor and report drug-related activities. They will work closely with the Police to keep peddlers and smugglers out of their areas. Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann said the campaign, which began on February 4 this year, has reached its final phase. “The backbone of the drug supply chain has been broken. These committees will now ensure that our villages and cities remain drug-free,” he said.

August - 5, 2025
Between 2016 and 2021, fake Indian currency notes (FICN) seizures more than doubled, while registered cases dropped by 50 per cent, suggesting a higher volume of fake notes per seizure, reports IndiaSpend on August 5. In 2022, law enforcement seized 4.2 million counterfeit notes worth INR 3820 million—seven times more in volume and 19 times in value than the previous year, according to NCRB data. However, bank detections have declined, with only 230,000 fake notes identified in 2022—about 2 per million notes in circulation, down from 7 per million in 2016. By March 2025, bank data showed per million notes:  two fake INR 100 and INR 500 notes, and four fake INR 200 notes.  Following the 2023 withdrawal of INR 2,000 notes, counterfeit detections for that denomination fell from 22,000 (2018–19) to 3,508 (2024–25). State trends show Gujarat led with over 3 million fake notes in 2022, followed by Karnataka (450,000) and Bihar (270,000), while West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh saw declines. Despite higher seizures, cases filed fell from 1,662 in 2015 to 688 in 2021, pointing to fewer but larger hauls. The INR 500 note remains the most counterfeited, while fake INR 200 notes have surged—from 79 in 2017–18 to 32,660 in 2024–25.

August - 5, 2025
Martin Kerketta, the ‘chief’ of the People’s Liberation Front of India (PLFI), a splinter group of the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist), was gunned down during an encounter in the Parhi-Chhangabari Forests in the Gumla District of Jharkhand on August 5, reports The New Indian Express. Kerketta carried a bounty of INR 1.5 million on his head and had been on the Police radar for a long time. According to Police sources, Kerketta had assumed leadership of the PLFI following the arrest of its former ‘chief’, Dinesh Gope, in Nepal. Both Gope and Kerketta were childhood friends and had studied together, later working jointly to expand the organisation. Terming it a significant blow to the PLFI, an offshoot of the banned CPI-Maoist, Police officials said the operation was launched following a tip-off that Kerketta was in the area to collect extortion money from a local businessman. A team, led by Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Nazir Akhtar, was dispatched to trace his location. On spotting the Police, Kerketta and his squad opened fire. In retaliatory firing, Kerketta was killed on the spot, officials said. “A few weapons have been recovered from the encounter site,” said the Superintendent of Police (SP). “Two firearms were seized. A team of Gumla Police was actively involved in the operation,” he added. It is believed that two other Maoist operatives were also injured during the exchange of fire. Kerketta, a resident of Redma village in Kamdara, was an active member of the PLFI’s ‘central committee’. He played a key role in formulating strategies related to extortion, intimidation, and armed operations. His criminal activities largely revolved around extortion in the name of the PLFI.

August - 6, 2025
Nine cadres of the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) carrying a combined bounty of INR 2.4 million surrendered in the Bijapur District in the Bastar division of Chhattisgarh on August 6, reports The Times of India. The surrendered rebels included members of company number 1, platoons number 12 and 13 of the Marh division, as well as members from the technical team of the south Bastar division and the ‘DGN (Dhamtari-Gariabandh-Nuapada) division’. Among them were two ‘area committee members (ACMs)’, a Dandakaranya Adivasi Kisan Majdoor Sangathan (DAKMS) member, and a ‘commander’ of the Bhoomkal ‘militia’ (people’s army of the Maoists). They were identified as Baksu Oyam, carrying an INR 800,000 bounty, active since 2007, a party member of company number 1; Budhram Potam, carrying a cash reward of INR 500,000, an ACM of platoon 12, active since 2000; Hidma alias Hiriya, worth INR 500,000, ACM of platoon 13; and those carrying an  INR 200,000 bounty were Mangu Uika alias Toggi, from South Bastar's technical team; Roshan Karam alias Ajit, from the Chinnapalli area committee under the ‘DGN division’; and Manglu Podiyam, a party member from the Bhairamgarh area committee. The others were DAKMS members Kamlu Hemla and Budhram Hemla, and Pandru Punem alias Padkhuta, Bhoomkal ‘militia’ ‘commander’ of Mankeli, active since 1997. The cadres cited disillusionment with the ideology, internal conflict within the organisation, and aspiration for a peaceful family life as key reasons for leaving the insurgency. Many also acknowledged that rapid infrastructure development, improved healthcare, education, and electricity access in remote villages influenced their decision.

August - 9, 2025
On August 9, Special Judge National Investigation Agency (NIA) Sandeep Gandotra rejected the bail application of Abdul Rouf Badan, a Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) handler, in a high-profile narcotics and terror funding case, reports Daily Excelsior on August 10. Abdul Rouf Badan, who was arrested in August 2022 after remaining absconding for over two years, is facing multiple charges under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA) and the Indian Penal Code (IPC). The court observed that his alleged role includes acting as a courier for smuggling heroin and arms from across the Line of Control (LoC) and collecting funds used for terrorist activities in Jammu and Kashmir. The court, while dismissing the application, cited the gravity of the offences, the ongoing investigation, and the sensitive nature of the evidence, including mobile communications, financial transactions, and witness testimonies. It was noted that 30 material witnesses against the accused are yet to be examined, and granting bail at this stage could jeopardize the prosecution’s case. Agreeing with the Special Public Prosecutor K S Pathania, the court emphasized that the delay in recording witness statements was largely due to the accused being on the run and directed the prosecution to expedite examination of all relevant witnesses. It also clarified that the decision does not affect the merits of the main case.

August - 9, 2025
On August 9, the Haryana Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee (HSGMC) has unanimously opposed the state government’s proposed amendments to the Haryana Sikh Gurdwara Management Act, 2014, accusing the Cabinet of bypassing consultation with its 11-member executive body, reports The Tribune. At a General House meeting in Kurukshetra District of Haryana, attended by 32 of its 49 members, the committee passed a resolution rejecting the changes and sought a meeting with Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini. Key objections include shifting the power to remove members from the HSGMC to the Haryana Sikh Gurdwara Judicial Commission, and altering the appeal process to bypass district courts in favour of direct appeals to the Punjab and Haryana High Court. The committee plans to convene a Sikh Sammelan before the August 22 Assembly session to gather community feedback. Some prominent members were absent but had earlier voiced opposition to the amendments.

August - 10, 2025
Personnel of the 209th Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (COBRA) Battalion destroyed three Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) bunkers during an intensive anti-insurgency operation in the dense Saranda Forest along the Odisha–Jharkhand border in the Chaibasa area in West Singhbhum District of Jharkhand, reports Deccan Chronicle on August 10. The seizure, officials said, points to the bunkers’ role in sustaining insurgent activities in the area.

At United Nations Security Council (UNSC) debate on maritime security in New York, India reaffirmed its commitment to a free, open, and rules-based maritime order, grounded in international law and guided by the principles of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), reports TheHansIndia.com on August 12. August - 12, 2025
On August 12, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) Special Court in Patna, Bihar, filed a supplementary chargesheet against four individuals — Nazar Saddam, Waris, Zakir Hushain, and Muzaffar Ahmad Wani alias Sarfaraz — in connection with the 2024 Champaran fake currency case, reports Daijiworld.com. The accused are suspected to be linked to a transnational racket that smuggled counterfeit currency from Pakistan via Nepal into India. All four have been booked under provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) for their alleged role in smuggling and circulating Fake Indian Currency Notes (FICN). The NIA investigation revealed that the racket was part of a well-organised cross-border syndicate, with counterfeit notes sourced from Pakistan-based operatives and routed into India through Nepali intermediaries. Cryptocurrency transactions were allegedly used to facilitate payments and evade detection. The case originated from the seizure of FICN worth INR 1,95,000 in Champaran District of Bihar in 2024. Local police initially filed charges in October that year before the NIA took over the probe in December 2024, citing national security concerns. According to investigators, Nazar Saddam, Waris, and Zakir Hushain were directly involved in smuggling the fake currency from Nepal into India, while Wani allegedly acted as the financier, arranging logistical support and managing inland circulation. The case, registered as RC-17/2024/NIA-DLI.

August - 12, 2025
The Gram Panchayat (village-level local self-Government institution) of Yechali village in the Bhamragarh taluka (revenue division) in the Gadchiroli District of Maharashtra passed a resolution last month declaring a ‘gaonbandi’, a complete ban on the entry and support of Naxals [Left Wing Extremists, LWEs], reports The Indian Express on August 12. A letter to this effect was formally handed over to officials at the Mannerajaram Police Station on August 7 during a Krishi Melava (agriculture fair) in the village. The villages in Bhamragarh, including Yechali, were once known as strongholds of the Naxals, but for a few years now, several villages have been adopting a ‘gaonbandi’ (village ban). Earlier in 2024, seven tribal hamlets of Bhamragarh taluka in the foothills of Abujhmarh also banned the CPI-Maoist from entering their villages. This year too, in February, two villages in Bhamragarh declared gaonbandi against Naxals. Yechali’s Sarpanch, 38-year-old Kamala Kursam, said, “A ‘gaonbandi’ for Naxals was the need of the hour. Times have changed; it’s not like before. Earlier, Naxals would enter the village and intimidate people. But if we stand together, they won’t be able to cross the village boundaries. This will lead to our development,” said Kursam, who has been leading the village for over three years. The resolution marks a significant shift for Yechali, which once faced persistent trouble due to Naxal presence.

August - 14, 2025

The case was initially registered by the Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), Gujarat, after uncovering a conspiracy between a Juvenile in Conflict with Law (JCL) and the accused to launch multiple Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks on websites of the Government of India and various state governments between March and May 2025. The attacks were publicised online, with the accused sharing screenshots and inflammatory messages in retaliation to India’s ‘Operation Sindoor’ against Pakistan-sponsored terrorism, with the intent to threaten the country’s unity, integrity, and sovereignty. Digital forensic analysis confirmed the accused’s role in orchestrating a planned and ideologically motivated cyber offensive. The probe also revealed his efforts to train others in unlawful cyber techniques while concealing identities to evade law enforcement.

August - 14, 2025
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) Special Court, Mumbai, has convicted and sentenced three accused in the 2020 Sahar Fake Currency case, which involved smuggling high-quality counterfeit notes from Malaysia into India, reports NIA on August 14. Danish Haji Mohammed Petiwal and Sarasvati Dattaram alias Muskan have each been sentenced to five years, six months, and two days of rigorous imprisonment (RI) along with a fine of INR 6,000. J. Kaleel Rahman has been sentenced to five years, five months, and 18 days of RI and fined INR 5,000. The case originated from intelligence received by the Mumbai Customs Department regarding a parcel from Malaysia containing Fake Indian Currency Notes (FICN) worth INR 68,000 (34 notes of INR 2,000 denomination). The parcel was addressed to one Sangita Kapoor in Goregaon (West), Mumbai. On August 19, a local court awarded life imprisonment to a Hizbul Mujahideen (HM) terrorist for killing a civilian in Bandipora three decades ago in 1993, reports Kashmir News Service. Court of Additional Sessions Judge Bandipora Susheel Singh convicted HM terrorist Abdul Wahid Mir for the cold-blooded murder of carpet weaver Mohammad Shafi Hajam (32) in Onagam village of Bandipora. The killing, which took place on December 7, 1993, had been initially buried as “untraced” but was reopened after 11 years on the insistence of the victim’s family. The court sentenced Mir to life imprisonment under Section 302 RPC, three years’ rigorous imprisonment under Section 201 RPC, and seven years' rigorous imprisonment under Section 7/27 Arms Act. All sentences will run concurrently.

August - 19, 2025
Unregulated online money gaming platforms pose serious national security and economic threats, according to the draft of the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025, reports Money control on August 19. "Use of digital wallets and cryptocurrencies for money laundering and illicit fund transfers", use of platforms for "helping terror organisations", "cross-border data flows without compliance with Indian data protection laws", and "offshore entities circumventing Indian tax and legal obligations", the draft says. It further added, "Modern online games are often integrated with social media, digital wallets, and real-time multilayer networks, making them difficult to monitor or control at the state level."

August - 20, 2025
India Today reported on August 20 that Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM) is attempting to rebuild and expand its terror infrastructure, setting a target of PKR 3.91 billion to establish 313 new markaz (centres) across Pakistan. On May 7, Indian forces carried out precision strikes under Operation Sindoor, destroying nine terror launch pads in Pakistan and Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir (PoK). The strikes, conducted in retaliation for the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir that killed 26 civilians, eliminated more than 100 terrorists. In the aftermath, intelligence inputs indicate JeM is ramping up its fundraising efforts to establish new training centres for recruits and secure hideouts for its chief, Masood Azhar and his family. The group has reportedly turned to digital wallets such as EasyPaisa and SadaPay, linking accounts to mobile numbers associated with Azhar’s relatives, including his son Abdullah Azhar. JeM commanders are also collecting donations in mosques during Friday prayers. Though these contributions are publicly presented as aid for Gaza, officials believe the funds are being diverted to JeM operations. The Al Rahmat Trust, a Bahawalpur-based charity long associated with JeM, is said to be central in this drive, routing money through a dedicated account operated by Azhar and his aides. Reports suggest the fundraising campaign has already achieved significant success, with funds flowing from both Pakistan and abroad. The money is reportedly being channelled into the procurement of advanced weapons, including machine guns, rocket launchers, and mortars.

August - 20, 2025
On August 20, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) conducted searches at nine locations in Tamil Nadu and arrested one more accused in connection with the 2019 Ramalingam murder case, linked to the banned Popular Front of India (PFI), reports NIA. The arrested accused has been identified as Imthathullah, proprietor of Ambur Biryani Hotels in Kodaikanal, Tamil Nadu. He is accused of knowingly and voluntarily harbouring absconding proclaimed offenders (POs) in his hotel outlets from 2021 onwards. During the searches in Dindigul and Tenkasi Districts, the agency also seized incriminating documents and digital devices. According to NIA, of the three POs harboured by Imthathullah, two — Abdul Majeed and Shahul Hameed — were arrested on January 25. The third, Muhammad Ali Jinna, remains absconding. The case (RC-06/2019/NIA/DLI) pertains to the brutal killing of Ramalingam in February 2019, which investigators say was intended to spread fear and communal hatred. The NIA took over the probe from Tamil Nadu Police in March 2019 and filed a chargesheet against 18 accused before its special court in Poonamallee, Chennai, in August 2019. Six of them were declared absconders. In 2021, NIA arrested one of the absconders, Rahman Sadiq. In November 2024, the agency traced Abdul Majeed and Shahul Hameed to the Poombarai area of Kodaikanal in Dindigul District and also arrested a harbourer, Jinnah, who was named as the 19th accused in the case. The NIA has announced a reward of INR 5,00,000 each for information leading to the arrest of Ali Jinna, Burhanudeen, and Nafeel Hasan — all residents of Thanjavur district and former office bearers of the PFI.

August - 20, 2025
On August 20, the Press Information Bureau (PIB) released data and a summary of defence-related developments over the past 11 years, under the title Transformation of India’s Defence and Internal Security Posture, Business Standard reported. The report states that, unlike in the past, India has now emerged as a “global force to reckon with” and approaches issues from a position of strength. It highlights the government’s “firm and clear approach towards cross-border terrorism,” noting that the pattern of action over the last decade reflects this policy. According to the synopsis, the government’s goals are threefold: to ensure defence systems are researched, developed, and manufactured in India; to anticipate future warfare scenarios through predictive technologies; and to create precise, targeted systems for counter-action. By 2035, the aim is to establish a comprehensive national security shield for both strategic and civilian assets. The PIB report further states that India’s defence and internal security posture under Prime Minister Narendra Modi has undergone a “profound transformation,” marked by stronger deterrence, greater clarity of purpose, and a sustained drive for self-reliance. Defence expenditure has risen steadily, from INR 2.53 trillion (₹2.53 lakh crore) in 2013–14 to INR 6.81 trillion (₹6.81 lakh crore) in 2025–26, the report added.

August - 22, 2025
Following directions from the Ministry of External Affairs, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has instructed all banks and financial institutions to immediately freeze accounts or assets linked to five individuals named in the updated United Nations Security Council (UNSC) terror sanctions list released on August 22, reports Tribune India. The individuals, suspected of ties to Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) (Da’esh) and Al-Qaida, include Libyan militant Ibrahim Ali Abu Bakr Tantoush, Tunisian extremist Al-Azhar Ben Khalifa Ben Ahmed Rouine, Kuwaiti nationals Sulaiman Jassem Sulaiman Ali Abo Ghaith and Shafi Sultan Mohammed Al-Ajmi, and Tajik commander-turned-IS recruiter Gulmurod Khalimov. The RBI reminded regulated entities that, under Section 51A of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), 1967, they are legally obligated to block all funds and financial services of UN-designated terror-linked individuals and organisations. It also directed that any delisting requests received by banks be forwarded to the Ministry of Home Affairs. Reiterating the importance of strict compliance, the RBI stressed adherence to Know Your Customer (KYC) norms and underlined that enforcement of the UAPA order is non-negotiable.

August - 22, 2025
The High Court of Jammu and Kashmir (J&K) and Ladakh dismissed the bail plea of Syed Iftikhar Andrabi (53), of Handwara in Kupwara District, in a high-profile narco-terrorism case being investigated by the National Investigation Agency (NIA), reports Hindustan Times on August 22. A division bench comprising justices Sanjeev Kumar and Sanjay Parihar upheld the order of the Special NIA Court, Jammu, which had earlier rejected Andrabi’s bail application in connection with the case registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA) and the Indian Penal Code (IPC). The appellant was represented by advocate Warisha Farasat and her team. She contended that Andrabi, a political activist, had been falsely implicated after his release from preventive detention in 2019 and has already undergone nearly five years in custody. The defence argued that there was no direct evidence against him and sought parity with co-accused who were granted bail. The NIA opposed the bail plea, asserting that Andrabi had direct links with Pakistan-based handlers of Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and Hizbul Mujahideen (HM) and was part of a cross-border syndicate engaged in drug trafficking and terror financing. The division bench observed that on the disclosure of the appellant, 3.2 kilograms of heroin and cash amounting to more than INR 3.5 million were recovered. “His mobile phone data suggested his communication with operatives across the border,” observed the division bench. While acknowledging that Andrabi had spent almost five years in custody, the court held that the seriousness of the charges and evidence on record outweighed his plea for bail.

August - 23, 2025
On August 23, 2025, the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) conducted the maiden flight test of the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS) off the coast of Odisha, reports India Today. The IADWS is a fully indigenous, multi-layered air defence system comprising Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missiles (QRSAM), Advanced Very Short-Range Air Defence System (VSHORADS) missiles, and a high-power laser-based Directed Energy Weapon (DEW). Together, these technologies form the “Sudarshan Chakra” integrated air defence shield, first announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Independence Day. The multi-layered framework aims to integrate advanced surveillance, cybersecurity measures, and physical safeguards to protect citizens and critical infrastructure from enemy strikes. The successful test marks a significant breakthrough in India’s pursuit of a robust and self-reliant air defence ecosystem.

Forensic examination confirmed Langoo’s DNA on the seized pistol. CCTV footage, protected witness testimonies and call records further linked the accused to the crime.

Punjab’s Batala District Police claimed to have unearthed a Pakistan-Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI)-backed terror module operating in Punjab, allegedly in connivance with the United Kingdom (UK)-based Babbar Khalsa International (BKI), The Times of India reported on August 27. August - 27, 2025
At least four Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) cadres, including three women, were killed in an encounter near the border of Gadchiroli and Narayanpur District of Chhattisgarh, in the Koparshi Forest area in Bhamragad in Gadchiroli District of Maharashtra on August 27, reports The Print. Acting on credible information that Gatta Dalam (armed squad), Company No 10 and other Maoist formations of ‘Gadchiroli Division’ were present in the Koparshi Forest area, 19 units of C-60, an anti-Naxal commando force of Gadchiroli Police, and two units of Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF)’s Quick Action Team (QAT) were sent to the area. Maoists opened fire on seeing the Security Forces (SFs), resulting in an exchange of fire that lasted nearly eight hours. While several Maoists managed to flee into the forest, four were gunned down. The slain Maoists identified by Gadchiroli Police are Malu Pada (41), Company No. 10, rank 'People's Party Committee Member (PPCM)', carrying an INR 600,000 reward, and eight crimes were registered against him; Kranti alias Jamuna Rainu Halami (32), Company No. 10, rank party member, carrying an INR 400,000 reward, booked for 27 crimes; Jyoti Kunjam (27), Aheri Local Organisation Squad (LOS), rank party member, carrying an INR 200,000 reward, booked for eight crimes; and Mangi Madkam (22), Gatta LOS, rank party member, carrying an INR 200,000 reward and booked for three crimes. From the encounter site, SFs seized four firearms, one Self-Loading Rifle (SLR), two INSAS (Indian Small Arms System) assault rifles, and one .303 rifle, along with 92 live rounds, three walkie-talkies, Maoist literature, and daily-use items.

August - 27, 2025
Continuing the war against drugs “Yudh Nashian Virudh” waged to eradicate drug menace from State consecutively for the 179th day, Punjab Police conducted raids at 333 locations on August 27 leading to the arrest of 99 drug smugglers after registration of 68 first information reports (FIRs) across the State, reports Patiala Politics. With this, the number of total drug smugglers arrested has reached to 27,409 in 179 days. The raids have resulted in recovery of 985 grams heroin, 21 kilograms poppy husk, 1625 intoxicant tablets/capsules and INR 9850 drug money from the possession of arrested drug smugglers. The operation was conducted on the directions of Director General of Police (DGP) Punjab Gaurav Yadav simultaneously in all 28 Police Districts of the State. Divulging details, Special DGP Law and Order Arpit Shukla informed that over 100 Police teams, comprising over 900 Police personnel, under the supervision of 64 gazetted officers have conducted raids across the state. Police teams have also checked as many as 364 suspicious persons during the day-long operation, he added.

August - 27, 2025
In a renewed attempt to destabilize India from within, Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) is pushing Babbar Khalsa International (BKI) to escalate its terror operations in Punjab and nearby States, Daijiworld reported on August 27 quoting Intelligence sources. Intelligence and law enforcement agencies believe this is a strategic move aimed at reviving the Khalistan movement by directly targeting the Indian establishment. Police sources in Punjab have noted a disturbing rise in BKI-related terror module busts in recent months. Unlike earlier attacks which often resulted in civilian casualties, the group's latest strategy is more focused: targeting Police stations, Intelligence Bureau offices, Government buildings, and courts. According to security analysts, this shift in tactics is meant to send a clear message — that BKI’s fight is not against the public, but against the Indian State, which they accuse of preventing the creation of a separate Khalistan nation. By avoiding civilian harm, BKI is attempting to gain public sympathy and recruit support, particularly among disaffected youth.

Pakistan-based Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) is facilitating Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM) from traditional weapons—such as assault rifles, mortars, and rocket launchers—to advanced tools like quadcopters, drones, and digital warfare systems, reports swarajyamag.com on August 27. August - 28, 2025
Terrorists chose the Baisaran meadow as the target for the terror attack in Pahalgam in Jammu and Kashmir (J&K) due to its high tourist presence and relative isolation, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) revealed on August 28, reports Daily Excelsior. “Three terrorists” were directly involved in the brutal terror attack in which 26 people were killed in cold blood on April 22, NIA officials said. The target was also chosen considering the “response time” from the security agencies, said a spokesman for the NIA, which is probing the case. The terrorists chose Baisaran as the target due to its “high tourist presence” and “relative isolation”, and after considering that the “response (from the security agencies) would take time”, he said. In the targeted attack, terrorists killed male tourists milling around eateries, taking pony rides or just picnicking with their families, including young children and parents, in the meadow near Pahalgam. The NIA in June arrested two men for harbouring the three Pakistan-based terrorists, who were killed by the armed forces late last month. The arrested duo, Parvaiz Ahmad Jothar from Batkote and Bashir Ahmad Jothar from Pahalgam, disclosed the identities of the three assailants as Pakistani nationals affiliated to the proscribed outfit Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT).

August - 29, 2025
An intelligence report has revealed that Sambhal town in Uttar Pradesh (UP) has repeatedly figured in India’s counter-terror investigations, with agencies describing it as a recruitment ground for global extremist groups, reports India Today on Aug 29. Once considered the nerve centre of Al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS), the town produced its first chief, Maulana Asim Umar, who was killed in a US drone strike in 2019. Over the years, several men from Sambhal have been linked to Al-Qaeda, Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIS), Hizbul Mujahideen (HM), and the banned Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI)—some arrested, others acquitted, and a few still missing. More recently, Sambhal has figured in probes into the ISIS-backed Pune module, with operatives arrested or surrendering in 2024. Compiled by the Sambhal Police LIU with inputs from national security agencies, the report describes the town as once functioning like a “campus recruitment hub” for extremist groups, making it a continued point of watch for intelligence agencies.

September - 2, 2025
Punjab Police’s intensive anti-drug campaign, ‘Yudh Nashian Virudh’, has completed six months with significant breakthroughs in the State’s battle against narcotics, Kalinga TV reported on September 2. Since March 1, Police have registered 17,957 FIRs and arrested 27,796 drug smugglers, leading to the recovery of 1,129 kilograms of heroin along with other contraband. The drive launched to make Punjab a drug-free State. The campaign is being closely monitored by a five-member Cabinet Sub-Committee, led by Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema, while day-to-day operations are supervised by the Director General of Police (DGP) Punjab, Gaurav Yadav. Special Director General of Police (Law and Order) Arpit Shukla, who has been personally overseeing the operations, said the crackdown has also led to the seizure of 384 kilograms of opium, 232 quintals of poppy husk, 29 kg of charas, 430 kilograms ganja, 6.3 kilograms ICE (crystal meth), 33 lakh intoxicant pills/tablets, and INR 12.44 crore in drug money. On the 184th day of the campaign alone, Police arrested 58 drug smugglers and recovered 8.4 kilograms of heroin, 4,087 intoxicant pills, and INR 2,300 in drug proceeds. Over 120 Police teams, comprising more than 1,000 personnel and supervised by 67 gazetted officers, carried out raids at 309 locations. These operations resulted in 43 fresh FIRs, while 337 suspicious individuals were also checked.

September - 3, 2025
On September 3, the Border Security Force (BSF) recovered fake Indian currency notes (FICN) worth INR 1,99,500 in INR 500 denomination from the India-Bangladesh border in Sovapur, Kaliachak, Malda District of West Bengal, reports ianslive.in. According to officials, troops of the 71st Battalion BSF received intelligence about an attempt to smuggle counterfeit notes through their area. Around 1 p.m., jawans spotted suspicious movement on the Bangladesh side of the border fence. During a search, they seized a packet containing 399 fake currency notes of INR 500 denomination, allegedly thrown across the fence by Bangladeshi smugglers to be collected by their Indian counterparts. A senior BSF official said such high-quality fake notes are often printed in Pakistan and other countries before being smuggled into India via the India-Bangladesh border, with nearly 70 per cent of such seizures reported from Kaliachak. Investigators revealed that Indian smugglers purchase these counterfeit notes at INR 200 apiece and sell them for INR 300, hidden in bundles of genuine currency for distribution in the market.

September - 3, 2025
On September 3, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (UMHA) and Manipur Government, signed a renewed Suspension of Operations (SoO) agreement with Kuki-Zo insurgent groups, introducing re-negotiated ground rules, reports The Hindu. The pact, effective for a year, reiterates Manipur’s territorial integrity, mandates relocation of designated camps, verification of cadres, deportation of foreign nationals, and stricter monitoring by a Joint Group. Insurgent groups agreed to shift seven camps away from conflict zones and deposit weapons with CRPF/BSF camps. The agreement comes ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s September 13, scheduled visit to Manipur—his first since ethnic clashes erupted between the Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities in May 2023. The Kuki-Zo Council also committed to facilitate free movement on National Highway-2, a vital lifeline to Nagaland and Assam, though it stressed security is the Centre’s responsibility. This is the first revision since the SoO was signed in 2008, reflecting changing demands post-violence.

September - 3, 2025
The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has announced that foreigners may be refused entry into or stay in India if convicted of offences such as anti-national activities, espionage, rape, murder, terrorist acts, child trafficking, or membership in a banned organisation, reports Assam Tribune on September 3. The order specifies that individuals of Afghan, Chinese, or Pakistani origin will not be permitted to visit protected or restricted areas. These include the entire states of Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, and Sikkim, as well as parts of Jammu & Kashmir, Uttarakhand, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, and Rajasthan, among others. Issued under the newly introduced Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, the directive requires every state government and Union Territory administration to establish dedicated holding centres or detention camps to restrict the movement of foreigners pending deportation. The MHA further directed that all foreigners applying for any category of visa, including registration as an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder, must provide biometric information before approval. Illegal immigrants apprehended within India will also face restrictions on movement in designated holding centres until deportation. According to the order, foreigners may be denied entry or stay in India if convicted of crimes such as crimes against humanity, terrorist or subversive activities (including financing, money laundering, or hawala), trafficking in narcotics or psychotropic substances, human or child trafficking, racketeering in fake travel documents or currency (including cryptocurrency), cybercrime, or child abuse. The Bureau of Immigration will maintain an updated list of foreigners prohibited from entering India.

September - 3, 2025
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) traced 463 phone calls linked to anti-India elements, uncovering financial networks of the Resistance Front (TRF) tied to Pakistan, Malaysia, and Gulf countries, reports NDTV on September 3. TRF, a proxy of Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT), was found to have received about INR 9,00,000 through Malaysia resident Yasir Hayat, with further links to LeT’s most wanted terrorist, Sajid Mir. Evidence gathered from mobile data, chats, bank transactions, and call records, along with documents seized during raids in Srinagar District and Handwara District, has strengthened India’s case against Pakistan before the Financial Action Task Force (FATF). Officials believe this evidence could push Islamabad back onto the FATF grey list, from which it was removed in 2022 after four years of scrutiny.

September - 4, 2025
A Special National Investigation Agency (NIA) Court in Chennai has sentenced Noorudeen (39) to rigorous imprisonment of five years on three counts (to run concurrently) and fined INR 1,000 for trafficking Fake Indian Currency Notes (FICN) linked to Chennai’s counterfeit racket, part of an international conspiracy orchestrated by a serving Pakistan Navy officer, reports Times of India on September 4. The wider plot involved Sri Lankan national Sakir Hussaien and Amir Zubair Siddiqui, then counsellor at the Pakistan High Commission in Colombo, Srilanka. Intelligence inputs from the US and Malaysia confirmed that phone numbers used by Siddiqui were registered with Pakistan Naval Headquarters in Islamabad, establishing that he was Director of Counter Intelligence, Pakistan Navy, and not merely a diplomat. According to the judgment, Siddiqui instructed operatives to conduct reconnaissance of the US Consulate in Chennai, Kalpakkam Atomic Power Plant, and Bengaluru’s Electronic City, while also channelling funds through counterfeit currency networks. Investigators recovered emails in which code words such as “Wedding Project” (bomb planting), “Wedding Hall” (the Consulate), and “Spice contents” (explosives) were used. In Chennai, Noorudeen acted as the main conduit. Suppliers from West Bengal delivered INR 6,50,000 in fake notes to him, of which he passed on INR 2,75,000 to two men in T Nagar in Chennai on May 1, 2014. The funding trail revealed deposits made through Axis Bank, with three original pay-in slips seized and sent for forensic examination. Experts confirmed the handwriting matched that of Saleem, one of the men arrested in T Nagar, proving that he deposited money under Noorudeen’s instructions to procure counterfeit notes from Malda.

September - 4, 2025
Intelligence reports suggest that the Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP) and Al Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS) are coordinating to launch attacks on India using bases in Bangladesh, Pakistan, and Afghanistan, reports ommcomnews.com on September 4. Despite past rivalry, the two groups have agreed to divide their areas of influence—ISKP focusing on South India and AQIS on North and Northeast India, where it has a stronger support base from Bangladesh. The deal was reportedly brokered by Pakistan’s ISI, which aims to prevent clashes between the outfits while keeping their shared anti-India agenda intact. AQIS, aligned with the Taliban, has been recruiting in Bangladesh and India, even running the magazine Nawa-i-Ghazwa Hind to spread propaganda. ISKP, meanwhile, exploited the banned Popular Front of India (PFI) network in South India, with the PFI earlier radicalising and sending recruits to Afghanistan. Security agencies warn that with the PFI underground, ISKP may attempt to fill the void. While both groups target India, the ISI has ensured they do not operate in Jammu and Kashmir to avoid friction with Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM) and Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT).

September - 4, 2025
Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) has activated modules in Gulf nations and Canada to sabotage India’s economy, reports Zee News on September 4. Indian agencies have tightened surveillance on ISI and its proxies, including Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT) and Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM). In Canada, ISI relies on Khalistani elements, not only for violent acts but also to manage finances routed into India. The agency has instructed operatives to identify major marketplaces in Delhi, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, and Bengaluru and set them on fire, while making the incidents appear accidental. Similar plans target railway operations, with derailments and onboard fires intended to cause disruption and financial loss without being traced back to Pakistan. Investigations also revealed ISI’s role in illegally routing Pakistani goods such as rock salt, spices, and dry fruits into India via Dubai. Goods are re-labelled to bypass restrictions, with United Arab Emirates (UAE) based front companies facilitating the trade. A recent DRI seizure of dry dates worth INR 90 million traced back to Khairpur District in Sindh, Pakistan, exposed the network. Since setting up this underground economy, the ISI is estimated to have earned nearly INR 5000 million, channelled into anti-India activities.

September - 5, 2025
On September 5, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) arrested a key wanted terror accused, identified as Sharanjit Kumar alias Sunny, from Gaya ji District in Bihar, in connection with the March 2025 Amritsar temple grenade attack case in Amritsar District of Punjab, reports NIA. Sharanjit, a resident of Bhaini Bangar village in Qadian, Batala, Gurdaspur District of Punjab, had been absconding from Batala. Gursidak and Vishaal were also involved in procuring and supplying multiple consignments of grenades as well as arms and ammunition. Investigations found that on March 1, 2025, Sharanjit received a consignment of four grenades from another arrested accused in Batala. He subsequently handed over one grenade to Gursidak and Vishaal just two days before the attack. The case is being investigated under RC-08/2025/NIA/DLI, and further inquiries are ongoing.

September - 9, 2025
The Delhi High (HC) Court dismissed a plea filed by Nasir Mohd Sodozey alias Aftaab Ahmed, serving a life sentence for his role in a terror conspiracy involving the 1994 kidnapping of four foreign nationals to pressure the Indian government into releasing jailed militants, reports Times of India on September 9. Sodozey challenged the Sentence Review Board’s June 30, 2023, order rejecting his application for early release, citing over 26 years of incarceration. A close aide of Ahmed Omar Saeed Sheikh—released in 1999 during the IC-814 hijacking swap—Sodozey was convicted in 2002 under the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act (TADA), the Indian Penal Code (IPC), and the Foreigners Act for acting under the banner of the banned terror outfit Harkat-ul-Ansar (HuA). Initially sentenced to death, his punishment was commuted to life imprisonment by the Supreme Court in 2003. While dismissing the plea, the court observed: “The petitioner, in concert with his co-conspirators, abducted and held captive four foreign nationals, not for private gain or personal animosity, but with the intent of compelling the sovereign Government of India to yield to demands of a militant organisation. Such conduct is not merely an ordinary crime but an attack upon the very fabric of civil order... placing it in a category of exceptional gravity.” The convict had argued that under Delhi’s 2004 remission policy, the maximum prescribed term of incarceration is capped at 25 years, making him eligible for release after completing over two decades in jail.

September - 9, 2025
The Financial Action Task Force (FATF), in its latest report, praised the Union Home Ministry’s online Mutual Legal Assistance (MLA) portal for streamlining international cooperation in money laundering cases, reports Times of India on September 9. The report cited an Enforcement Directorate (ED) probe, conducted jointly with the US Department of Justice (DOJ), into a darknet-based Fentanyl syndicate as a “best practices” case. The 2022 investigation revealed that two brothers controlled over 8,500 bitcoins worth $150 million, used for laundering drug proceeds. Responding to a US request, ED launched a parallel probe, seizing 268.2 bitcoins (INR 1,300 million) and attaching assets worth INR 96 million. FATF noted the case as a strong example of real-time cross-border coordination, supported by US officials in India. The report also appreciated India’s standardised MLA guidelines, saying the portal has reduced delays and improved efficiency in handling international requests.

September - 15, 2025
On September 15, the Supreme Court declined a plea by the kin of slain Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) leader Nambala Keshav Rao alias Basavaraju, over the handing over of his body for performing final rites, reports ETV Bharat. In May, Rao along with 26 others, was killed in a fierce encounter with Security Forces (SFs) in the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh. The matter came up for hearing before a bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta. The bench was hearing the plea by two family members of Rao challenging a May 29 Andhra Pradesh High Court order, which rejected their plea seeking contempt action against authorities for allegedly violating its May 24 order. A counsel, representing the kin of Basavaraju, contended before the apex court that on May 24, the advocate general of Chhattisgarh had made a statement before the high court that the post-mortem of the bodies would be completed during the day. The counsel stressed that it was contended before the high court that after the completion of the autopsy, bodies would be handed over to the relatives. The counsel said the bodies of those who were from Chhattisgarh were handed over to their relatives, but the kin of Basavaraju, who were from Andhra Pradesh, were not given the body. The counsel stressed that even the ashes of the deceased have not been returned. The counsel submitted that he is not pressing on contempt; rather, he is urging the court to entertain this matter and lay down some guidelines. The bench orally observed that many times, the family members don't even come forward to claim the dead body. The counsel kin of Basavaraju had gone to the authorities the same day to take the body. The bench said it is an issue to be decided in appropriate proceedings, not in this contempt, and told the counsel that he should avail himself of other remedies instead of this contempt petition. Declining to entertain the plea, the bench said it is open for the petitioner to avail such other remedy as may be available under law before an appropriate forum.

September - 15, 2025

Addressing the second National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) chiefs in New Delhi, Shah highlighted that drug seizures rose from 26,00,000 kg (worth INR 400 million) between 2004 and 2013 to 10 million kg (INR 1.65 trillion) between 2014 and 2025, while arrests jumped from 1,73,000 to 7,61,000 in the same periods. September - 16, 2025
On September 16, the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) reported that 660 foreign nationals were arrested across India on drug trafficking charges last year, with Nepalese (203), Nigerians (106), and Myanmarese (25) topping the list, reports the Indian Express. The data also shows arrests of 18 Bangladeshi nationals, 14 from the Ivory Coast, 13 from Ghana, West Africa, and 10 from Iceland in connection with drug-related crimes. The report highlights the growing use of drones in trafficking, with 163 cases recorded in Punjab, leading to the seizure of 187.149 kilograms (kgs) of heroin, 5.39 kg methamphetamine, and 4.22 kg opium. In Rajasthan, 15 drone-related cases were reported with 39.155 kg heroin recovered, while in Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), one case was reported with 0.344 kg heroin seized. “India faces a growing challenge in combating narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances trafficking due to its geographic location between the ‘Death Crescent’ (Afghanistan, Pakistan, Iran) and the ‘Death Triangle’ (Myanmar, Thailand, Laos) – two major global drug-producing regions,” NCB Director General Anurag Garg said in the annual report. He noted that while Punjab, Rajasthan, and J&K remain vulnerable to heroin smuggling from Pakistan, the north-eastern states — Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Assam, and Arunachal Pradesh — are affected by their proximity to Myanmar. Coastal routes in Mumbai, Gujarat, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu are also increasingly being exploited for smuggling synthetic drugs and precursors, he added.

The Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) has offered a temporary ceasefire, hinting at a likely breakthrough in the Centre’s efforts to end Naxalism by 2026, reports Moneycontrol News on September 17. The statement, issued by Maoist leader ‘spokesperson’ of the CPI-Maoist Mallojula Venugopal Rao alias Abhay, is dated August 15 and has been released to local journalists in Chhattisgarh. “We have decided to unconditionally lay down arms,” the CPI(Maoist) writes in the letter, adding that the move was in response to “appeals made by the prime minister, home minister, and senior police officers.” The statement also referred to changing national and international circumstances as influencing their decision. “We have decided to declare a temporary ceasefire, but we will continue to raise issues of public importance and engage with political parties and organisations,” it noted. It mentioned the group’s intention to continue advocacy through political and civil channels even while suspending armed activities. “We are also willing to engage with government representatives via video call,” the statement added. The press note included Abhay’s latest photograph, which sources said was meant to establish authenticity and build confidence with authorities should video calls be used to hold discussions. Inspector General of Police (IGP) for Bastar Range, Sundarraj P, remarked, “We have taken note of a press release issued in the name of the CPI(Maoist) central committee regarding the laying down of arms and the prospect of peace talks. The authenticity of this release is being verified, and its contents are under careful examination." "Any decision on engagement or dialogue with the CPI(Maoist) lies solely with the government, which will take an appropriate call after due consideration and assessment of the situation and circumstances," he further added.

September - 18, 2025
Five C-60 commando teams and a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) battalion cordoned off a guerrilla hideout in the dense Modaske jungles in Etapalli tehsil (revenue unit) in the Gadchiroli District of Maharashtra on September 18 and shot dead two wanted women cadres of the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist), who carried a bounty of INR 1.4 million, reports The Times of India. Following a credible tip-off on a sabotage plot by Maoists, C-60 commando teams from Pranhita headquarters, bolstered by the Gatta (Jambiya) Police post and CRPF's 191 battalion, swiftly sealed the jungle perimeter with commandos, who were on physical training at base camp, donning their gear and rushing out to save precious response time. As commandos combed the jungles, Maoists fired bullets from a vantage point. Security Forces (SFs) retaliated, forcing guerrillas to scatter into the forest. The operation continued for at least eight hours, and when the gunfire receded, the bodies of two elite woman Maoists, identified as Sumitra alias Sunita Veladi (38) and Lalita alias Laddo alias Sandhya Korsa (34), were recovered along with an AK-47 rifle, a pistol, 37 live rounds, two walkie-talkies and sundry insurgent gear. Sumitra, from Madvei village of Aheri tehsil, the Gatta Local Organisational Squad (LOS) ‘commander’, was involved with 14 encounters and 12 murders, including the killing of a top C-60 commando, Mahesh Nagulkar. While Lalita, hailing from Neltola in Chhattisgarh's Kanker District, was a People's Liberation Guerrilla Army (PLGA) ‘assistant commander’ with eight encounters, four murders, one arson, and one additional case against her.

September - 18, 2025
The maiden bilateral maritime exercise between the Indian Navy and the Hellenic Navy of Greece concluded on 18 September 2025 in the Mediterranean Sea, PIB reported on September 20. The exercise was held in two phases: a harbour phase at Salamis Naval Base from September 13 to 17, and a sea phase on September 17–18. The Indian Navy was represented by the guided missile stealth frigate INS Trikand. Key activities included cross-deck visits, professional interactions, and a pre-sail conference onboard HS Themistokles, an Elli-class frigate of the Hellenic Navy. The sea phase featured complex manoeuvres, including night Visit, Board, Search and Seizure (VBSS) operations, replenishment-at-sea, anti-submarine warfare, coordinated gun firing, and cross-deck helicopter operations, all of which enhanced interoperability between the two navies. The exercise underscored the growing convergence between India and Greece on maritime security and their shared commitment to ensuring safety, stability, and freedom of navigation. Following its conclusion, INS Trikand proceeded to the next phase of her Mediterranean deployment.

September - 19, 2025
Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) presence continues to remain a challenge in Odisha’s Kandhamal District, with reports confirming that insurgents are active in eight out of the district’s 12 blocks, reports Odisha TV on September 19. The affected areas include Phiringia, Khajuripada, Chakapada, Raikia, Baliguda, Tumudibandh, Kotagarh, and Daringbadi, where Maoist movements and camps have been detected deep inside the forests. Officials and security sources indicate that cadres of the CPI-Maoist’s ‘Bansadhara–Ghumusar–Nagavali (BGN) Division’, as well as the ‘Kalahandi–Kandhamal–Boudh–Nayagarh (KKBN) Division’ are currently operating in the region. Their strongholds stretch across a vast forest corridor beginning from Rampur in Kalahandi through Belghar, Barakhama, Sadingia, Gochhapada, and Balandapada in Kandhamal, extending to Kantamal in Boudh and further up to the Padmapur forests along the Bolangir border. Another corridor runs from the Gajapati–Kandhamal boundary at Katingia through Ranaba and Indragarh in Raikia, reaching Gasamatha in Chakapada, and further into Banigocha, Badala, and Adnigada forests leading into Boudh District. Reports suggest that, particularly, the ‘KKBN Division’ Maoists are highly active, with eight to 10 armed groups operating simultaneously in different jungle areas. Local intellectuals point out that Maoist disturbances have stalled or delayed several developmental initiatives in Kandhamal.

On September 20, Chhattisgarh Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Sharma said the government was willing to positively consider the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) offer to lay down arms and start peace negotiations, but the outfit must immediately stop civilian killings and remove Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs) it had planted across its areas of influence, reports The Times of India. “The CPI(Maoist) letter issued by its spokesperson Abhay was written on Aug 15 but issued a month later. But even after Aug 15, there have been killings of two shikshadoots (temporary, visiting teachers), on Aug 27 in Bijapur and on Aug 29 in Sukma. On Sept 2, two more civilians were killed by Maoists in Sukma,” he said. Inspector General of Police (IGP), Bastar Range, P Sunderraj added that it would take Maoists no more than a week to deactivate the IEDs—laid across ‘core areas’ in the Dandakaranya region and on the Bihar-Jharkhand border—if such a directive was issued by the top leadership. The Chhattisgarh deputy CM said the final call on CPI-Maoist’s peace offer will be taken by the top political leadership, comprising the prime minister and home minister, after careful consideration and due consultation with all the stakeholders. “We are ready to welcome Maoists with open arms if they choose to come forward, including starting with a video call, and lay down arms; we will ensure their rehabilitation and reintegration into the mainstream,” said Deputy Chief Minister Sharma.

September - 20, 2025
Union Home Minister (UHM) Amit Shah has directed the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to work with the Intelligence Bureau (IB) and National Investigation Agency (NIA) to draft a standard operating procedure (SOP) for preparing dossiers on fugitives involved in terror, narcotics, and arms smuggling, reports the Indian Express on September 20. The directions came at the National Security Strategies Conference-2025 in New Delhi. Shah suggested workshops with central agencies, state police, and legal experts to fast-track extradition and deportation. He said dossiers should be prepared within a month, with dedicated teams assigned for the task. Since 2020, the CBI has brought back 137 fugitives—nearly double the number repatriated in the previous decade. To speed up Red Notices, the CBI launched the Bharatpol portal in January, enhancing international police collaboration. At a separate anti-narcotics conference, Shah stressed that those running drug trades from abroad must be brought under Indian law, urging a “liberal approach” to deportation alongside extradition.

In the September 8 meeting, the NCST directed Valasa, the petitioner, to share its survey data with the Chhattisgarh government and asked the latter to "recheck" the numbers. The Commission also advised Chhattisgarh to frame a "detailed strategy" for the return of displaced tribal people affected by "violence between Maoist guerrillas and Indian security forces". Security Forces (SFs) dismantled a Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) ordnance factory designed to manufacture weapons and explosives targeting security personnel on a forested hill near Koimenta village in Sukma District in the Bastar division of Chhattisgarh on September 27, reports Ommcom News. The SFs seized a vertical milling machine, two BGL (barrel grenade launcher) units, 12 empty BGL shells, 94 BGL heads, a hand grinder machine, six wooden rifle butts, trigger mechanisms for muzzle-loaders and pistols, solar batteries, a borewell drilling bit, three directional Improvised Explosive Device (IED) pipes, 80 steel pipe pieces for BGL, and a large quantity of gas cutter heads, moulding pots, iron cutter wheels, and iron scrap. Acting on intelligence inputs, a joint team of the Sukma District Force and the elite 203rd battalion of the Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (CoBRA) launched the operation from the nearby Metaguda camp, and all security personnel returned safely after completing the search.

September - 27, 2025
Security Forces (SFs) recovered a substantial cache of explosives, Naxalite literature, and combat equipment from the dense Kodliar Michingpara Forest in the Abujhmad region under the jurisdiction of Kohkameta Police Station in Narayanpur District in the Bastar division of Chhattisgarh on September 27, reports Telangana Today. The de-mining and search operation was carried out by the District Force, the “B” Company of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) 53rd Battalion, and the District Bomb Disposal Squad (BDS) deployed in Kutul who meticulously combed the forest terrain, suspecting the presence of Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs). The search yielded a large quantity of explosive material, lithium batteries, wires, booby trap switches, Biokeng walkie charger adapters, Naxalite uniforms and belts, and combat gear, including slings, pouches, and bags. Naxalite propaganda literature was also seized, indicating the ideological footprint of the Kutul Area Committee, whose active presence is suspected in the region, the officials said.

September - 28, 2025
On September 28, Union Home Minister (UHM) Amit Shah asserted that the union government will meet its target of eradicating Naxal terrorism by March 2026 and said there will be no ceasefire, but those who want to lay down arms will be given a chance to rehabilitate and rebuild their lives, reports Hindustan Times. “...There will be no ceasefire. If you want to surrender, there’s no need for a ceasefire. Lay down your weapons. The police won’t fire a single bullet,” he said. Rebutting the argument that Naxal violence stemmed from lack of development, he said those who support that narrative should question why schools and healthcare facilities were prevented in the red area. “LWE did not start because of development. Development was halted because of left-wing extremism,” he said. Shah said the government’s response to the terrorism led to 17 members of the ‘central committee (CC)’ being killed. “Targeted operations were carried out. Forensic investigation, location tracking and mobile service tracking, scientific cell log analysis and social media analysis were used to track down their hidden supporters… After 2019, the thrust was on empowering states,” he said. He went on to say, “I have no hesitation in using ruthless strategies. In Chhattisgarh there is a good policy… a red carpet for those surrendering. We don’t want to kill anyone, but it is my dharma to save innocent people and kill those who attack them.”
