September - 29, 2025
On September 29, Canada designated the Lawrence Bishnoi Gang — led by jailed Indian gangster Lawrence Bishnoi — as a terrorist entity, citing its targeting of diaspora communities, including pro-Khalistan elements, reports Business Standard. “The Bishnoi Gang is a transnational criminal organization operating primarily out of India. They have a presence in Canada and are active in areas with significant diaspora communities,” said a Canadian government release. It stated that the gang is involved in murders, shootings, arson, extortion and intimidation, creating insecurity by targeting individuals, businesses and cultural figures within diaspora communities. Delhi has rejected accusations of using the Bishnoi network against Sikh separatists, calling such claims “baseless,” while renewing demands for Canada to act on pending extradition requests against its members. Lawrence Bishnoi, a former Punjab student leader now lodged in Sabarmati Central Jail in Gujarat, has been accused in several high-profile cases, including the killing of singer Sidhu Moosewala and issuing threats to Bollywood actor Salman Khan. The gang’s name also surfaced after the 2023 killing of Sikh separatist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Canada, which heightened diplomatic tensions. In 2024, it reportedly claimed responsibility for shootings outside the homes of Punjabi artists AP Dhillon and Gippy Grewal. Key figures in the network include Bishnoi’s brother Anmol Bishnoi, Goldy Brar and Rohit Godara, though reports suggest recent factional rifts. Calls for stronger action against the gang have come from Canada’s Conservative leaders and sections of the Sikh diaspora.

September - 29, 2025
On September 29, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) Special Court in Ernakulam, Kerala, sentenced Mohammed Azarudeen H, the mastermind of the ISIS Tamil Nadu module, and Shiek Hidayathullah Y of Coimbatore, to eight years’ imprisonment in the Kerala-Tamil Nadu ISIS case, reports The New Indian Express. The court awarded eight years’ imprisonment for each offence, but ordered the sentences to run concurrently. The counsel for the accused stated that they would appeal to the High Court. According to the NIA, the two men were active members of the proscribed terrorist group ISIS/Daesh since 2017 and conspired to further its activities by forming a module with three others. They held secret classes in Coimbatore to spread the group’s violent extremist ideology and recruited vulnerable youth in Tamil Nadu and Kerala, both online and in person. Investigations revealed that Azarudeen, associated with Wahadath-e-Islami, a frontal organisation of Jamaat-e-Islami Hind, had delivered religious speeches at various locations, including Coimbatore’s Rayan Mosque, since 2013. He was also in contact with Sri Lankan nationals via Facebook and encrypted platforms, where they exchanged jihadi propaganda. Forensic analysis of their digital devices recovered speeches and materials of Sri Lankan ISIS leader Zahran Hashim, along with content from radical preachers such as Anwar al-Awlaki, Abu Bara, Moosa Cerantonio, and others. The NIA stated that both men became radicalised through extreme Salafi content online from 2016 onwards.

September - 29, 2025
On September 29, UK-based Babbar Khalsa International (BKI) operative Paramjit Singh Pamma, a close aide of Khalistani activist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, vandalised the statue of Mahatma Gandhi at Tavistock Square in London, reports News18.com. Intelligence sources described the act as a psychological warfare tactic aimed at instilling fear, provoking outrage, and asserting separatist relevance at a symbolic site. They said Khalistani leaders like Pannun and Pamma operate from safe havens abroad, outsourcing execution to radicalised youth and criminal gangs. The strategy, they noted, is part of an Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI)-backed proxy war designed to destabilise India through communal polarisation, gangster-terror networks, and targeted attacks. This is not the first incident involving Khalistani groups in London. Earlier this year, pro-Khalistan protesters disrupted External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar’s visit to the UK, drawing strong condemnation from India.

September - 30, 2025
The 9th meeting of the India-Uzbekistan Joint Working Group on Counter-Terrorism was held in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, on 30 September, reports mea.gov.in. Both sides strongly condemned the terrorist attack on innocent civilians in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, on 22 April 2025. September - 30, 2025
The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) in its 2023 report revealed that Uttar Pradesh (UP) topped the country in seizures of fake currency in lower denominations, including INR 200, INR 100, INR 50, and INR 20 notes, reports Times of India on September 30. According to the data, UP seized 6,558 fake INR 200 notes, valued at INR 13,11,000, followed by Karnataka (4,903 notes) and Rajasthan (3,593 notes). Nationally, 28,474 fake INR 200 notes worth INR 56,94,000 were recovered. In the INR 100 category, UP again led with 7,901 fake notes worth INR 790,000, ahead of Delhi (7,286) and Karnataka (4,852). Across India, a total of 35,762 fake INR 100 notes valued at INR 3,576,000 were seized. The trend extended to INR 50 notes, where UP recovered 12,068 fake notes worth INR 603,000—over four times higher than Delhi (3,027 notes) and Maharashtra (1,457). Nationwide, 18,739 fake INR 50 notes worth INR 9,36,000 were detected. Even in the rarely counterfeited INR 20 denomination, UP topped with 2,233 notes worth INR 44,660, out of a national total of 2,411 notes. While UP dominated the lower denominations, Delhi led in high-value fake currency seizures. The capital confiscated 3,609 fake INR 2,000 notes worth INR 7,218,000, compared to UP’s 440 notes worth INR 8,80,000. For INR 500 notes, Rajasthan led with 38,087 fake notes worth INR 19 million, closely followed by Assam with 37,240 notes worth INR 18.6 million. UP’s seizure stood at 6,848 notes worth INR 3,424,000. Overall, Delhi recorded the highest number of fake notes in 2023, with 45,242 notes worth INR 22.7 million. Rajasthan followed with 44,126 notes (INR 22 million), and Gujarat with 39,856 notes (INR 18.6 million). In total, 3,51,656 counterfeit notes worth INR 168.6 million were seized across India in 2023.

October - 1, 2025
Manipur recorded a staggering 14,427 violent crimes in 2023, the highest in the Northeast, marking a sharp surge from just 631 cases in 2022, according to the latest National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) report, Northeast Now reports on October 1. The state, gripped by ethnic violence between Meiteis and Kukis since May 2023, witnessed the deaths of 15 police personnel—11 killed by riotous mobs. Additionally, 24 civilians were killed by extremists, the highest such toll in the country. Six people were killed in Police lathi charge during riots. The violence has claimed over 260 lives and displaced thousands. Despite the surge in crime, only 247 cases were sent for trial in 2023, while 5,594 cases remained pending.

The special civic action programme, covering seven districts of the Bastar region, was initiated by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) at the beginning of this year with a budgetary allocation of INR 16.2 million, a senior official said. A CRPF commander based in Bijapur District said a total of 10,800 radio sets were distributed by 180 companies deployed across interior locations. The programme has aimed to link almost 54,000 individuals, considering each family to be a five-member unit, he said. “The aim of the mega radio distribution drive is to connect the locals, tribals and villagers with the mainstream of the country.”

October - 5, 2025
The Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) announced the observance of ‘Resistance Week’ from October 8 to 14, followed by a bandh (general shutdown strike) on October 15 across several eastern states, reports ETV Bharat on October 5. As a result, the Police headquarters has issued a statewide alert, strengthening security, especially in vulnerable areas and Naxal hotbeds, the Police said. The Jharkhand Police Special Intelligence Branch (SIB) has sent a directive to all district Senior Superintendents of Police (SSPs) and Superintendents of Police (SPs), asking them to increase vigilance and put all personnel on special alert. “Security personnel have been advised to move only for operational purposes in Maoist-affected areas,” the letter stated. “All routes to and from camps will undergo Improvised Explosive Device (IED) checks. National highways and key roads are being assessed for Maoist influence, and vehicle movement will be permitted only after clearance.” The letter also directed the concerned officials to increase vigilance around rural markets and fairs, where ambushes may occur.

October - 5, 2025
The United Kingdom’s (UK) Carrier Strike Group (CSG), led by aircraft carrier HMS Prince of Wales, began Exercise Konkan-25 with the Indian Navy on October 5, in the Western Indian Ocean, reports The Hindu. The four-day drill, involving India’s INS Vikrant, marks the first-ever carrier group participation from both nations. The exercise includes anti-submarine warfare, cross-deck flying, and air defence operations, enhancing interoperability between the two navies. Part of the UK’s eight-month global deployment, Operation Highmast, the CSG will also make port calls in Mumbai and Goa, underscoring growing bilateral defence ties. British High Commissioner Lindy Cameron highlighted the exercise as a step toward the U.K.-India Vision 2035. The deployment will conclude with joint aerial defence drills with the Indian Air Force.

October - 7, 2025
Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) ‘politburo’ and ‘central committee (CC)’ member and ‘spokesperson’ Mallojula Venugopal alias Sonu, has issued an unsigned appeal acknowledging the leadership's failure to sustain the armed struggle and urging cadres to consider abandoning it, reports The Times of India on October 7. In the latest letter, he states that he and the leadership "failed to continue the armed struggle" and declares himself unfit to serve as a leader. Venugopal asks cadres to read his appeal in full, discuss it with fellow Maoists, and share their views — either in person, where possible, or in writing via intermediaries or online, if direct meetings are not feasible. He says he is placing specific internal ‘CC’ discussions before cadres so they can assess the merits. The appeal attributes current setbacks to long-standing mistakes. It states that the party failed to establish an "impervious underground revolutionary party" among the people, instead over-relying on armed formations. It cites reversals across regions, including Dandakaranya, Bihar, and Jharkhand, despite past gains, and notes that the base has eroded in several states. The letter by Venugopal reviews internal debates since the 2007 Congress, arguing that the leadership underestimated the state, persisted with unsuitable tactics, and failed to correct course in time. It highlights the absence of robust clandestine structures distinct from armed units, the public visibility of formations, and operational practices that left cadres vulnerable to attack. As a corrective measure, Venugopal urges cadres to seriously debate a temporary cessation of armed struggle, go among the people, patiently rebuild the underground parties and mass organisations, and study changing legal and political conditions in depth. He argues that bloodshed must stop, unnecessary sacrifices must end, and the movement requires a comprehensive review before determining any future course. The letter further states that, even at "the most difficult time," a pause is necessary to regain public confidence. According to the Telangana Special Intelligence Branch (SIB), the letter is authentic, though unsigned.

October - 7, 2025
On October 7, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) charge sheeted eight more individuals in a 2020 transnational narco-terror network case involving drug smuggling from Pakistan into India via the sea route off Gujarat, reports Daily Excelsior. In its eighth supplementary charge sheet filed before the Special NIA Court in Ahmedabad, the agency established a narco-terror conspiracy allegedly masterminded by Italy-based Simranjit Singh Sandhu, Australia-based Tanveer Bedi, and India-based Ankush Kapoor. The charges were filed under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA) based on extensive digital, technical, and documentary evidence. The other accused named include Pakistani national Tariq alias Bhaijaan; Gagandeep Singh Arora; Tamanna Gupta; Sukhbir Singh alias Happy; and Anwar Masih. The case involves the smuggling of 500 kilograms of heroin from Pakistan into Gujarat, with proceeds used to fund the banned terrorist organisation Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT). NIA investigations revealed the conspiracy spanned multiple Indian States and several countries, including Italy, Australia, the UAE, Pakistan, Iran and Thailand. According to the NIA, Ankush Kapoor managed on-ground operations in Punjab, while Simranjit Singh organized the transportation and processing of drugs. Tariq coordinated smuggling via sea routes, and Tanveer Bedi facilitated international hawala transfers to fund LeT activities. Gagandeep Singh Arora, currently absconding, is accused of money laundering. The Gujarat ATS filed the original chargesheet, and the NIA has now filed eight supplementary chargesheets. So far, 26 accused have been arrested, while eight remain at large as the investigation continues.

October - 8, 2025
The Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) ‘Maad divisional committee’ has extended support, in a signed letter, to ‘politburo’ member Bhupati alias Sonu alias Mallojula Venugopal's call to renounce armed struggle, marking another endorsement of the proposal in recent weeks, reports The Times of India on October 8. With this, at least three major Maoist divisions, including ‘North Bastar and Gadchiroli’, backed the appeal, while the ‘Jharkhand committee’ is also believed to be supportive. The ‘Maad division’, considered vital to the organisation's remaining strength, also announced that it was laying down arms, revealed the Telangana Special Intelligence Branch (SIB). The statement, signed by ‘commander’ Ranita Sanita, described giving up arms as "the right decision under the current circumstances". In its letter dated October 4, 2025, the ‘Maad divisional committee’ said it supported the decision "to renounce armed struggle, led by our ‘politburo’ member, Sonu." The committee acknowledged that the ‘central committee (CC)’ failed to "recognise the changing circumstances in the country and the world" and could not adapt the movement to those realities. "As a result, the movement steadily weakened," the letter said, adding that public participation decreased. "We had many opportunities to strengthen and advance the movement, but we failed to seize them." The committee stated it now intends to "work among the people in collaboration with all friendly organisations" and appealed to the public to understand and support the decision. The ‘Maad Committee’ urged both central and state governments to temporarily suspend Police patrols to allow its members to explain the decision to local party and people's committees. "We are responsibly stating that there will be no illegal activities in the Maad area," the letter said. "To achieve this, please suspend police patrols for a while. We will complete this task before the 15th of this month." Signed by Ranita, also ‘secretary’ of the ‘Maad divisional committee’, the statement signifies a growing internal consensus within the CPI-Maoist for ending decades of insurgency and exploring peaceful engagement.

October - 10, 2025
On October 10, Zee News reported Islamic State (IS) is leveraging the networks of the Indian Mujahideen (IM) to strengthen its presence in India. After the decline of the IM, some of its members reportedly joined IS in Syria, including key operative Shafi Armar, who oversaw IS operations related to India from abroad. More details emerged during a raid conducted by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and Pune Police in the Pune Islamic State case. Investigations revealed that IS operatives were using a former Indian Mujahideen facility to continue their activities. The raids at Ashoka Mews Society in Kondhwa in Pune, Maharashtra, brought this to light. This location had previously served as a hub for the Indian Mujahideen and was the site of a control room bust in 2008. An official from the Intelligence Bureau (IB) noted that the Indian Mujahideen remained highly active between 2008 and 2012, highlighting the enduring potential for these networks to be exploited by IS.

October - 15, 2025
On October 15, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (UMHA) said the number of Left-Wing Extremism-affected (LWE) districts has now come down to 11 from 18 earlier this year, reports The Hindu. The number of “most-affected” districts has reduced from six to three, with Bijapur, Sukma, and Narayanpur Districts of Chhattisgarh now falling under the category, the UMHA said. In 2013, there were 126 LWE-affected districts and following continuous operations, the number was restricted to 18 in April 2025. Since 2021, more than 100 forward-operating bases or camps of security forces have been established in affected areas, a majority of them in Chhattisgarh, said a senior government official. Besides Bijapur, Sukma, and Narayanpur, the other affected districts are Dantewada, Gariabandh, Kanker, and Mohla-Manpur-Ambagarh Chowki in Chhattisgarh, West Singhbhum in Jharkhand, Balaghat in Madhya Pradesh, Gadchiroli in Maharashtra, and Kandhamal in Odisha.

Investigations suggest that the camp was operated by members of the Sunabeda-Dharambandha Area Committee, a Maoist faction active in the region.

October - 17, 2025
As many as 210 Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) cadres, including 110 women cadres, have laid down arms at Reserve Police Line in Jagdalpur in Bastar District of Chhattisgarh on October 17, reports The New Indian Express. The surrendered cadres led by senior Maoist leader ‘central committee (CC)’ member Takkallapalli Vasudeva Rao alias Rupesh alias Satish alias Aashanna also deposited 153 weapons, including AK-47 rifles, INSAS (Indian Small Arms System) assault rifles, Self-Loading Rifle (SLR), Barrel Grenade Launcher (BGL), besides other arms. The other high-ranking cadres include Dandakaranya Special Zonal Committee (DKSZC) members Bhaskar alias Rajman Mandavi, Ranita, Raju Salam and Dhannu Vetti alias Santu; and ‘regional committee member (RCM)’ Ratan Elam. All cadres were given a copy of the Indian Constitution and a rose on the stage under a formal ceremony, ‘Puna Margem’, indicating the Maoist cadres rejoining the mainstream. The list of weapons deposited include: 1) AK-47 rifle: 19, 2) SLR rifle: 17, 3) INSAS rifle: 23, 4) INSAS LMG: 01, 5) .303 Rifle: 36, 6) Carbine: 04, 7) BGL launcher: 11, 8) 12 Bore/ Single shot: 41 and 9) Pistol: 01. "We realised we could no longer continue the armed struggle. We took time to arrive at this decision, as we lost many of our men and it became a necessity to give up arms. However, our aim remains the same — to work for the rights of the people that we once fought for, but through peaceful means," Aashanna said. He said he placed other demands before the government, including preventing forced displacement of tribals from their land for development projects, amendments to the Panchayats Extension to Scheduled Areas (PESA) Act, 1996, and the extension of Sixth Schedule protections to Abujhmarh. In his recorded statement, Rupesh acknowledged internal differences within the Maoist ranks saying survival was now the foremost priority. "Those who are still in the forests must reflect on the reality," he said, adding, "At this stage, our first responsibility is to stay alive. Only then can we think about the future."

October - 17, 2025
On October 17, a Special Court of the National Investigation Agency (NIA) at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, sentenced two accused, identified as Mohammad Haroon Haji Abdul Rehman Lakdawala, and Imran Yakub Gitel in the Visakhapatnam Navy Espionage Case, reports NIA. Mohammad Haroon Haji Abdul Rehman Lakdawala of Mumbai (Maharashtra) was sentenced to 5½ years of simple imprisonment under Sections 17 and 18 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). Imran Yakub Gitel of Godhra in Gujarat was sentenced to six years of simple imprisonment for the same offences. Both were fined INR 5,000 each and face an additional one-year imprisonment in case of default. The two were found guilty of acting as agents of foreign intelligence agencies and engaging in espionage activities targeting sensitive naval installations in India. They maintained regular contact with Pakistani agents through messaging platforms and laundered funds through illegal businesses and financial channels to support espionage operations. Lakdawala was arrested in May 2020, and Gitel in September 2020. The NIA took over the case from the Counter-Intelligence Police, Intelligence Department, Andhra Pradesh Police, Vijayawada, in December 2019. A total of 15 persons had been arrested, including 11 Navy personnel. Fourteen accused were chargesheeted in June 2020, followed by a supplementary chargesheet against one more accused in March 2021. Further investigation and trial in the case are ongoing.

October - 17, 2025
On October17, the Special Judge National Investigation Agency (NIA) Court, Jammu, Sandeep Gandotra has rejected the bail plea of Gurpartap Singh, alleged kingpin of a cross-border narco-terror module, accused of attempting to smuggle large consignments of heroin and arms from Pakistan to fund the banned terror outfit Babbar Khalsa International (BKI), reports Daily Excelsior. Singh, arrested in October 2020, has been in custody for nearly four years and sought bail citing prolonged incarceration, delay in trial, and lack of direct evidence. His counsel argued that several prosecution witnesses had not supported the case, making conviction unlikely, and that Singh was being falsely implicated. The NIA, however, strongly opposed the plea, pointing to the bar under Section 43-D (5) of the UAPA and Section 37 of the NDPS Act, which restrict bail in cases involving terror funding and commercial quantities of narcotics. The prosecution maintained that Singh was a key conspirator, coordinating with Pakistan-based handlers and financing heroin consignments for BKI’s revival.

October - 18, 2025
On October 18, the sixth vessel in the series of eight Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Crafts (ASW SWCs), BY 528 (Magdala), was launched at Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL), Kochi, in Ernakulam District of Kerala, reports Press Information Bureau. October - 20, 2025
The Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) has dubbed the recently surrendered Maoists Mallojula Venugopal Rao and Takkalapalli Vasudeva Rao as ‘traitors’ and asked the public to punish them, reports Telangana Today on October 20. In a four-page statement issued on October 19 and signed by the ‘Central Committee (CC)’ ‘Spokesperson’ Abhay, the CPI-Maoist sought to explain how Venugopal Rao alias Sonu turned into a ‘renegade’ over the past several years. He suspected that Sonu was in touch with Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and the Police after the surrender of his wife, Vimala Sidam alias Tarakka, to the Police last year. While stating that the surrender of Sonu and Sathish was a betrayal, divisive and a counter-revolutionary act, Abhay maintained that if anyone who feared for their lives could surrender, but they should not surrender the weapons belonging to the party to the government. The Maoist party faced a difficult situation in 2011 and suffered a setback by 2018. Operation Kagar started in January 2024, and the death of the party ‘general secretary’, Basavaraju, posed a challenge to the cadres, who faced a life and death situation every day. Sonu’s selfishness and desire for a comfortable life led to fear for his life, and it resulted in his surrender. Abhay recalled that Sonu had presented a document in the ‘CC’ meeting held in December 2020 with conclusions on the shortcomings in the Dandakaranya revolutionary movement while finding fault with the party’s political and revolutionary stand. However, the ‘CC’ rejected it. The party told Sonu to correct his wrong political views, individualism, egoism and extreme authoritarianism, but he failed to do so. Sonu breached the party’s discipline; he did not discuss his decision to surrender and divided the party in consultation with party members, Abhay said. Abhay also appealed to the cadres who surrendered to the police along with Sonu and Sathish to reconsider their decision; come back to the party fold, and there would be no harm to them from the party. The surrender of Sathish along with ‘Dandakaranya Special Zonal Committee (DKSZC)’ members Santhu, Bhaskar and Ranitha indicated that Sathish was in touch with Chhattisgarh police and turned into a covert. Sonu, Sathish and those who surrendered to the police along with him were being expelled from the party.

The Central Government has decided to provide Y category security to Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) leaders Mallojula Venugopal alias Sonu and Takkalapalli Vasudeva Rao alias Ashanna, who recently surrendered after handing over their weapons to the government, reports vidhaatha.com on October 21. According to information from central intelligence, a section of the Maoist party strongly opposed Mallojula Venugopal and Ashanna, who had decided to end the armed struggle in the current circumstances. In the wake of the subsequent developments, the Maoist Party, in the name of Abhay, described the two as traitors to the revolution and announced that the people would punish them. There is an opinion among the people that if the Maoist Party leaders announced that the people would punish them, it would be like indirectly declaring that they would kill them. Intelligence sources say that the Centre has decided to provide Y category security to provide full security to the Mallojula and Ashanna who have surrendered their weapons to the government and come out of hiding.

October - 22, 2025
Days after they laid down arms to return to the mainstream, Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) leaders Mallojula Venugopal Rao aka Abhay aka Bhupati aka Master aka Sonu (69) and Takkalapalli Vasudeva Rao aka Satish aka Rupesh aka Aashanna (59) were expelled from the Central Committee of CPI-Maoist, reports ETV Bharat on October 22. Bhupathi had surrendered before the Police along with 60 of his colleagues. Later, Satish surrendered along with 209 Maoists in Chhattisgarh. The letter issued by the Central Committee of CPI-Maoist states that Satish has also been expelled from the organization. Not only this, around 271 Maoists who surrendered along with Bhupati and Satish have also been expelled from the organization. The letter alleges that Bhupati and Satish joined hands with the enemy (Police.) "We had been suspecting since 2011 that Bhupati had links with the Police", the letter states. The Central Committee announced through the letter that the outfits' armed struggle against the police and security forces will continue. "Naxalite leaders like Bhupathi and Satish who surrendered were opportunists and selfish. They betrayed the decades-long struggle of the Naxalites. Both of them surrendered to the police along with their supporters and also handed over vital weapons of the Naxalites to the police. Both of them will be given appropriate punishment at the right time," the letter warned. It said Bhupathi and Satish will not be forgiven under any circumstances. ""However, if other Naxalites who went to surrender with them want to return to the Naxalite organization in the future, we will take them back," the letter said.

October - 23, 2025
On October 23, declaring that Naxalism in Maharashtra was "almost eliminated," Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said that a new Jan Suraksha Vidhayak (Public Security Bill) would soon be sent to the President for assent, reports The Times of India. "The law will help prevent resurgence of Urban Naxal activity and safeguard progress we've achieved," he said. He credited continuous security operations and developmental outreach in Gadchiroli for restoring stability and said the state's next challenge was to tackle "urban Naxalism". Fadnavis also issued a stern warning against ‘urban Naxals', describing them as a major security challenge for the state and the nation. "Unlike jungle warfare, where we know the enemy, urban Maoists [Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist)] are faceless. We don't know who is launching the attack, but we must stand firm," the chief minister said. He underlined that these elements target impressionable youth at their formative stage, sowing seeds of anti-government, anti-system, and anti-Constitution sentiments. "They (urban Maoists) are trying to target our institutions and constitutional framework. They divert, provoke, and tell youngsters that the system is against them. This is their core strategy to spread discord," he said. The chief minister asserted that any anti-Constitution activity would be met with a befitting reply through constitutional means. He highlighted the Jan Surakshya Kaida (Public Security Act) as a robust legal tool. "The Act is now being fine-tuned after consultations across government departments and agencies. The laws, like the Jan Suraksha Kaida, have several overlapping provisions in other contemporary laws which would need to be deliberated upon," Fadnavis said. On the Maoist insurgency front, he revealed that Maharashtra's surrender policy — now in its second part — has nearly eradicated the problem. "Fewer than 10 Maoists remain active in the state. The issue is on the verge of complete resolution. Chhattisgarh is also close to wiping out the menace," he noted, expressing hope that the Red insurgency would be eliminated before the policy's third phase.

October - 24, 2025
On October 24, Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL) achieved a twin launch milestone with the commissioning of two state-of-the-art Fast Patrol Vessels (FPVs) — ICGS Ajit and ICGS Aparajit — for the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) at its Vasco da Gama yard, reports The Goan. The vessels were launched by Manju Sharma in the presence of Chief Guest Dr. Mayank Sharma, Financial Advisor (Defence Services). These are the seventh and eighth FPVs in a series of eight indigenously built vessels under the Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan. The FPVs will undertake coastal surveillance, anti-smuggling, anti-piracy, and rescue operations.

October - 27, 2025
On October 27, Counter Intelligence Kashmir (CIK) dismantled a digital radicalization network operating through multiple social media platforms, reports Daily Excelsior. A statement issued by the Police said that acting on precise intelligence inputs and sustained cyber surveillance, CIK identified two radical social media handles ‘faithful_warrior57’ and ‘Gurkboru.08’ engaged in glorifying terrorism and circulating extremist narratives. “These accounts were actively sharing propaganda material, including audio clips and digital content of known terrorists, designed to sow discord, promote secessionist sentiment, and attract vulnerable youth towards violent extremism,” the statement said. “Both individuals were traced, apprehended for questioning and found to be juveniles. Digital forensic examination of ‘one of the mobile devices established him as the user of ‘Gurkboru.08’, and evidence revealed he was disseminating terror content under the direct guidance of an online handler. Investigations further disclosed that he had been using encrypted communication tools and VPNs to sustain covert interaction with cross-border handlers.” The statement further said that the inquiry traced the online handler operating under the Ahmad Salar alias Saqib, a Pakistan-based propagandist linked to The Resistance Front (TRF). “Salar was orchestrating a sophisticated online indoctrination effort, exploiting social media to manipulate vulnerable youth through ideological grooming, false promises and glorification of militant activities.” The second juvenile, operating the handle ‘faithful_warrior57’, was similarly influenced by the same handler. Digital traces revealed instructions, emotional manipulation, and ideological conditioning intended to draw both minors deeper into extremist networks. The statement said that through meticulous coordination, superior cyber analytics, and swift operational execution, CIK successfully disrupted the network, effectively preventing the recruitment of two juveniles and thwarting an emerging radicalization threat that could have endangered community safety.

In a letter dated November 22, Ananth addressed to Chief Ministers of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh-Devendra Fadnavis, Vishnu Deo Sai and Mohan Yadav- as well as Chhattisgarh Home Minister Vijay Sharma and asked the respective governments to give them a breathing space time till February 15, 2026 to reach a consensus. Referring Vijay Sharma’s suggestion that the government was ready to listen and would try to fulfill if Maoists put forward any proposals and demands, Ananth said they would do so just before joining the mainstream or after rehabilitation. Ananth noted that while the Maoists are agreeing to disarm, it should not be interpreted as surrendering out of fear or pressure. He stressed that: The decision is collective, not individual, armed struggle is being temporarily suspended, current circumstances are not favourable for continuing militant activity, and weapons should be seen as a means, not an end. October - 28, 2025
In a bid to wean away the misguided youths who have joined the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) and its frontal organisations and bring them back to the mainstream and rehabilitate them, the Odisha government has announced an increase in the surrender package for Maoists, reports Ommcom News on November 28. The package includes financial incentives based on the type of weapon surrendered and the rank of the Maoist cadre. The government has fixed the following incentives for Maoists surrendering with weapons: INR 495,000 for a Light Machine Gun (LMG), INR 330,000 for an AK-47 rifle, and INR 165,000 for a Self-Loading Rifle (SLR). Additionally, Maoists with a INR 1 million reward will receive an extra INR 500,000 upon surrender. Besides, the rank-based incentives are as follows: ‘Politburo’ and ‘Central Committee Members (CCMs)’ will receive INR 11 million, ‘State Committee Members and Special Zonal Committee Members (SCMs/SZCMs)’ will get INR 5.5 million, ‘Regional Committee Members (RCMs)’ will get INR 3.3 million, ‘Divisional Committee Members (DVCMs)’ will receive INR 2.75 million, and lower-ranked ‘DVCMs’ will get INR 2.2 million. The government will also withdraw minor cases registered against surrendered Maoists. The Odisha government, in line with the central government’s efforts, aims to rehabilitate Maoists and reintegrate them into society through this initiative.

"My health is deteriorating. The chief minister called us brothers and urged us to rejoin society. But I will continue the same struggle. The DGP said Chandranna and Bandi Prakash had not surrendered with arms. "The duo stated that their weapons were handed over to the party before leaving," he added. Chandranna rose to the level of ‘CC’ member, serving as a strategist, organisational head, and later as a guide for the Telangana State Committee. October - 29, 2025
On October 29, National Investigation Agency (NIA) charge-sheeted 11 accused arrested in Suhas Shetty murder case, reports The New Indian Express. The chargesheet was filed before the NIA Special Court, Bengaluru in Karnataka. Shetty, a member of Bajrang Dal, was hacked to death by seven persons on May 1, 2025. The targeted killing was carried out in full public view “to instill fear and spread terror in society”, NIA stated in an official released on October 30. “The terror plot was hatched by accused Abdul Safwan alias Kalavaru Safwan alias Chopu Safwan, who is an ex-member of the banned Popular Front of India (PFI), along with Niyaz alias Niya, Mohammed Musamir alias Mahamed Musameer alias Mohammad alias Muzammil, Noushad alias Vamanjoor Noushad alias Chotte Noushad alias Chotu. The latter is a former member of the Karnataka Forum for Dignity (KFD) and PFI. Accused Adil Maharoof alias Adil had provided funds which were used to recruit other accused on the promise of payment or by exploiting any previous existing enmity with the victim,” NIA stated. NIA has “found a larger conspiracy behind the targeted killing”. Investigation revealed that Shetty’s activities were meticulously tracked over several months, and on the fateful day, seven accused trailed his Toyota Innova in two cars. The five men, along with Kalandar Shafi alias Mande Shafi, M Nagaraja alias Naga alias Appu, Ranjith, Mahammed Rizwan alias Rijju, Azaruddin alias Azar alias Ajju, and Abdul Khader alias Noufal are named in the chargesheet.

October - 31, 2025
Central forces have been redeployed in Rourkela in Sundargarh District to thwart attempts by the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) to revive their organisation in the region, which was removed from the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (UMHA)’s list of districts affected by Left-Wing Extremism (LWE) in 2024, reports The Times of India on October 31. Three CRPF camps, also known as Forward Operation Bases (FOBs), have been established at Topadihi, Langalketa, and Giti Jharan under the Rourkela Police District in the Sundargarh Revenue District in the last few days. These locations are strategically positioned along the border with the Naxal-affected West Singhbhum District of Jharkhand. Police sources said central forces were initially withdrawn from Sundargarh in December 2023 due to a significant reduction in Maoist activities and violence over several years. This led to the UMHA declaring the district as Maoist-free in March 2024. However, two recent incidents, including the death of a railway employee in a Maoist-triggered landmine blast on August 3 and the theft of 5,000 kilograms of gelatine sticks from a local stone quarry on May 27, prompted a reassessment of the security situation, especially ahead of the Centre’s March 31, 2026 deadline to eliminate Naxalism from the country. “The FOBs have been strategically placed to prevent Maoist infiltration from West Singhbhum’s Saranda Forests. The presence of these security camps is expected to reassure local residents,” said Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIGP), Western Range, Brijesh Kumar Rai. Police sources report that Naxals from West Singhbhum have been active in Rourkela’s K Balang and Lathikata Police Station areas, seeking logistics such as essential commodities, medicines, and food from local markets. They have attempted to expand their influence by spreading fear through posters and soliciting local support. Additionally, they have tried to extort money from contractors at nearby railway sidings in Rourkela. “With the establishment of security camps in West Singhbhum, Naxals may be attempting to find refuge in Rourkela, using the Saranda Forest as a transit route. We have recalibrated our strategy and strengthened our security measures. Their activities will not disrupt our ongoing fight against LWE,” another Police officer said.

October - 31, 2025
On October 31, National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval said that Jammu and Kashmir (J&K) has long been a “theatre of proxy war” and “covert warfare” for Pakistan, while terrorism in the rest of India has been effectively controlled, The Times of India reported. Speaking at the Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture on Governance, Doval stated, “The facts are facts, and they cannot be disputed. Terrorism in this country has been effectively countered. We had a major incident of terrorism on July 1, 2005, and the last one in 2013 in the hinterland. Except for Jammu and Kashmir, which has been a theatre of proxy war or covert warfare for Pakistan, the whole country has remained secure from terrorist attacks. Efforts were made. People were arrested. Explosives were recovered.” Doval further said that no terror attacks have occurred in the Indian hinterland since 2013, despite continuous attempts by “enemies” to destabilise the nation. He also noted that left-wing extremism has sharply declined since 2014, affecting “less than 11 per cent of the areas” compared to earlier years.

November - 2, 2025
Jharkhand Police have launched an investigation into suspected terror funding networks linking some of the state’s criminals with arms smugglers in Pakistan, The Statesman reports on November 2. Gang leaders including Prince Khan and Sujit Sinha were suspectedly procuring weapons from Pakistan through intermediaries in Punjab and routing payments via hawala (illegal money transaction) and international money transfer channels. Anti-Terror Squad (ATS) and Ranchi Police are jointly investigating the role of more than a dozen individuals under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967. Those named include Sujit Sinha’s wife Riya Sinha and associates Babloo Khan alias Inamul Haq, Ravi Anand, Mohammad Shahid and Mohammad Seraj. Investigators have found that the Sinha and Khan gangs used Pakistan-based arms suppliers to procure sophisticated weapons, which were transported to Jharkhand via Punjab. Of the 21 weapons ordered, only ten have been recovered. Police believe the remaining eleven are still in circulation within the state’s criminal networks. Officials said the gangs made payments through hawala routes, often routed via Dubai and Malaysia, with money transfers conducted through Western Union. Funds were first moved to Europe and then redirected to Asia, where Pakistani handlers received them through restaurant-based conduits in Malaysia.

November - 2, 2025
The latest review of categorisation of Naxal violence-affected Districts in the country saw their number come down to 38 in nine states from 46 in April, with only four ‘districts of concern’ and three ‘most affected districts’ remaining, reports Telangana Today on November 2. The latest categorisation was notified by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (UMHA) on October 15. Official records and sources in the security establishment said that a “marked improvement” was recorded in the insurgency theatre. Hence, the number of districts covered under the Security-Related Expenditure (SRE) has decreased to 38 from 46 as of April 1. The number of Left-Wing Extremism (LWE)-affected districts has dropped to 11 from 18 in April, and they are sub-categorised as ‘most affected districts’, ‘districts of concern’, and ‘other LWE-affected districts.’ According to the latest categorisation, only three ‘most affected districts’ remain, down from six on April 1. These three districts are Bijapur, Narayanpur, and Sukma — all in Chhattisgarh. This sub-category under the LWE-affected districts was created in 2015 with 35 districts to ensure “focused” deployment of resources. The four ‘districts of concern’ are Kanker in Chhattisgarh, West Singhbhum in Jharkhand, Balaghat in Madhya Pradesh, and Gadchiroli in Maharashtra. Districts put under this head are those where Naxal influence is waning, but focused development of resources is still required. In April, four out of the six districts were removed from this category, and two were added after the review. There are four ‘other LWE-affected districts’ — Dantewada, Gariyaband, and Mohla-Manpur-Ambagarh Chowki in Chhattisgarh and Kandhamal in Odisha. The districts that require “consolidation” of the security situation, as well as development, and are neither included in the ‘most affected districts’ nor ‘districts of concern’ categories are put under ‘other LWE-affected districts.’ There were six districts in this category in April. The latest review puts 27 districts under ‘Legacy and Thrust Districts’. These include eight from Odisha, six from Chhattisgarh, four from Bihar, three from Jharkhand, two from Telangana, and one each from Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and West Bengal. These are the districts that have seen the end of Naxalism but are “prospective sites” for LWE expansion, and therefore, continued government support is required for capacity-building of the states, according to the records. In April, there were 28 districts under this category. After the latest review, eight districts were excluded and seven were included, the sources said.

While Dawood’s brother, Anees Ibrahim, continues to oversee international operations, Salim has been tasked with reviving domestic trade networks…We believe the D-Syndicate views the northeastern region as a key transit point because of its proximity to porous international borders with Myanmar and Bangladesh”, added the official

November - 5, 2025
The Financial Action Task Force (FATF), in its report “Asset Recovery Guidance and Best Practices”, highlighted India’s proactive use of both conviction-based and non-conviction-based confiscation provisions and credits the Enforcement Directorate (ED) for its coordination with foreign counterparts in cases pursued under mutual legal assistance treaties, India Today reports on November 5. FATF noted that ED’s asset recovery strategy reflected “a mature, well-resourced, and technology-driven approach” to financial investigations, aligning with the revised FATF standards that call for making asset recovery a national policy priority. It also commended India’s legislative framework under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), which enables swift freezing, attachment, and confiscation of criminal proceeds even before conviction. The report further referred to India’s effective inter-agency coordination between the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU-IND), Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), and ED, calling it a model for jurisdictions seeking to integrate intelligence, enforcement, and prosecution in financial crime cases.

November - 15, 2025
On November 15, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) said that the cause of the blast at Nowgam Police Station in Srinagar District of Jammu and Kashmir (J&K) was under investigation and urged people to avoid unnecessary speculation, reports Greater Kashmir. Briefing the media, MHA Joint Secretary Prashant Lokhande confirmed that nine people were killed and 32 were injured in the “massive” and unfortunate accidental explosion late Friday night. He said a large cache of explosive materials and chemicals, recovered during a recent probe into a terror module, had been stored in an open, secure area within the police station premises. As part of standard procedure, the materials were being examined by forensic and chemical experts. “Due to the voluminous nature of the recovery, the examination had been underway for the last two days,” Lokhande said. The substances were “unstable and sensitive,” and were being handled with utmost caution. However, at around 11:20 pm on November 14, an accidental explosion occurred during the examination process. The blast damaged the police station and affected nearby buildings. Among the injured are 27 police personnel, two revenue officials, and three civilians.

The approval underscores Canada’s long-standing approach to freedom of expression and political rights.

November - 17, 2025
A report revealed that India's traditional hawala networks have rapidly adapted to cryptocurrencies, enabling illicit funds to move across borders with greater anonymity and speed, reports The Indian Express on November 17. It highlighted how crime proceeds, black money and cyber fraud gains are increasingly routed through virtual assets, complicating enforcement efforts. In one case cited by the report, a trader from Ghaziabad funnelled Rs 1.3 crore (13 million) of crime-linked money in 2024 into a Dubai-based crypto wallet. In another case, a Delhi businessman has been charged with moving over Rs 4,000 crore (40,000 million) overseas using fabricated invoices and shell companies. Agencies reported that more than Rs 1,000 crore (10,000 million) generated from cyber fraud has already left India this year (2025) through crypto channels. These transactions mirror hawala's informal structure but use blockchain pathways that make tracing more complex. Traditional hawala typically connects two regions with a limited chain of intermediaries. With crypto, however, transfers can pass through many more layers across several jurisdictions.

November - 17, 2025
Amid resurfacing terror threats, Indian Coast Guard (ICG) recently executed a high-intensity mock drill off the Paradip coast to enhance preparedness for maritime infiltrations, reports news9live.com on November 17. This crucial exercise simulated counter-terror operations at sea, drawing significant lessons from the 26/11 Mumbai attack, which exposed vulnerabilities in India’s coastal defence when terrorists infiltrated via a sea route. The drill, conducted 10 nautical miles inside the Bay of Bengal from Paradip, focused on intercepting and neutralising potential infiltrators approaching India’s eastern coast. Scenarios involved surrounding a terrorist boat and forcing surrender or neutralisation, demonstrating the Coast Guard’s operational readiness. This proactive measure addressed concerns about potential infiltration from coastal routes, particularly from Bangladesh, and reinforced India's commitment to safeguarding its critical waterways and coastal areas.

On November 20, Security Force (SF) personnel and the Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad (BDDS) detected and safely destroyed a powerful 10-kilogram Improvised Explosive Device (IED) planted by the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) on the Chihka-Uspari Road in the Uspari village under Bhairamgarh Police Station limits in the Bijapur District in the Bastar division of Chhattisgarh, reports SocialNews.XYZ. November - 24, 2025
On November 24, Canadian courts and the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB) continue to dismiss refugee claims filed by Punjabi nationals citing persecution for alleged Khalistan activism, reports The Indian Express. In 2025, dozens of petitions were rejected as judges flagged “templated,” “opportunistic,” or “fraudulent” narratives, often supported only by Sikh for Justice (SFJ) voter cards or last-minute social-media posts. In a notable July 2025 case, the Refugee Appeal Division overturned protection granted to Gagandeep Singh of Haryana, calling his claim “yet another fraudulent refugee claim,” noting that nearly 200 similar applications were prepared by the same consultant. In August 2025, the Federal Court upheld the rejection of Amandeep Singh and Kanwaldeep Kaur, ruling their sudden political conversion to Khalistan support as lacking credibility. IRB data show Indian nationals—mainly from Punjab—filed 9,947 claims in the first six months of 2025, accounting for 18% of all claims. Rejection and abandonment rates for Indian claimants remain double the global average. At least 30 Federal Court reviews of Khalistan-linked claims were dismissed in 2025. Canadian Immigration Minister Marc Miller stated that audits of immigration consultants and inadmissibility screenings have intensified amid concerns of misuse of the “Khalistan card.” Courts have reiterated that participation in Canadian Khalistan rallies or possession of SFJ referendum cards does not establish pre-flight persecution.

November - 25, 2025
Twenty-eight cadres of the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist), with a cumulative bounty of INR 8.9 million on their heads, surrendered to the police in Narayanpur District in the Bastar division of Chhattisgarh on November 25, reports The Hindu. “Under the initiative ‘Poona Margem: From Rehabilitation to Reintegration,’ a significant achievement was made today in Narayanpur District, where 28 Maoist cadres, carrying a total reward of INR 8.9 million, decided to abandon the path of violence and reintegrate into the mainstream,” said Inspector General of Police (IGP), Bastar Range, P. Sundarraj. He added, “The remaining Maoist cadres, including Politburo member Devji, Central Committee Member (CCM) Ramder, Dandakaranya Special Zonal Committee (DKSZC) member Pappa Rao, Deva (Barse Deva), and others, have no option but to give up violence and join the mainstream.” Nineteen of the 28 cadres who surrendered are women. Among those who gave themselves up were a Divisional Committee member (Maad), members of the military wing People's Liberation Guerrilla Army (PLGA) company, Area Committee members, technical team members, military platoon members, and Local Organising Squad members. Three Maoist cadres among the 28 formally handed over their weapons, including a Self-Loading Rifle (SLR), an INSAS (Indian Small Arms System) assault rifle, and a .303 rifle, to the Security Forces.

November - 26, 2025
On November 26, a Special Court of the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in Jaipur in Rajasthan, sentenced a Pakistani national identified as Ran Singh to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment (RI) and imposed a fine of INR 30,000 in a 2019 Fake Indian Currency Notes (FICN) case, reports NIA. Investigators stated that Singh entered India via the Thar Express and was allegedly recruited by Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) to smuggle FICN.

November - 26, 2025
The Union Government informed the Supreme Court (SC) that unregulated online real-money gaming (ORMG) has demonstrable links to terror financing (TF) and money laundering, Hindustan Times reports on November 26. In an affidavit, the Centre said ORMG facilitates tax evasion, mule accounts, crypto-based fund diversion, hawala channels and offshore shell structures. Inputs from multiple Ministries and agencies, including Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs), indicated ORMG platforms were used to route proceeds from drug trafficking, fraud, human trafficking and weapons smuggling. Suspicious gaming-related STRs rose from one in 2019–20 to 239 in 2023–24, involving over 7,000 accounts and outward remittances exceeding INR 5.7 billion. The Centre asserted that ORMG is a public-order and national-security threat and defended Parliament’s authority to ban such games.

December - 1, 2025
On December 1, Inspector General (IG) of the Border Security Force (BSF) Kashmir Frontier, Ashok Yadav, said that terror launch pads remain under BSF radar despite relocation into Pakistan after “Operation Sindoor”, reports Daily Excelsior. Speaking at the BSF’s 61st Raising Day event in Humhama, Srinagar District of Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), Yadav said BSF intelligence is monitoring 69 active launch pads along the LoC, where 100–120 terrorists are waiting to infiltrate. Greater Kashmir noted there was no terrorist infiltration into Kashmir across the Line of Control (LoC) during the current year, with eight infiltrators killed by the Security Forces (SFs), while five others were pushed back — foiling four intrusion attempts by terror operatives While the infiltration modus operandi remains largely unchanged, “some new routes are being explored,” he added. Thirteen BSF companies remain deployed in support of the Jammu and Kashmir Police (JKP). On narco-terrorism, Yadav warned that the threat is “growing and serious,” with narcotics being pushed into Kashmir to “turn youth into addicts and finance terrorism.” The BSF has intensified monitoring in the Tangdhar sector to counter such attempts. He noted that drone activity is being observed across the LoC but remains limited to the Pakistan side and is largely for reconnaissance. “Drones are under constant observation,” he said. Yadav also highlighted ongoing BSF modernisation initiatives, including drone warfare training, enhanced surveillance systems, cyber-readiness measures, drone forensics labs, and the BSF Drone Warfare School in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.

In the last five years, the government has declared 23 organisations, including Students' Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) and Popular Front of India (PFI), as Unlawful Associations, Minister of State for Home Affairs Nityanand Rai told Lok Sabha (Lower House of Indian Parliament) on December 2, ommcomnews.com. The latest addition or the 23rd organisation to be declared unlawful is Awami Action Committee (AAC), he said. Highlighting achievements of NIA, he said that it has now emerged as a globally renowned investigative agency, with a conviction rate of 92.44 per cent in judgments pronounced in 172 cases (out of the total 692 registered cases since its inception). Exclusive Divisions, such as ‘Anti Human Trafficking Division (AHTD)’, ‘Anti Cyber Terrorism Division (ACTD)’, ‘Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Cell’, ‘Financial Analysis Unit (FAU)’ and a Special Cell comprising of legal experts have also been created in the NIA, he added.

December - 4, 2025
Assam Government has issued a notification banning the publication, circulation, possession, and digital transmission of radical and jihadi literature associated with Jama'atul Mujahideen Bangladesh (JMB), Ansarullah Bangla Team (ABT), Ansar-Al-Islam/pro-AQIS, and other similar banned outfits, pratidintime.com reports on December 4. The move follows recommendations from the Assistant Inspector General of Police (Law & Order) and observations from the Judicial Department, citing intelligence reports and investigations by Assam Police and the Special Task Force (STF) that indicate continued circulation of extremist material in both print and digital formats. Assam Government invoked Section 98 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, empowering the state to forfeit material promoting enmity between groups, acts prejudicial to national integration, or content intended to outrage religious feelings. Offences may also attract action under Sections 196 and 197 of BNSS and Section 67 of the Information Technology Act, 2000. The notification cites that such material: Glorifies violent jihad and promotes radicalization; Provides ideological indoctrination and recruitment guidance; and Incites violence and threatens India’s sovereignty and internal security. Under the notification, any form of publication, printing, sale, exhibition, possession, or storage, physical or digital, of these materials is prohibited with immediate effect. The ban also extends to websites, social media pages, encrypted channels, online groups, and digital platforms propagating extremist content.

December - 5, 2025
On December 5, the United Kingdom (UK) imposed sanctions on British Sikh businessman Gurpreet Singh Rehal and the entity Babbar Akali Lehar in its first use of the Domestic Counter-Terrorism Regime to disrupt financing for the proscribed Babbar Khalsa International (BKI), reports The Tribune. Rehal, linked to Panjab Warriors, faces an asset freeze and director disqualification for allegedly promoting, funding, and recruiting for BKI. Babbar Akali Lehar was similarly sanctioned for involvement in BKI’s activities. HM Treasury stated that both were engaged in recruitment, financial facilitation, and procurement of weapons. All UK persons are prohibited from dealing with their funds without a licence. Penalties for violations include imprisonment up to seven years. Following the sanctions, Morecambe FC and Panjab Warriors clarified that Rehal no longer holds any role in their organisations.

December - 5, 2025
Security Forces (SFs) foiled a Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) plot by recovering and destroying three powerful Improvised Explosive Device (IED) cooker bombs planted along a sensitive forest trail, averting a major attack on Police and civilians in the Toyameta–Padbeda Forest area under Chhote Dongar Police Station limits in Narayanpur District of Chhattisgarh on December 5, reports Ommcom News. Acting on credible intelligence, the Indo-Tibetan Border Police’s (ITBP) 29th Battalion from Orchha, the Bomb Disposal Squad (BDS) from Narayanpur, the local Police force, and the ITBP Dog Squad launched a coordinated search along the Padbeda trail near the Madin River. During the search, they recovered three pressure cooker bombs, each weighing around three kilograms, strategically planted on the riverside trail. These devices were designed to cause maximum damage to patrolling Police parties and posed a grave risk to villagers who frequently use the route. The BDS neutralised the explosives on the spot, adhering to technical protocols and safety procedures.

December - 7, 2025
On December 7, the Border Security Force (BSF) Jammu Frontier has asserted that no fresh terrorist infiltration has occurred from the International Border (IB), reports Greater Kashmir. Inspector General (IG) Shashank Anand stated that recent sightings in Jammu are linked to old groups of terrorists who previously infiltrated via the LoC or IB. IG Anand noted that sightings in Rajouri, Poonch, Doda, Kishtwar, Kathua, and Udhampur relate to a few roaming groups, with Rashtriya Rifles (RR), Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), J&K Police Special Operations Groups (SOGs), and other security forces conducting large-scale counter-insurgency operations. Many operations have successfully neutralised terrorists, he added. About reports of infiltration through IB after the recent frequent sightings of terrorists in Samba, Kathua, Udhampur and Chenab valley districts. IG Anand described them as “mere speculations.” He stated, “They keep on shifting their bases and they act as per instructions they get from their handlers. Mostly they are dormant. They strike as and when they receive instructions (from across the border).”

On December 11, a youth, identified as Akash alias Golu Pandit, was shot dead by three car-borne assailants in the parking lot of the Abohar court complex in Fazilka District of Punjab during a court hearing, reports Hindustan Times. On December 11, Arunachal Pradesh Police arrested two persons, identified as Nazir Ahmad Malik and Sabir Ahmed Mir, in Itanagar, Arunachal Pradesh, both of whom are residents of Kupwara District of Jammu & Kashmir (J&K), on charges of espionage and links to Pakistan-based handlers, reports Hindustan Times. December - 11, 2025
On December 11, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) has submitted a chargesheet naming 11 armed cadres of the Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) who were involved in looting around 4,000 kilograms of explosives during its transportation to a stone quarry in Sundargarh District in Odisha, reports The Hindu. According to a statement issued by NIA, all 11 cadres of the banned organisation have been charged under various sections of Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA), the Arms Act and the Explosive Substances Act. During investigation, the NIA had found the accused to have been actively involved in the criminal conspiracy, planning and execution of the loot of around 200 explosive packets, each containing 20 kilograms of explosives, it said. “The explosives were being transported from Itma Explosive Station to the Banko stone quarry on May 27, 2025. The driver, along with the vehicle, was taken into control by 10-15 armed Maoists and was taken to their stronghold,” the NIA further said. The agency, which took over the case from the local police in June, found during investigation that the huge quantity of explosives had been looted for use against the government machinery, including police and security forces, through the commission of terror acts. The loot was part of a conspiracy of CPI (Maoist) to disturb the nation’s security and stability, said the NIA. The CPI (Maoist) cadres who were arrested included Jarja Munda alias Kulu Munda, Anmol alias Sushant alias Lalchand Hembram, Ramesh alias Pritam Manjhi alias Anal Da.

December - 11, 2025
On December 11, the Supreme Court (SC) said it will hear the bail plea of Kashmiri separatist leader Shabir Ahmed Shah on January 7, in a terror‑funding case, Daily Excelsior reported. December - 11, 2025
The Odisha government has established a special court to speed up the trial of Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist) leader Dunna Kesava Rao alias Azad (52), who has been in judicial custody since 2011, a Home department notification said on December 11, reports The Hans India. The notification said, “... in compliance of the order of Supreme Court, the State government, in consultation with High Court of Orissa, do hereby establish court of Additional District and Sessions Judge at Paralakhemundi in addition to the existing number of such courts in the judgeship of Gajapati with effect from the date the said court functions with the local limits of jurisdiction in the entire state of Odisha and fix the place of sitting of the said court at Paralakhemundi for speedy trial of cases pending against D Kesava Rao.” However, the special court will hear cases excluding those registered under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, for the time being, it said. This is perhaps the first instance in the State when a separate court has been created solely to dispose of pending cases of one individual undertrial prisoner. At least 37 criminal cases are currently pending against Azad in Odisha and in his native Andhra Pradesh. He was the prime accused in the killing of Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) leader Swami Laxmanananda Saraswati, which led to large-scale communal violence in Kandhamal in 2008. At least 39 people were killed, and thousands of houses were burnt in the month-long violence.

December - 14, 2025
The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (UMHA) has begun to recast India’s counter terror architecture with a turn toward artificial intelligence driven intelligence systems, big data fusion centres and a wide expansion of forensic and digital surveillance capabilities, senior security officials familiar with the changes have stated, sundayguardianlive.com reports on December 14. Officials said the government is embedding technology at the core of counter terror operations, a shift driven by the rise of encrypted cross border communication, drone based networks, cryptocurrency enabled financing and online radicalisation. As per official documents, the Multi Agency Centre (MAC), the national intelligence coordination platform under the Intelligence Bureau (IB), and its subsidiary units have been upgraded with artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) tools that allow predictive analysis and real time correlation of inputs down to the district level. An official described the changes as the first major technological overhaul of the MAC system in years and a move toward pre-emptive intelligence rather than post-incident response.

December - 17, 2025
December 17, Lieutenant Governor (LG) Manoj Sinha said that terrorists hiding in mountains and forests will be eliminated soon, asserting that local terror recruitment has sharply declined in Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), reports Daily Excelsior. December - 17, 2025
On December 17 (today) the Supreme Court dismissed the bail plea of a woman advocate accused of influencing and recruiting young women into the banned Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-Maoist), underscoring the gravity of the allegations and directing that the trial in the case be concluded within four months, reports Hindustan Times. A bench of justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta took note of the submission made by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) that the trial was progressing expeditiously and was likely to be completed within three months. Recording this assurance, the bench directed that the trial be brought to a logical conclusion within a maximum period of four months. Additional solicitor general SD Sanjay, appearing for the NIA, highlighted the seriousness of the charges against the accused, Chukka Shilpa, a practising advocate of the High Court and an alleged member of Chaitanya Mahila Sangham (CMS), which the agency has described as a frontal organisation of the banned CPI-Maoist. Shilpa was arrested from her residence in Hyderabad in June 2022 and has remained in custody since then. The Supreme Court noted that the case involved grave allegations relating to the radicalisation and recruitment of young women into a proscribed terrorist organisation. In view of the nature of the accusations and the advanced stage of the trial, the bench declined to grant bail, observing that there was no reason to interfere at this stage while the trial was moving swiftly. The case has its origins in a complaint filed by the mother of a young nursing student, Radha, who has been missing since 2017. According to the prosecution, Radha was allegedly influenced and radicalised by members of CMS, including Shilpa, under the guise of social work. The NIA, in a charge sheet filed in December 2022, alleged that CMS functioned as a feeder organisation, identifying and grooming young women before channeling them into the CPI-Maoist.

December - 19, 2025
On December 19, Indian Coast Guard (ICG), commissioned ICG Ship ‘Amulya’, the third vessel in the series of eight new-generation Adamya-class Fast Patrol Vessels, at a ceremony held in Goa, reports indianews.com. The commissioning marks another milestone in India’s push towards strengthening coastal security through indigenous defence platforms. Designed and built by Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL), the 51-metre-long vessel represents a new benchmark in indigenous shipbuilding. With more than 60 per cent indigenous components, the ship reflects India’s growing defence self-reliance under the ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ (Self-Reliant India) and ‘Make-in-India’ initiatives. The fast patrol vessel incorporates a modern design philosophy focused on efficiency, endurance and rapid response. Powered by two advanced diesel engines generating 3,000 KW each, the ship can achieve a top speed of 27 knots and has an operational endurance of 1,500 nautical miles, enabling it to undertake extended missions across India’s maritime zones.

In addition, cash rewards of INR 3.75 million each have been declared for two ‘military platoon commanders’, while rewards of INR 3.2 million have been announced for 10 ‘divisional committee members (DVCMs)’. Police have assured the public that the identity of informers will be kept strictly confidential. Anyone with information has been asked to contact the Police helpline number 9437643839. Alongside the reward posters, the Police have also displayed separate notices appealing to Maoists to surrender and rejoin the mainstream. These posters outline the benefits available under the government’s surrender and rehabilitation policy.

December - 22, 2025
On December 22, Haryana Government has amended the Haryana Private Universities Act, 2006, strengthening its authority to oversee and regulate private higher education institutions, in the wake of a White-Collar terror module of November 10, Red Fort blast, suspectedly linked with Al Falah University and seek to address loopholes in the earlier law that led to inadequate monitoring and weak enforcement, reports moneycontrol.com. The revised Act now clearly defines the grounds and procedures for action against private universities found guilty of mismanagement, furnishing false or misleading information, or failing to comply with academic and regulatory standards. Possible penalties include suspending admissions in specific departments, imposing fines between INR 10 lakh and INR 1 crore, appointing an administrator to run the institution, and, in severe cases, dissolving the university in a phased manner.

December - 24, 2025
According to the State’s annual crime data report, Punjab Director General of Police (DGP) Gaurav Yadav, recorded an 88 per cent conviction rate, among the highest nationally, with 5,901 convictions out of 6,728 decided cases, and accounted for nearly two-thirds of India’s heroin seizures, 25 per cent of national Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) arrests, and 20 per cent of NDPS cases, reports The Tribune on December 24. Preventive measures saw 23,940 persons admitted to de-addiction centres and 59,840 referred to OOAT clinics. Proactive policing neutralised ISI-sponsored terror threats, with police solving 12 terror-related incidents, including hand grenade attacks and a Rocket-Propelled Grenade (RPG) attack on a police station, arresting 50 module members and dismantling seven additional terror modules. From 131 arrests, recoveries included nine rifles, 188 pistols and revolvers, 12 Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs), 11.62 kilograms (Kg) of Research Department Explosive (RDX), 54 hand grenades, 32 detonators, four RPGs, one rocket launcher sleeve, two timer switches, three walkie-talkies, and eight remote-controlled devices. The Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF) dismantled 416 gangster and criminal modules, arresting 992 offenders, and seized 620 weapons and 252 vehicles, while coordination with the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) led to 11 Interpol Red Notices and two Blue Notices, resulting in the deportation or arrest of Anmol Bishnoi, Parminder Singh alias Pindi, Sukhdev Kumar alias Manish Bedi, and Sajan Masih alias Goru. Overall crime declined compared to 2024, with murders down 8.7 per cent, kidnappings and abductions 10.6 per cent, snatchings 19.6 per cent, and thefts 34.3 per cent, even as cases under the NDPS Act, Arms Act, and Excise Act rose due to intensified enforcement. Border security was strengthened with anti-drone systems in Tarn Taran, Ferozepur, and Amritsar Rural, installation of 2,367 CCTV cameras at 585 locations costing INR 49.58 crore, and deployment of 896 personnel from specialised units, while cybercrime enforcement saw INR 79.96 crore frozen—19 per cent of INR 418.29 crore defrauded—ranking Punjab fourth nationally; road safety also improved as the Sadak Surakhiya Force reduced fatalities from 4,829 (2023) to 4,759 (2024) and accidents from 6,269 to 6,063, placing Punjab among nine States/UTs recording declines in both.

On December 26, a high-level tripartite meeting between the Assam Government, the Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council (KAAC) and Karbi civil society groups ended without resolving the core issue behind weeks of tension in West Karbi Anglong, particularly Kheroni, where protests are underway over alleged encroachment of tribal land, reports Northeast Now. Leaders of the Karbi Cultural Society (KCS) and Karbi Lamet Amei (KLA), spearheading a fast-unto-death protest, said their key demand—eviction of alleged encroachers from Professional Grazing Reserve (PGR) and Village Grazing Reserve (VGR) land—was not addressed. Despite these steps, protest leaders warned that agitation could intensify if indigenous land rights remain unresolved.

December - 26, 2025
On December 26, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) provided access to a database containing 400 dossiers on organised crime and terror networks to Police Forces and Security Agencies of States and Union Territories (UTs) across India, reports etvbharat.com. According to NIA officials, the database includes comprehensive profiles of Terrorist Organisations (TOs) and criminal syndicates operating in the country, including Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM), Ansarullah Bangla Team (ABT), Khalistani militant groups, and the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. The dossiers comprise First Information Reports (FIRs), interrogation records, fingerprints, voice samples, family details of terrorists, and other critical intelligence inputs. The initiative was announced on the sidelines of a two-day anti-terror conference in New Delhi, inaugurated by Union Home Minister (UHM) Amit Shah. The conference focused on emerging terrorism trends, major cases such as the Delhi bomb blast and Pahalgam attack, terror financing, digital forensics, and inter-agency coordination, in line with the Government of India’s zero-tolerance policy towards terrorism.

December - 26, 2025
On December 26, the United Liberation Front of Asom–Independent (ULFA-I) announced a major organisational overhaul by disbanding its three councils and constituting a new 24-member Central Committee, with co-founder Paresh Baruah appointed as its ‘president’, Hindustan Times reports. In a statement, ULFA-I said the decision was taken unanimously after reviewing the “present circumstances”. Baruah (68), the group’s self-styled ‘general’, will head the Central Committee, while two senior leaders, identified by aliases Michael Asom and Maitri Asom, were named ‘vice-president’ and ‘general secretary’ (GS), respectively.
